# Changelog

All notable changes are documented in the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car-releases/releases) for this repo.
This file is a chronological index linking to each release's full notes.

## [v0.65.0] — 2026-11-25

### Changes

- The daemon's default peer listener now follows this host's LAN address. After a DHCP renewal or a Wi-Fi or VPN change took the bound address off the host, other CARs could not reach it until the daemon restarted. Now it moves to the new address within about 60 s, and its mDNS record, new invites and the synced endpoint name the new URL. After a move it follows the next pick once more (back to Wi-Fi after a tunnel), which can also be a VM bridge that outranks the LAN; otherwise a listener on an address the host still has never moves. A daemon that boots with no LAN address starts its listener once one appears. An explicit `--a2a-bind` never moves (car#4865).

- An approval an agent draws as an A2UI card can no longer leave Slack and iMessage approvers with only a headline. A card sent without `details` gets the card's own text as `details.card_text`, and a card with no text and no details is refused. An `Image` on an approval card must now be a `data:` image it carries itself: a remote address is refused, so opening the card no longer contacts a server the agent chose before you decide (car#3717).

- When the organization admission check is refused as busy (HTTP 429 or 503), the daemon now logs one warning with the status, the Retry-After it was given, the organization and the API base. Until now those refusals left no trace, so a long "organization admission is rate-limited" spell could not be traced to its cause (car#5279).

- In-chat agent builder: a build whose saved session CAR no longer holds is now reported by a structured error code, so the card recognises it without matching English text; an approval CAR could not take or record is no longer shown as "you didn't approve"; and only your own host can turn on the agent-draft card. On a draft card, a build CAR cannot reach now offers Stop beside Try again; a finished build whose age CAR cannot read no longer keeps the card on "No sign of it yet"; the wait for CAR's check of a draft is not restarted when the card is drawn again; an added agent's card and a failed card's message are the last things dropped when CAR keeps only the newest 500 cards; Run now no longer says "didn't finish" for a run Work still shows as queued or working; and two drafts waiting on an approval from an older daemon are each settled by their own approval. The dashboard window is watched again whenever it is shown again, so unsent card choices are saved when it closes.

- A supervised agent can now declare the models it is served from, in order: `models` on `agents.upsert`, or `[agent] models` in its bundle (`[runtime] bundle_format_version = 4`). The daemon serves the agent's `infer` and `infer_stream` calls only from that list, tries the next model only when the one before it fails, records each switch as a `model_fallback` event in the agent session's event log, and returns an error naming every model tried when the list runs out. Each entry must be a model already registered with CAR, so a spec cannot add an endpoint; a call naming a model outside the list is refused. An agent with no declaration uses the owner's default routing, exactly as before (car#3401).

- Setting or checking an always-allow tool override while that agent is mid-run now answers within 5 seconds (an error saying to try again, or the override reported inactive) instead of hanging the client. A damaged `agent-permissions.json` logs its cause once each time the file changes instead of on every read, and the Agent Permissions reference now gives the one-time `jq` rewrite for the unreleased flat file shape.

- Setting an agent tool override with a standing authorization no longer leaves the override active when saving the authorization fails.
  - **An error means no new access.** `agent_permissions.set_tool` with `standing: true` now publishes the override and records its authorization together; if the authorization cannot be saved, the call fails and the override is not published.

- `car ls --json` (`agents.list`) and every other agent row no longer print an agent's `env` values, which is where a provider key in a manifest showed up.
  - **Names, not values.** Each `env` name is still listed; its value reads `<redacted>`, except CAR's own session bookkeeping (`CAR_LAUNCHER_PID`, `CAR_LAUNCHER_START`, `CAR_SELF_ENROLLED`, `CAR_ENROLLED_AT_MS`). The in-process `agentsList` / `agents_list` rows from the Node and Python packages also drop the agent's token, as the daemon's already did.
  - **Round trips keep the keys.** Sending a listed row back to `agents.upsert` keeps the stored values; a `<redacted>` value with nothing stored behind it is refused rather than saved.

- Removing a person's delegate agent now also forgets the messages the daemon was holding for it to forward.
  - **No stale forwards.** A delegate removed and enrolled again under the same id can no longer forward a message that was delivered to its earlier registration.

- Android: a denied approval card stays Denied. When a failed gate save denied an approval before the phone's own Approve call returned, the card used to change to "Approved once". A deny from the ledger now always wins, and the phone's own answer settles only a card that nothing has settled yet. An approval the daemon closes as `unknown` (the agent disconnected before it confirmed what happened) now closes the card with "Outcome unknown", the Mac card's wording, so it no longer offers Approve and Deny (car#4318).

- `car-engine` builds for Android targets again. A symlink check in its guarded file open compared a 32-bit file mode with Android's 16-bit file-type constants, so `car-ffi-uniffi` failed to compile for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 Android (car#5061).

- `run_applescript` (assistant tool, `automation.run_applescript`, NAPI `runApplescript`, PyO3 `run_applescript`) takes `imessage_send: null | { to, body }`. For a declared send CAR records it in the send log before the script runs and passes `[to, tagged]` as argv, where `tagged` is the body plus a 64-character invisible tag only CAR makes; the echo of that exact text is marked `own_echo` on its first read, across restarts, for 24 hours. `CAR_APPLESCRIPT_IMESSAGE=required` makes the argument mandatory (car#4450).
- The send log's context query no longer keeps owner-sent rows from chats with no open send (the owner's text in another chat stays out of the log), and it finds a send's chat through its participants; an `Authorization:` header value is redacted from feedback even when it reads like an auth word (car#4572).

- An approval card now shows a field the requester sent empty, such as an empty Cc, as a labelled "(empty)" row. The person deciding can tell it from a field that was never sent (car#4625).

- Approval cards no longer hide fields the requester sent. A mail or text approval shows every field it has no line for under **Other details** (a `bcc`, a `replyTo`, a forwarding address). A request missing what its layout needs (a text with no recipient) shows as the plain list of every field. A long request scrolls inside the card instead of being cut after 40 rows behind a "more fields not shown" line (car#3713).

- `host.approvals` without `pending` now lists, for the host client and the signed-in dashboard, every ask the pending view lists (collaboration Decisions and Approvals, direct asks, board handoffs and assignments, Lattice requests) beside the approvals ledger, with the same ids, plus each one settled in the last 24 hours, in the ledger row's shape. Before, it listed only the ledger, so a collaboration question waiting on the person was missing from it. The ledger's own rows are unchanged. The pending view, the unfiltered list and the `collab.list` and `collab.wait` counts now read one state, so they cannot disagree.
- `host.resolve_approval` takes `acknowledge_processing` for a `lattice:` ask from another owner's CAR: from CarHost it agrees to that connection's processing notice and sends, exactly as `lattice.respond { acknowledge_processing: true }`, so such a question can be answered from Approvals. The dashboard is refused `consent_is_host_only`.

- When a long conversation's older turns are compacted out of the assistant's context, the compaction notice now keeps a per-tool tally of the actions those turns attempted (for example `read_file 3 ok; shell 1 ok, 1 failed; write_file 1 declined`), and later compactions add to it in place. The assistant's prompt counts that tally as actions it attempted, so asked what it did or looked at, it no longer omits or denies an earlier read or write just because that turn is gone from its context. Declarative agents, which have no event log to look in, get the same tally (car#1644).

- Fixes in organization adoption, secret redaction, the dashboard, the machine sampler and tool permissions.
  - **An adopted organization stays when another device still holds it.** If the device it was adopted from drops it, but another of the owner's devices has it configured with the same granters, it is adopted again from that device in the same pass.
  - **Quoted GitHub permalinks keep their commit hash.** A permalink inside Markdown backticks is no longer redacted.
  - **The dashboard's stale notice names its day.** "Showing the last good read" now says which day it shows.
  - **Each Docker sampling pause is logged.** A "VM owner unknown" pause that clears and comes back is logged again.
  - **A tool permission change that may be in force says what ended.** The error names the earlier standing authorization that was ended and says to set it again with `--standing`.

- A coding-assistant session whose `car claude`/`car codex` launcher died while the assistant kept running now keeps its name and mail, instead of losing them to a replacement session (which left the running assistant with `NotHolder` on its next read). The identity takeover rule now counts the live assistant named in the run-dir pid file, with the same reused-pid guard `agents.message` uses (car#4876).

- Spend from an `embed` that CAR's assistant makes while serving a peer message now names who asked, as its `infer` already did.
  - **Every model call in a peer turn is attributed.** The daemon records `requested_by` for any call that names a peer message it delivered to the calling agent, and `car do --serve` tags `embed` as well as `infer`. The assistant still pays.

- Spend history now names the agent that asked CAR's assistant for a model turn.
  - **The assistant still pays.** A message from another agent to CAR's assistant is charged to the assistant's own spend, and its ledger rows carry the authenticated sender as `requested_by`; older rows without it still load.

- **CAR keeps its plugin installed, not only up to date.** A release used to re-pin the CAR plugin only in an assistant that already had it; one with no plugin at all (never installed, or lost) was taken as the person's choice, and the refresh still recorded itself settled. So sessions in that assistant had no work board or peer tools while `car doctor` stayed quiet. Now `car update`, `car doctor --repair` and the first `car` of a new release install the plugin into Claude Code and Codex wherever it is missing, pinned to the running release. To keep CAR out of an assistant, set `install_car_plugin = false` under `[assistants]` in CAR's config.toml.

- An older `car` (a branch build, or a second install left behind) no longer moves the Claude Code or Codex CAR plugin back to its own release when a newer `car` has already pinned it to a later one. A build run from a Cargo profile directory is now recognised as a development build even when the target directory has no `CACHEDIR.TAG`, so it never refreshes the plugin at all. Before this, two versions on one Mac took turns re-pinning the plugin, and each turn could leave Claude Code without it (car#4726).
- When `plugin marketplace remove car` fails or times out during a refresh, CAR now reads the marketplace list back. If the remove took the marketplace or the plugin anyway, the previous setup is put back; it no longer reports "nothing was changed" without checking (car#4724).

- `car update` (and the automatic plugin refresh after an update) no longer leaves Claude Code or Codex without the CAR plugin when a step fails after the old `car` marketplace was removed. The previous marketplace and plugin (installed, enabled or disabled) are put back, and the message says what failed and whether the restore worked; when the restore fails too, it names the exact commands that finish it by hand, written for PowerShell on Windows (car#4710).

- An agent-scoped audit export now attributes each event to the agent that owns its run, not to a generic `caller` label in the event's data.
  - **Nothing hidden.** An event whose data says `caller: "dashboard"` stays in its run owner's export. The data labels are used only when the run's file is gone.

- `car audit export --output` now creates an owner-only file on Windows too (a protected ACL naming only you), not just on Unix (car#4376).

- `car auth login` now says when the signed-in Parslee account has no organization yet, and points to https://parslee.ai to finish setup, instead of reporting plain success and leaving the first model call to fail. The login is still stored.

- A slow keychain no longer costs a Parslee sign-in. When saving a renewed refresh token timed out, CAR kept the new token in memory, but the next renewal sent the older token the keychain still named. Parslee had already replaced that token, so it answered `invalid_grant` and every org call failed until `car auth login`. CAR now sends the newest rotation it holds, from memory or the keychain. It blocks a token for good once Parslee has replaced it, and it no longer marks the stored login as rejected while a newer rotation is still held for it. When every rotation CAR held has been replaced, it asks you to sign in without sending another request (car#5292).

- A sync journal reads its history only after it holds the journal's writer lock, so two writers can no longer pick the same sequence number and fork the journal (#4125).
- A file the local-path guard refuses is never listed by `find_files` or the other file walks, whether it sits in a folder or is the walk's own root (#3525).
- The Parslee relay pump wakes as soon as organization work starts on this CAR, from an MCP session opening or an agent attaching with an organization work context, so the first relay pull comes in seconds instead of after the rest of a 30-second idle wait. An organization MCP session left idle past its lifetime no longer keeps three-second polling on (#3485).
- A relay pin renewal the Parslee relay refuses is retried on the next pass instead of after 30 minutes; a refusal's retry delay still holds the next directory read back (#2531).
- While a verified connection to another CAR briefly sits beside the unverified one it replaces, organization traffic and connection lookups use the verified one, whatever order the two are kept in (#3479).
- A subscription token refresh that the provider answers with success but CAR cannot use (unreadable, missing a field, another account) now marks the account as needing a login, because the provider may already have rotated the refresh token; so does a refresh whose connection fails after the request went out, or that gets a 5xx, and one the provider refuses as a dead grant (`refresh_rejected_login_required`). CAR no longer retries the old token (#4097).
- A remote connector whose server goes silent no longer hangs the call. A server that takes over 10 seconds to accept the connection, or does not finish `initialize` or `tools/list` within 120 seconds, ends the call with an error naming the wait, and the same bounds end adding an OAuth connector whose authorization server goes silent. A tool call ends at the action's own `timeout_ms` when it has one, else after 600 seconds with nothing sent, so a tool that works silently for minutes still answers (#2755).
- Registering a tool whose parameter or return JSON Schema cannot compile (through `tools.register`, `session.init`, or a `runAgent` terminal tool) now fails at setup with an error naming the tool, instead of being accepted and failing only when the model calls it (#3874).
- The assistant's and coder's delegate executors (and the bench memory router) now pass a delegated tool's failure on with its type intact, so an "unknown tool" error relayed from a client or MCP server can never make CAR run its own built-in file tool instead, however the executors are combined (#3622).
- Node and Python gain `evolutionApplyFrom` / `evolution_apply_from`: it applies a harness mutation computed against an earlier config (`baseJson` / `base_json`) by rebasing it first, so two approvals from the same base both survive instead of the later one erasing the earlier, as the daemon's `evolution.run` already does. `evolutionApply` / `evolution_apply` are unchanged (#2664).
- External Claude Code and Codex runs use the CLI's own subscription login by default: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` no longer reach the CLI from the daemon's environment, so a stray key cannot move a run to API billing. A non-isolated Codex run also loses `CODEX_API_KEY`. A run that should bill an API key declares it with `api_key_credential: true` (an option of `agents.invoke_external` and the bindings, or a declared agent's metadata; `external_api_key_credential` on `coder.start` and the bindings' coder start; `--external-api-key-credential` on `car code`, `car coder-ab` and the harness bench; a coder run's declaration reaches every foreman farm-out worker too) and is handed its key from the environment or the secret store; network-isolated Claude Code runs and isolated Codex runs keep their keys as before. Each result records what CAR selected (`credential`: `login`, `api_key`, or `cloud` for Claude Code on Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry), and a Claude Code result also carries what the CLI reports it used (`api_key_source`), which the daemon logs (#2208).
- A daemon that lost its Calendar or Contacts permission (a rebuilt, ad-hoc signed development `car-server` can lose earlier macOS grants) no longer leaves `calendar.list` and the other calendar and contacts calls waiting without end. An unanswered permission request gives up after 10 seconds with a reason naming the rebuild (a person at a terminal gets a minute to answer the macOS prompt), and a helper that stops answering is ended 10 seconds later as a timeout; for a calendar change, the timeout says the change may already have been saved. `scripts/install-dev-binaries.sh` now warns when it replaced an ad-hoc signed `car-server`, so the grants can be given again (#2177).
- `car mail send` through Mail.app no longer reports `sent: true` for a message Mail refused to send: it returns `sent: false` with a `send_refused:` reason saying to check the account in Mail, and the unsent message is discarded (#3902).
- A Node script that runs the packaged agent loop now exits on its own when its work is done, including after a failed run; before, the tool-cancel handler the loop registers held the process open. A tool handler a script registers itself to serve the daemon's calls still keeps it up until it unregisters (#3851).

- The policy hook now appends each credential-read record under an exclusive lock, treats an unparseable record line as a read so a later send is still cautioned (asked in strict mode), and no longer records a read the hook itself denied. Fixes #4365.

- The release docs now say `~/.cache/car-build.lock` is shared by nightly releases, the first shared build slot and the generated-files merge driver, while ordinary builds are kept apart by the shared build slots, list the nightly wait setting's exit-64, lock-error and `0` behaviours, and note that the lock frees when the last process holding its descriptor exits; the nightly release test now runs the timed wait. Fixes #4368.

- `car claude` and `car codex` now warn at the terminal when the session you launched has not joined the Lattice within 20 seconds, naming the session id and pointing at `car lattice nodes`, instead of leaving it off the Lattice silently; in an interactive session the warning is printed after the session exits, not over its screen. Fixes #4370.

- The test-isolation guard now scans `integration_state_isolation.rs` like every other integration test, so a raw `ServerState` constructor there is reported. Fixes #4372.

- A build no longer reuses another checkout's cross-target output when `rustc --print target-list` fails: the source refresh now stops with an error naming the command and leaves the last-checkout marker unchanged. Fixes #4373.

- A wrapped `car codex` session's direct `git worktree add` in a pool-on repository is now logged and refused like Claude Code's, including when Codex runs it through a `zsh -lc` shell wrapper. A command that hands `worktree add` text to something the guard cannot read (a shell or interpreter reading stdin, a here-doc or a script file, `eval`, `xargs`, backticks or `<(…)`) is judged from every directory it could run in, as is one that follows a `{` group or a `cd` that may fail; the docs now say a plainly started Codex session is not guarded. Fixes #4380.

- `host.resolve_approval` now returns a `journal_warning` naming the journal path and the error when a resolved approval could not be written to `host-approval-resolutions.jsonl`; the approval still resolves, and `car-host approve` / `car-host deny` print that warning to stderr and the dashboard shows it as a toast. Fixes #4383.

- The audit export now resolves each event's run owner through its own journal directory, so a run id shared by a personal and a work-context journal is no longer attributed to whichever directory was read last, and an agent-scoped export includes exactly that agent's events. Fixes #4386.

- The worktree pool's direct `git worktree add` guard now follows `--git-dir`, `--git-dir=` and `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_COMMON_DIR` (as a prefix, an `export` or an earlier assignment, including into a `sh -c` script, whatever the order of `-C`, and through a symlinked `.git`), through a wrapper such as `timeout`, `nice`, `sudo` or `env -C` (including a `GIT_DIR=` among the wrapper's words, as in `env -i GIT_DIR=...`), and from an inherited `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_COMMON_DIR` the session started with, and through an alias defined with `git -c alias.<name>=...` whose value runs `worktree`, to the repository the command actually changes, instead of judging the agent's current directory; and a message to a coding-assistant session whose recorded process id was reused by an unrelated process now reports the session as ended instead of queuing it for nobody. Fixes #4392.

- `car codex` startup instructions now name the repository's Lattice project (the main checkout's name) instead of the current folder, so a Codex session in a worktree or subdirectory stays in its repository-wide project. Fixes #4426.

- The worktree-pool skill now says that a restarted session re-binds its lease to its new process on its next acquire of the same branch, and that a dead holder's slot with uncommitted work passes to another owner only on the same branch or after `car worktree reclaim --archive-dirty`; a regression test covers both. No behaviour changes. Fixes #4431.

- The `car-cli` Codex integration tests no longer copy the operator's `~/.codex` sign-in or provider settings into their fixture home; only the ignored live-model tests do, and only with `CAR_TEST_COPY_CODEX_SIGNIN=1`. Fixes #4435.

- `car-local-peers` no longer falls back to the default daemon's MCP port when `CAR_DAEMON_URL` selects another daemon: with no usable `CAR_MCP_BIND` (unset, `disabled` or not an address) it now exits with a message naming `CAR_MCP_BIND` instead of joining the default daemon's Lattice, the plugin passes `CAR_DAEMON_URL` through to the server, and a daemon hands its children its own `CAR_MCP_BIND`, so a session under a daemon started with another `--host` or `--mcp-bind` reaches that daemon's endpoint. Fixes #4442.

- `car worktree acquire` now refuses a branch argument that looks like a commit SHA and names no branch, telling you to pass a branch name with `--base <sha>`, or to create the hex-named branch first if you meant it; before, it silently created a branch named after the SHA. Existing branches with hex names are unaffected. Fixes #4448.

- `car worktree` now reports git's own error (the command, its exit status and git's message) when it cannot read the repository for a reason other than "not a git repository", instead of always saying the directory is not in a git repository. Fixes #4453.

- The collaboration server's stdio tests now strip every collaboration variable (credentials file, pending file, session project) from each spawned process, so running them inside a `car claude` session no longer fails them. Fixes #4462.

- The car3732 worktree-pool test fixtures' prepare loop now ends when its temp directory is removed or after 5 minutes, so an interrupted test run no longer leaves a shell holding a build slot. Fixes #4486.

- `car worktree` no longer loses track of a finished slot when parking it fails (a release or reclaim that cannot park leaves its record as it was), puts a slot back on its branch when its lease cannot be removed, switches a slot that a failed release left parked under a lease back to its branch when its owner acquires it again (a detached head the owner made is left alone), keeps the slot's built-head record when a release fails after writing it, and no longer counts build output (`target/`, `.build/`, `dist/`, `.next/` and the other build and cache directories) as a recent edit when deciding whether a slot is idle. Fixes #4502.

- `car codex exec` now gives a worktree-pool session write access to the shared git directory when a value-taking option such as `-m <model>` or `--profile <name>` comes before `exec`, so commits from the slot no longer fail. Fixes #4504.

- **A Link key can read a run's log by id.** `car-release log <run-id>` was refused for the `link` role even though `status <run-id>` and `runs --after <run-id>` were allowed, so Link could follow a run it started but not read its log. The server still refuses a run id that is not a plain run name (#4556).

- **`car-release nightly --dry-run` now previews the resume of an unfinished nightly.** It used to print a fresh plan, or `no nightly due`, even when the real command would resume a tagged nightly that had failed or been interrupted. The dry run now runs the real command's resume check without touching the lab's mirror or records, and prints the version, commit, the step the run would resume from, the `REFUSED tag-mismatch` the real command would end with, or `release already running` while another release holds the lock (#4557).

- **A promotion retried after its verification passed now finishes `DONE`.** When an earlier run of the same nightly passed `verify` and then stopped before `DONE`, the retry skipped `verify` but started with the verifier result still pending, so it ended `FAILED` with exit 4. The retry now carries the earlier pass into its own record (#4558).

- **Policy hook: a shell command whose only credential word is a search pattern no longer counts as reading key material** (#4610). A Bash call used to count whenever its command text named credential material anywhere, so `git grep -n "DenyCredentialAccess"` or `… | grep -i "keychain|secret"` made every later flagged upload in that session ask. Now the hook first tries to parse the whole command under an exact allowlist of programs (grep, rg, ag, git, gh, find, sed, awk, jq, cat and similar readers) and their exact options. When it parses, the call counts if a file it opens (an operand, an option's file, a redirection) names credential material, judged both by its text and by the file it opens in the call's working directory with symlinks followed (`grep secret config` run in `~/.ssh` counts), or if any of its text other than an exempt pattern value does (an option, a comment, a here-doc, a here-string). A grep or git grep pattern, a git `--grep`, `--author`, `--committer`, `-S` or `-G` value, or a find `-name`/`-path`/`-regex` value may name a credential word, provided its pipeline writes no file and feeds only programs that read piped data, and the command opens only files its text spells: with a glob, a recursive grep, rg or ag (which walk directories), a `cd`, a `~+`/`~-`/`~user` path, a git diff path or `--no-index`, or a file that has another hard link, the pattern counts as before. Anything the allowlist does not cover counts exactly as before. That includes an expansion (`$…`, backticks), a subshell, a leading assignment or wrapper, an interpreter, an unlisted program or option, an option that takes file names from input, an `@` operand, and awk, sed or jq text, a commit message or gh text naming a credential word. A file named for a credential word (`credential_access.rs`) still counts. What a text check cannot see stays as it was: which binary a name resolves to through PATH, and the helpers that environment variables and config files choose.

- **Policy hook: commit messages, gh text, tracked source files and in-repo searches that only mention a credential word no longer count as reading key material; hard-linked files and `gh -F key=@path` now do** (#4729, #4751, #4762). The words `credential`, `secret`, `password` and `keychain` name a topic as often as a file. A Bash call that names one of them only in message text no longer makes a later flagged upload ask. Message text means echo and printf text, a `git commit -m`/`--message` (including the common `-m "$(cat <<'EOF' … EOF)"` form), gh `--title`/`--body`/`-f`/`--search`, a here-doc body, a here-string or a comment. It still counts when awk, gawk or sed is in the command, since they can turn that text into a file name or a command. Two other cases also no longer count:
  - reading a git-tracked source or doc file named for one of those words (`cat crates/car-policy/src/credential_access.rs`), where the file has one link, a source or doc extension and no key-material name;
  - a recursive grep, rg or ag below a worktree subdirectory, where every file it can reach is tracked source with one link or a harmless untracked file, and nothing below it is a nested repo or the `.git` directory.

  A key-material name (`.netrc`, `id_rsa`, `.aws/credentials`, a `.pem`, …) still counts anywhere. So do awk, sed and jq programs naming any credential word, and any check that cannot complete: no working directory, git failing or taking over 2 s, `$HOME` unset, or a worktree at or above `$HOME`.

  Two new cases now count:
  - A file with another hard link is read whatever its name, by a shell command or a Read, Grep or Glob call, since a hard link can hide key material under a harmless name.
  - A gh `-F`/`--field` value `key=@path` reads `path`, as gh does.

  None of these exemptions applies when the same command opens a file its text does not spell (a glob, a `cd`, a hard link) or walks a directory it cannot check: then the whole command counts, as before.

- The worktree pool's direct-add guard no longer refuses a git alias that runs a non-add worktree subcommand, such as `git -c alias.wl='worktree list' wl` or `git -c 'alias.wp=!git worktree prune' wp`. An alias of bare `worktree` is refused only when the next word is `add`, and an alias whose subcommand cannot be read, such as a shell function, is still refused (car#4777).

- A lane daemon that runs as a launchd Background job (the logout-surviving `car-lane.sh` lanes) can now sign in to Parslee. It runs in its own macOS security session, where the login keychain always reads as locked even on an unlocked, logged-in Mac, so every secret read failed with "macOS keychain is locked". On macOS a process whose security session has neither graphic access nor a terminal now uses the headless store `<CAR_HOME>/secrets`, as headless Linux already does. Daemons in the GUI session and SSH sessions keep the keychain. Secrets a Background lane held in the keychain before were never readable by it, so nothing moves; sign in again through that lane (car#5241).

- `car-beads` accepts a labelled ISA claim line: `- [ ] GR-168 [W]: …` (or `[H]`, `[Hd]`) now satisfies the claim check for `GR-168`, so an ISA copied from the build process no longer needs its labels stripped. Other bracketed suffixes still do not match (car#5043).

- `car beads rebuild --offline` rebuilds the bead index from the enrolled repositories with no daemon running, against `CAR_HOME` (a scratch home, say). It holds the daemon's lock while it runs, and refuses while a daemon is running for that home or when a sync passphrase is set or the home's journal is one only a daemon with a passphrase opens (Parslee-synced, encrypted or waiting for sign-in) (car#4760).

- On Bedrock, `tool_choice: "none"` with tools present no longer becomes a forced call to a tool named "none". `infer` and `infer_stream` now refuse it before sending anything, with `UnsupportedMode` mode `tool-choice-none` and backend `bedrock`, because Bedrock Converse has no `none` mode. Omit the tools, or route to a provider that supports `"none"` (car#5158).

- An image sent by URL to a Bedrock model is refused with `UnsupportedMode` (`image-url-content-block`), before anything is signed or sent. Bedrock's Converse API carries image bytes only, so the URL used to reach the model as the text `[image: <url>]` and the model could answer as though it had seen the image. Send the image as base64 (`ImageBase64`), which Bedrock still accepts, or route to a provider that takes image URLs. The check covers request images and every multimodal turn of the history.

- Benchmark runs no longer publish a zero for a model whose backend hung.
  - **A hang is withheld, not scored.** `car-bench-run` now records a task that timed out before the backend answered even once as `timeout: backend produced no response`, and `bench-consolidate.py` counts it as an incomplete task under speed-scaled limits too. A task whose backend answered at least once and then ran past its scaled limit is still scored as a failure in the run's overall score, even if the backend then stalled mid tool loop. Generation is not streamed, so a first answer slower than the whole limit is withheld as a hang too. Results written before this keep reading as they did. (#3748)

- A CAR no longer floods the Parslee board with requests it has already been told to hold back. After a 429 from the board, every later board request signed by the same device key, from any part of the daemon, fails at once as `rate_limited` without being sent until the `Retry-After` time has passed (5 seconds when none is given, at most 5 minutes), and a 429 is no longer retried. `board.list` on an organization's sealed board no longer reads each item's log, so a listed row's `updated_by` is the item's content writer; `board.history` and the other single-item reads still name the member who last claimed, checked in or closed it. A refusal while reading an item's log now stops the read instead of being skipped (car#5288).

- On an organization's shared board, a card can be linked to every collaboration it came up in, not just one. `board.upsert` with only an item's `id` and `collaboration` adds a link to an existing card without changing the card, and linking the same collaboration again does nothing. Only the card's creator may link it. **Breaking for readers of `board.list`:** `came_up_in` on a sealed board row is now a list of `{ collaboration, title }`, one per linked collaboration the reader is in, and `[]` when there is none; it used to be a single object, absent when there was none. A card linked before this change reads as a one-entry list.

- Each comment on an organization board item now tells the item's creator. Two comments that read the same, or that match in the first 500 characters a notice quotes, used to give the same notice, and the second was dropped as a repeat. Each notice now names the comment's history entry (`board_history` lists it as `seq`). The same comment's notice sent again is still one (car#4884, car#4879).

- `board.list` on an organization's sealed board, and the Needs you lookups that read it, now read a local copy of the board kept current from Parslee's change feed. An unchanged board costs one request; a changed one reads only the changed items. A refused or rate-limited read returns the last copy marked `stale: true` with `stale_reason`, instead of an empty board.

- On an organization's sealed board, `board.history` takes a change row's fields only from a record added after that change, so a record forged before it can no longer stand in once its writer is erased. An erased writer's change with more than one such record is shown with none and `writer: "former_member:ambiguous"` instead of whichever came first. A collaboration post from an erased member whose signature can't be checked no longer names its session.

- Every `board.list` row now carries `lane`, the Board's lane for the item: `settled` (done or dropped), `waiting_on_person` (waiting, or a handoff or assignment pending), or `under_way` (everything else, stale items included), so a screen can show each item in exactly one lane.
- On an organization's shared board, `board.upsert` takes `blocked_by`, a list of items that block this one: it stays out of Ready until each of them is done or dropped. An open item that is still blocked can still be claimed.
- On an organization's shared board, `board.upsert` takes `collaboration`, the id of a collaboration you are in where the item came up. Its members see the item's `came_up_in` with the collaboration's title; the board records nothing about the collaboration, so org members outside it never learn its title or id from the board.

- Work board lines and briefings: "your account" now marks only an item
  whose words are all your account's, so a policy relays your owner's rule
  only then. `board.list` rows carry `written_by_you`; on today's account
  boards it equals `mine`, and every line reads as before. The briefing
  footer now reads "An item is changed by the account holding it, or by its
  creator while nobody holds it", which on today's boards means what it did.
  Once the org board is wired, a line there also names who holds an item
  ("held by you" / "held by X"), names every account whose words are in it,
  `mine` becomes an item you hold or created while nobody holds it, a row's
  `owner` becomes whoever holds the item (else its creator, and empty while
  stale), and a stale item reads "free to take" with no names. Another CAR's
  shared item never carries a holder.

- CarHost's Needs you no longer reads every organization's whole sealed board every 20 seconds. `board.list` on an organization's sealed board now returns the board's `change_seq`, and a call that passes it back as `unless_changed_since` while nothing has changed gets `{ unchanged: true, change_seq }` after one backend read, with no item pages read. CarHost sends it and keeps its marks on `unchanged`. It still reads each board in full about every 5 minutes, on reconnect, and after any listing that left out items whose key had not arrived yet. On an account board the parameter is accepted and ignored (car#4892).

- An org board notice is no longer queued for a creator or previous holder who has left the organization when the relay sends no roster, provided this CAR has verified the departure: its pair with them no longer has them as a member, or a history it holds records their `departed` while none has them as a member and they hold no certificate now. Their `notified` row says `queued: false` with the reason, and nothing carrying the item's title is stored for them. A notice is still queued when nothing this CAR has verified speaks to that account (before the first collaboration pass after a restart, or for someone who shares no conversation with it); the sealer still refuses to send it to someone who left (car#4880).

- An org board notice is no longer queued for a creator or previous holder who has left the organization. When the relay sends the org's roster, the write's `notified` row for someone its directory no longer lists says `queued: false` and why, and nothing carrying the item's title is stored for them (car#4880).

- On an organization's sealed board, `board.list` no longer shows an item as both held and ready. The rows and the backend's Ready are two reads, and a claim, release, handoff or assignment could land between them. A row is now marked `ready` only when Ready named the item at the same version the row carries, and never while the row names a holder who has not missed a check-in. An item freed between the reads reads free but not ready until the next list (car#4903).
- When CAR can't check whether an organization has a sealed board, it shows the board stored on this device, and its replies have carried a `notice` saying so. CarHost's Board screen and the `car board` commands now show that notice: CarHost as a line above the rows, the CLI on stderr. The organization still uses the file board until a check answers (car#4903).

- `car board reconcile` no longer abandons a work item whose branch has not been pushed yet. A branch missing from `origin` read the same as a deleted one, so an item announced before its first push was marked `abandoned` "with no pull request" within one pass. Now an item is abandoned for a missing branch only after reconcile has seen that branch on `origin`; a branch never pushed leaves the item in its owner's state, and an open pull request still moves it to `review`. Items whose branch an older daemon had already seen are still abandoned when it is deleted (car#4719).

- After someone leaves an organization, the shared board's new key is now copied only to devices on a device directory read from the relay at that moment. Before, the rotation, finishing a rotation that stopped partway, and a later open copying the key to newly listed devices could all use a cached directory that still listed the departed person's devices, and a key copy cannot be taken back. A read the relay's limit holds back, or a relay error, now stops the copy instead: the write that needed the new key fails and is retried, and an open keeps working without copying. The board's first key at setup still uses the cached directory (car#4763).

- An `ask` on an organization's sealed board (`board.upsert` / `board_upsert` with `kind: "ask"` waiting on `human:<name>`) now tries to send the question, as on a personal board, and returns `asked`. Before, the sealed board never tried, and the result had no `asked` and no reason. A session bound to an organization still cannot reach a person, so today `asked` says `queued: false` and why, and the item is not marked as asked. A question that does go out is recorded on the sealed item once, so an edit does not ask again (car#4914).

- On an organization's shared board, agents and people can now claim, check in on, release, hand off, assign, accept and decline items (`board.claim`, `board.check_in`, `board.release`, `board.handoff`, `board.assign`, `board.accept`, `board.decline`, the matching `board_*` MCP tools, and `car board claim|check-in|release|handoff|assign|accept|decline`). Claiming takes an item out of everyone else's Ready. `board.list` there now says which items are ready to pick up (`ready`, and a `ready: true` filter, as the backend decides it), who an item waits on (`pending`), check-in times, labels, and your `role`, so CarHost's Board screen offers these controls, counts Ready correctly, and hides write controls from a Viewer. A Viewer's writes are refused with "Viewers can only read this organization's board, not change it; nothing was written". `board.upsert` takes `description` and `labels`, and on a shared board an `id` no item has yet, with a project and title, creates the item under that id. `board.history` there names every action with who and when. `claimed` and `dropped` are accepted as `in_progress` and `abandoned`, so CarHost's Drop works on a shared board (car#4823).

- `car board setup` no longer tells a person without a terminal to use CarHost, which cannot run setup yet. Its prompt says items on the current board are kept on this device but no longer shown, and setup's reply says other members' CARs can still write to the old board until their once-a-minute check with Parslee succeeds, which for a CAR that can't reach Parslee lasts until it can (car#4792).

- CarHost's Board shows every card's history on first open again. Each card used to read its own history, and on an organization's shared board each of those reads opened the board again, so a Board of a few dozen cards used up this device's budget with Parslee and the cards said "May be out of date: CAR didn't answer". Cards now ask together: `board.history` takes `ids` (up to 50 items) and reads them all from one open of the board, answering each item with its history or the reason it wasn't read, without retry waits, so a refusal reaches the card that asked while CarHost still waits (CAR-975).

- On an organization's sealed board, `board.claim`, `board.release` and `board.accept` now tell the item's creator and its previous holder when they change who holds the item, as `board.transition` does, and every ownership verb's reply carries `notified`. An accepted handoff or assignment says it was accepted rather than reading as a takeover. A check-in, a handoff or assignment asked, and a decline still tell nobody and return `notified: []` (car#4887).

- The release lab's stable bookkeeping pull request now records a consumed changelog fragment with `main`'s text when `main` edited it after the nightly. A fragment flagged by the pull request's required `changelog` check can be fixed by rewording it on `main` and re-running bookkeeping, with no hand commit on the bookkeeping branch (car#4658).

- **A verifier check run's private build output no longer outlives the run when it stops early.** A check run's directory, with the cargo target built inside it, was removed only on the normal path, so an early error left the whole built target under `check-runs`; the run directory is now removed when the run ends, including on errors, panics and a cancelled run, once any copy into it has stopped. A run still in progress when the daemon shuts down can leave its directory behind (car#4396).

- The build.yml promotion-mode graph test knows the nightly smoke-linux-archives job again.

- `car-ast` indexes every name a C or C++ typedef declares: `typedef struct foo foo_t, *foo_ptr;` now yields both `foo_t` and `foo_ptr`, and a function-pointer typedef such as `typedef int (*cb_t)(int);` yields `cb_t`. Before, C kept only the first name and dropped function-pointer typedef names, and C++ indexed no typedefs at all (car#5065).

- A decision class can set `no_rungs: true`. Good, Wrong and Undo grades on its own entries are still recorded and counted (a Wrong or Undo still becomes a classifier case), but they never move the class's rung, so a grade never pulls the class back to asking the owner for approval, and an owner override that raised it stays. An owner override still moves it, and the `succeeds` family cap still applies when another class in its family moves. The dashboard shows no promotion bar for such a class and says grades never move it.

- CarHost no longer flips back to signed in when a background credential refresh finishes after you sign out.

- `car claude --background` (and `car claude -- --bg`) no longer passes `--session-id`, which Claude Code ignores under `--bg`. The launcher now reads the session's real id back from `claude agents --json` after the launch, names the launch spec with it and prints it, so `car sessions status` and `car sessions settings <id>` name the session that actually runs. A caller's own `--session-id` with `--bg` is dropped with a notice. A role is no longer passed through `CAR_SESSION_ROLE`, which a pre-warmed background process could carry over from an earlier call. Instead the launcher renames the agent the session's helper enrolled to `Claude Code - <dir> (role <role>)`, and prints `role not applied: <why>` when it cannot find that agent. What `claude --bg` prints is still shown unchanged (car#4881).
- An interactive `car claude` / `car codex` session that stays off the Lattice now raises a local notification while the session runs, telling you to check `car lattice nodes` and restart. Previously the warning was printed only after the session exited. If the notification cannot be shown, the warning is still printed after exit (car#4786).

- Sessions started by `car claude` can use CAR's collaboration tools when they cannot answer a permission prompt, and Claude Code background sessions keep their collaboration identity (car#4825, car#4824).
  - **No allow rule needed.** `car claude` passes `--allowedTools=mcp__plugin_car_car-collaboration` to every session it starts, so `lattice_join`, `board_*` and `peer_*` work under `denyInsteadOfPrompting`, in `-p` runs and in `--bg` sessions. Only that server's tools are allowed, and a deny rule for them still wins.
  - **`car claude -- --bg` is a background launch.** Claude Code's own `--bg` / `--background` after `--` (including `--resume <id> --bg`) now goes through the same path as `car claude --background`, instead of enrolling an identity for the `claude` that returns at once.
  - **A background session enrolls its own identity.** Claude Code runs a background session in a pre-warmed process that kept an earlier launch's environment, so its collaboration server can inherit another session's credentials file. The server no longer refuses with "this collaboration identity belongs to the `claude` that `car claude` started"; it enrolls the session through `car session-enroll`. A credentials file issued to another process is still never used, and neither is the pending-message file that came with it: the session keeps its own unread count beside its own identity, and its inbox reminders read that count, so another session's count is never overwritten.
  - **Removed when the session ends.** `car-mcp --collaboration` removes the agent it enrolled on SIGTERM or SIGHUP as well as when its stdin closes, so `claude stop` removes it at once.

- The direct `git worktree add` guard now follows a command that empties HOME. `HOME=; cd ~/pool` enters `/pool` in bash, zsh and dash, so the guard judges `/pool` instead of only the starting directory; a bare `cd` with an empty HOME stays put. A HOME set from `$OTHER` or a backtick is still treated as unknown (car#5080).
- `car update` no longer treats a repository git cannot read as clean. When a `.git` entry is present but `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` fails, the client-library update for that agent is refused with git's error instead of rewriting its package files; a directory with no `.git` anywhere above it is still a plain non-checkout (car#5107).
- With the worktree pool off, a subagent's stop no longer deletes a clean worktree that a process is still running in. The tree is kept and the hook says which process holds it, or that it cannot tell (car#5112).
- `car permissions status` asks the running CAR daemon first, so it reports the grant the app holds rather than the terminal's. Only when nothing is listening does it check its own process. The printed JSON gains `reported_for` (`daemon` or `this car process`), and the same is said on stderr. A daemon that answers with an error is reported as an error (car#3723).

- New `car job` command (macOS and Linux): `car job start --cwd <dir> [--key <name>] [--env-allow NAME...] -- <cmd>` starts a command that keeps running after the shell or agent session that started it ends, and prints a job id. The command gets no terminal, stdin from `/dev/null`, and only the environment variables you allow; its output goes to the job's log. From any later shell, `car job status`, `list`, `wait`, `logs [--follow]` and `cancel` read or stop it. `wait` exits with the command's own exit code, or 70 when the job was cancelled or lost. A `--key` makes a repeated start return the existing job instead of starting a second copy, and exits 4 if the same key was used for a different command. A job whose wrapper process is killed reads as `lost (wrapper gone)`, and `cancel` still stops what it left running while the command itself is alive; once the command is gone too, `cancel` refuses rather than signal a session id that may now belong to something else. Nothing is deleted automatically: `car job purge` lists finished jobs, and `car job purge --apply` archives each one's outcome to `jobs/archive/<id>.json` before removing it, logging every removal to `jobs/purge.log`. Windows is not supported yet (car#4417) (car#4412, car#4416).

- `car-server --help` now says which ports it binds next to `--port`.
  - **The dashboard port is derived.** `--port` help names the dashboard (UI) listener on `--port + 1`, and `--mcp-bind` help says its `127.0.0.1:9102` default does not follow `--port`.
  - **Handshake first.** The WebSocket protocol docs now say `host.subscribe` needs a successful `server.handshake` on the connection first.

- Build an Agent's schedule step no longer starts blank: it offers Only when I ask (preselected), Every weekday, Every day and Custom…, a day, time and time-zone picker that writes a phrase CAR's schedule grammar reads. Typing your own answer still works. Once an answer settles, the step and the review show how CAR reads it ("CAR reads this as: …"), or say that CAR can't read it, with Looks right / Change (car#2721).

- CarHost's Approvals screen now lists every ask waiting on you, the same asks its count shows, with who asks, the collaboration, the question and whether it is an approval or a decision. Answer an approval with Allow once or Decline, a decision with one of its options or a typed answer, and a handoff or assignment with Accept or Decline. An answered ask leaves the list and the count at once. When CAR refuses an answer, the ask stays and says why. With a CAR that does not list asks yet, the screen is unchanged.

- CarHost Chat takes dropped and pasted files while a reply is still coming in. They wait in the message box, which says they go with the message sent once the reply finishes; Attach Image… is offered during a reply too (car#2374).
- The collaboration composer says when agents answer: an ask or an @mention wakes them at once, and any other post waits for their next check-in, up to 15 minutes (car#5253).
- A declared agent's own page shows its schedule as CAR read it, the words the person wrote, and the time zone it keeps (car#2721).
- CarHost collaboration and Board polish (car#5178): VoiceOver names the Board's lane headings ("Coming up, 2 cards"), a work-panel card row ("Open <title>"), an ask's options and the folded agent-update button; a "Raised on the board" post for a card the Board hasn't listed reads the Board again at once; the header's member avatars no longer draw over one another and Invite clears the browser drawer's globe; the rail's Collaborate list keeps about three rows in the shortest window (it kept under two) and scrolls the open collaboration into view; and Tools, Settings, Home and chat history rows select in the same Parslee accent as collaborations.

- CarHost's Board reports a create whose reply was lost as saved only when the new item shows the note and the person asked, and a conversation no longer drops a recent send or keeps an old one below newer messages when the Mac's clock is set behind or ahead (car#4811).

- On the CarHost Board, your own item no longer reads "Stale · free to take" once it's a day old. It still says You. "Free to take" now appears only when CAR says someone else may take the item.

- CarHost's Board is a Tools screen again, right after Approvals, and no longer heads Collaborate. It shows three lanes, Waiting on a person, Under way and Settled, exactly as CAR sorts each item, and each card shows its title, description, where it came up and its trail. Needs you now counts only the asks waiting on you, on Approvals and on each collaboration's row; a plain @-mention still notifies you and bolds the row but adds to no count, and opening something never lowers a count.

- CarHost’s Board and People screens now fit the window they open in. Board’s Show filter becomes a menu when the window is too narrow for its segmented control and counts, and so does People’s organization filter when there are too many organizations to show side by side; a long organization or project name is cut short in its menu instead of widening the page, so neither screen is clipped any more (car#4837). While an agent that uses Mail has a schedule, the Scheduled screen now says plainly that its scheduled run may be refused Mail access even though Run now works, because nobody has checked yet whether macOS gives a scheduled run CAR’s Mail permission (car#3888).

- CarHost's Board is read-only. It shows the three lanes and their cards and nothing else: no Refresh, no New item, no filters, and a card opens nothing when clicked. People add and change items through their agents and the `board.*` calls. The screen still reads the board again on its own while it is open. A card whose trail is cut says how many earlier entries there are, without asking you to open it.

- The CarHost work board is safer to write to:
  - An older board read that answers late no longer overwrites a newer one.
  - When CAR saves a change but its reply is lost, CarHost checks the board instead of reporting a failure that invites a duplicate. It says the change saved, that it didn't, or that you should check first.
  - Links that read the same each keep their own row (car#4720).
  - A role this CarHost doesn't know now gets the read-only board instead of write controls.
  - People who share a name are told apart in the hand-off and assign picker. Typing a shared name is refused rather than silently picking one of them.
  - On a board with more items than CarHost lists, Add a blocker can find older open items through CAR (car#4732).

- CarHost's board no longer calls a pending request of an unknown kind a handoff or offers Accept/Decline for it. Such an item reads "<name> sent you a request this version of CarHost can't show" (or "Waiting on <name>" when it is addressed to someone else) and stays locked; if you hold it, Check in and Let it go remain (car#4894).

- The CarHost Board gets the shared org board's actions: Take it, Check in, Let it go, Hand off and, for admins, Assign. A handoff or assignment to you shows Accept and Decline. An item shows what blocks it, by title, and you can add or remove a blocker. A new Ready filter shows open items nobody holds and nothing open blocks. A Viewer can read the board but not change it. Items also show their description and labels. None of this appears until your organization's board offers these actions, so the board looks the same until then.

- CarHost has a Board screen: your organization's shared record of work, under Tools. Filter by Mine, Waiting on me, Stale or All, each with its count, and by kind and project. Open an item to see where it stands, its links, related items and its log, and to comment. On your own items you can edit the title and note and move them between Open, In progress, Waiting, Review, Done and Dropped. Waiting asks who you're waiting on and for what. A stale item shows "Stale · free to take" without naming anyone, and people show by name, never by an account id. When CAR can't be reached, the board says it may be out of date and keeps what it last read. Only an organization's board appears here, never your personal one.

- CarHost's Chat starter chips now follow a slow app's late permission answer without any action from you. Before, when you revoked or granted Mail, Calendar or Notes access while that app was slow to answer its Automation check, the chips kept the earlier state until Chat next came forward or the app was reactivated. The assistant's `agent.chat.tools` reply now carries `pending: true` when a check was still running at its 700 ms deadline, and the daemon passes that on as `tools_pending: true` on the flagship's `agents.list` row. Chat then reads the list once more, 2.5 s later, which is past the 2 s bound on each check. A turn inside the 15 s view window already reads the late answer once it is stored, so it stops offering a revoked app's tools (car#4237).

- CarHost marks what needs you in your collaborations. A post that @-mentions you or a question that asks you puts a "Needs you" mark on that collaboration in the sidebar, and when CarHost isn't in front a macOS notification names who sent what; opening the collaboration clears both. Any other new post, including one between agents that names nobody, only makes the collaboration's row bold with its unread count. Each collaboration's row now shows its title and its members, and Board in Collaborate shows its Needs-you count again.
- CarHost: answer a question from inside the collaboration. A question that asks you shows Answer (and its suggested answers reply to it); your reply joins the thread in order, shows which question it answers, and the question's Needs-you mark clears.
- Collaborations: `collab.wait` with `by_sender` gives each collaboration row `needs`, one entry per post that needs the caller: `{ message_id, from, kind, at_ms }`, where `kind` is `ask` for a question still asking them and `mention` for an unread post that @-mentions them by name, display name, email or first name. Other posts only count in `unread`.

- CarHost's collaboration screen shows "Work in this collaboration" beside the thread: the Board cards that came up there, in the Board's lanes, with Settled limited to today. Clicking a card opens its description and trail. The Board gains a Coming up lane, drawn first, for work nobody has started; it stays empty until CAR sends that lane. Hovering an agent in a collaboration's header says whose agent it is, for example "xavier · Keenan's agent".
- `board.list` rows on an organization's board carry `lane: "coming_up"` for an open item nobody holds, which is work nobody has started. Account boards keep open items `under_way`.
- CarHost reads a Board card's `came_up_in` as a list (CAR-984). A card linked to several collaborations shows in each one's Work panel, with one "Came up in" line per collaboration. The single object an older CAR sends still reads.

- CarHost's Collaborate list now shows at launch for a saved account, with no
  trip to setup: `collab.list` names the `account` it was read under, so
  CarHost shows the list without reading the account list from the Keychain,
  and drops it when CAR answers for another account. Collaborate's rows scroll
  on their own, so Tools, the chats, You and a thread's composer stay in the
  window however many collaborations there are, down to the shortest window,
  which still shows the first rows; an empty chat list's message scrolls
  rather than pushing them out. A thread opened from Approvals
  before the list loaded names its members once it has. A Start that CAR is
  still passing to Parslee now finishes and opens the collaboration on one
  press, and says "Starting…" in plain words while it waits.

- CarHost's sidebar runs Home, Collaborate, then Tools, and Tools holds exactly Approvals, Board, People and Settings. Scheduled, Coder, Agents, Live controls (A2UI) and the other screens left the sidebar: click Settings to open it, or use its menu to reach them. Nothing is pinned or unpinned any more, and More is gone. Collaborate lists each collaboration in two lines: its name, then who needs you ("xavier needs you on 2 things") while asks there wait on you. A dot shows while it holds posts you haven't seen, and a post that @-mentions you makes the row bold without adding to any count. Opening a collaboration shows its shared thread, which everyone in it reads and writes, people and agents, and new posts appear by themselves. Beside the thread, a lighter panel shows what waits on you, one ask at a time: a decision with its options or a typed answer, or an approval with Allow once and Decline. A chosen option goes to the asker alone; a typed answer is posted in the thread for everyone, and the card says so. Answer it and the next one appears. A run of agents asking or answering each other folds into one line. The panel folds to a strip that keeps the count. Approvals groups its asks by collaboration, each reading "From xavier in Friday trip swap" with a link that opens that collaboration; asks from agents working alone, direct asks and board handoffs each get a group of their own, and every row keeps its own answer buttons. When CAR couldn't read a board just now, Approvals says so in CAR's words and its count shows a + ("2+"), rather than quietly dropping that board's asks. These screens and the Board use Parslee's navy and emerald, in light and dark. Direct conversations are no longer listed under Collaborate. A CAR that doesn't serve collaborations yet shows one line saying they can't be loaded (car#4355).

- CarHost's Collaborate section lists your collaborations, with unread counts, and has New collaboration: give it a title and pick people and agents one by one, and it opens at once as one shared thread with its members named at the top. Posts from everyone, people and agents alike, read oldest first, each with who posted it and the time. Send clears the box at once and shows your post marked Sending, then Delivered; "Held on this Mac" shows only while Parslee is unreachable, and a refused post comes back to the box with the reason. Posts by others appear while the thread is open, with no refresh. Invite adds one person or agent at a time, and inviting a person never brings in their agents.

- CarHost conversations are more faithful to what CAR holds:
  - Past the newest 200 entries, a message CAR already took no longer reappears below newer ones.
  - A member's departure shows as a line in the conversation instead of disappearing.
  - A conversation reply CarHost can't read keeps what is on screen and says it may be out of date, instead of showing an empty conversation (car#4774).

- CarHost: Message on a colleague's People row opens your pair conversation with them, with no accept or connect step. Each message you send shows where it stands (Delivered, waiting with a clock, held on this Mac, Sent but not confirmed with Retry, or the reason it wasn't sent), and messages that can't be opened yet say so instead of showing nothing (#4405).

- CarHost no longer sends its host or daemon key to whatever program answers on the daemon port. Before sending a key, it asks the listener to prove it holds that key with the new pre-auth `session.prove` method (an HMAC over a fresh nonce, on the same connection). A program that took the port while CAR was down or restarting can't answer, so CarHost closes the connection, says it did not send its key, and tries again on its normal reconnect. A daemon too old to know `session.prove` gets no key either. On a direct loopback connection the proof is also bound to the port CarHost dialed, so a squatter can't relay the challenge to a real daemon on another port. A `CAR_DAEMON_URL` bridge, tunnel or remote endpoint keeps working; a loopback port forward must be dialed by this Mac's hostname or another alias rather than `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1` (car#3658).

- CarHost shows mail held for you in each organization's inbox. Mail sent to you while none of your sessions took it now appears under People's "Held for you", with the sender, the time, the message as it was written, and a note when it was meant for a session that had ended. It gets the same Needs-you mark and banner as other waiting items and adds to no Approvals count. CarHost reads it with `lattice.inbox` without `consume`, so a background read never marks mail read. Opening the list acknowledges exactly the messages it shows, each as `{ id, from }`, so mail that arrives later stays marked (car#4869).

- CarHost: reading a long collaboration thread upward past "Earlier posts" no longer skips posts. After the earlier page loaded, the thread stayed at the top of the new page instead of at the post you were reading, so scrolling up jumped about 50 posts and the ones in between were never on screen. The post that was at the top now stays in the same place on screen after the earlier page loads (car#5143, CAR-959).

- CarHost's Invite popover has an optional message box (up to 2,000 characters, CAR's limit for `collab.invite`'s `message`). The message goes with every invitation sent from it and the box clears after each send. Today CAR delivers it only for a registered agent, to the agent's owner (in their approval); a person's invitation does not carry it yet.

- CarHost's Invite is now a searchable list grouped as People, Agents and Your sessions running now, instead of one long menu of session and thread ids. Each session reads as what it is and where it runs ("Claude Code in car") with its name underneath; a name that is only an id is never shown, and a session that has ended is never offered. New collaboration uses the same list. `collab.who` now gives your own sessions' `program` and `folder` (the folder's own name, never the full path) when CAR knows them.

- CarHost no longer retires an unrelated launchd job just because one of its arguments is named `car-server`. A legacy `ai.parslee.car-server` or `ai.parslee.car.daemon` job counts as CAR's server only when the program it runs (after `env`) is a `car-server`, or its wrapper has a `car-server` beside it. Other programs under those labels are left loaded (car#3702).

- CarHost and the `.pkg` installer now install on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or newer, down from macOS 26, matching the `car` CLI and daemon.
- On macOS 15 through 25 the app runs, but Apple's on-device model and Apple Translation need macOS 26, and CAR does not offer them there. The Apple Translation error now says it needs macOS 26 instead of macOS 15.4, and the docs for both features say macOS 26.

- CarHost marks what is waiting on you until you open it: a new message from a colleague, a handoff or an assignment on your organization's board. The mark shows on the person in People, on the board row, on Board and People in the sidebar (or More), on the menu bar icon and on the Dock icon. While CarHost is not in front, a macOS notification names who sent what, once per new thing; opening the item, or accepting or declining a handoff or assignment, takes down both the mark and the notification. Relaunching CarHost keeps both until it has read your organizations again, so nothing is taken down or announced twice while it starts, and clicking a notification left from before opens its item once CarHost has read it. A handoff or assignment to you shows Accept and Decline on its board row, never as a pop-up (car#4867).
- `collab.wait` takes `by_sender: true` and then also answers who has unread mail for you, per conversation, with the count and the newest message, without marking anything read; opening the conversation (`collab.conversation` with `mark_read`) clears it.
- An approval whose `details.kind` is `colleague_request` (a colleague asking one of your agents to merge, approve, deploy, delete, spend, send outside the organization or change access) shows Allow once and Decline in CarHost, and while CarHost is not in front arrives as a notification with those two buttons; answering either way takes down the ask and the notification.
- CarHost reads a board assignment the way the daemon sends it (`pending.kind` `"assignment"`); it read only `"assign"`, so an assignment to you showed as an unknown kind.

- CarHost: a post from another person's session or agent no longer shows its owner beside the author. A member's owner shows in the member list and on hover only, as `<agent> · <owner>'s agent`, including for a session whose owner isn't a member of the collaboration, and the same on hovering a post's author or avatar, whether the post came from your own CAR or another (car#5136, CAR-986).

- CarHost compiles again on main. The collaboration thread passed the board cards it can open to a thread pane whose initializer didn't accept them, after car#5177 and the read-dwell work crossed.

- A remote session's owner no longer appears beside each of its posts in a CarHost collaboration thread; it shows only in the member list and on hover (CAR-986).

- CarHost's rail now lists the collaborations CAR holds even when it can't read the org list, for example while the Keychain is locked. Before, it showed nothing while `collab.list` returned dozens. Signed out, the rail says "Sign in to Parslee to see your collaborations." instead of looking empty (car#5242).
- CarHost names organizations by name, never by their `org_…` id, in the New collaboration menu and sheet and on the Lattice screens. The sheet names its org even when CAR can't list that org's people yet. Each colleague's "Verified by Parslee" line names their own org, so no screen assumes everyone is in one org (CAR-977).

- CarHost's rail ends with a You row: your initial, your name and your organization from your Parslee sign-in. Before you sign in it reads "You" over "Not signed in".

- CarHost: a message you retry, and CAR takes, stays in the conversation with the result CAR reported. That holds even when a reload during or just before the retry returns a page without it, or an older copy of it. A retry CAR never received changes nothing (car#4860).

- CarHost: clearing every day in Build an Agent's Custom… schedule now clears the schedule, and Continue waits for a day instead of building the last one chosen (car#5019).

- CarHost conversations: pressing Send clears the box at once and shows the message with a "Sending…" mark until CAR reports on it. A send CarHost couldn't make removes that bubble and puts the words back in the box, in front of anything typed meanwhile (car#4852).
- CarHost Board: an item's Log shows when each entry happened as a fixed time ("10:56 AM" today, the date before that, and the year once it isn't this year's) instead of a relative time that keeps counting. The Log stays oldest first with the newest at the bottom, as conversations are (car#4853).
- CarHost People and Board show an organization's name (for example "Fulcrum") wherever a person reads it: tags, the Organization picker, the board header, Message and Connect menus, Held for you and the out-of-date line. An org the signed-in login doesn't name reads as words with no underscores, and org tags stay on one line (car#4854).

- CarHost: a question asked of everyone in a collaboration shows who took it and what they answered, for every member ("Dana took this: “Hangar 5”"), once someone has answered it (CAR-985).

- Make CarHost collaboration read-dwell tests independent of scheduler speed, and ensure the owner-placement drawing test compares different hover labels in both layouts.

- CarHost marks a collaboration post read only once it has sat still on screen for a second. A post that passes by in a fast scroll, or that is on screen only while earlier posts load, stays unread, and so does one left open while CarHost is behind another app, minimized, or on a locked screen. Opening a thread no longer clears its unread count, and neither does a new post that arrives below the visible part of the thread; the count falls as you scroll through the posts (CAR-959).
- A collaboration thread shows a "New posts" line where your unread posts began when you opened it. It stays there while you read and goes when you leave the thread (CAR-959).
- A long collaboration thread opens on its newest 50 posts, with "Earlier posts" at the top to page back to the first post (CAR-986).
- Hovering your own agent in a collaboration reads "<agent> · your agent", not "You's agent" (CAR-986).
- A Decision asked of the whole collaboration says that your choice is posted in the thread for everyone and that the first answer settles it. A Decision asked of you alone still says the choice goes to the asker alone (CAR-985).
- `collab.conversation` with `collaboration` takes `mark_read` as a list of post `message_id`s, to mark exactly those posts read. `collab.wait` with `collaboration` takes `after`, a post's `seq`, so unread posts at or before it don't end the wait. `collab.read` takes `messages: false`, to take delivery updates and notices without handing out or acknowledging any message.

- CarHost's menu no longer goes grey when a scheduled update is found while another app is in front. Before, the update window opened behind that app and held every CarHost menu item disabled until someone found it. Now a scheduled update that would open in the background shows as an "Update Available…" item in the menu, and an update window that does open brings CarHost forward with it (car#4715).

- CarHost: a collaboration's "Work in this collaboration" panel shows only the lanes that hold a card, instead of "Nothing here." under each empty one, and VoiceOver names each lane ("Coming up, 2 cards") and each card by its title.

- The built-in model catalog adds Claude Opus 5.5 (`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`) and Claude Fable 5.2 (`anthropic/claude-fable-5-2`), with Anthropic's published context windows (1M), output limits (128K) and prices. The model menu now offers them. The rows carry no latency or benchmark figures until CAR measures them.
- A call to Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 or Fable / Mythos 5.1 and later that forces a tool (`tool_choice` `required`, `any` or a tool name) no longer fails with a 400. These models reject forced tool use, so CAR sends `auto` instead and logs a warning. CAR adds no fields to the tools, and the call keeps the thinking it asked for. A caller that wants schema-valid arguments sets `strict: true` on its own tool, at its top level or inside `function`. CAR now carries it through to Anthropic; before, the Anthropic tool conversion dropped it. Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Fable 5 and Haiku still get the forced choice.

- Dropping a folder on the Chat message box, or copying one in Finder and pasting it, now asks "Use <folder> for this chat?" with Use folder and Cancel, instead of refusing it or pasting its name. Use folder sets the chat's working folder exactly as Choose Folder does; Cancel changes nothing. Files dropped or pasted with the folder still attach.

- Chat's model menu now says under each model where it runs (On this Mac, Subscription, API key, Cloud, or External server for an Ollama or vLLM-MLX server) and whether it reads images. It says when no model on this Mac is installed, with a way to get one. When the chosen model can't read an attached image, Chat offers the connected models that can, as one-click "Switch to" buttons (car#2726).

- A dropped PDF with a page too large for Chat to read in full no longer sends that page's raw font codes as its text. In some fonts those codes were the wrong letters. Chat now stops the text before that page, marks it cut, and tells the agent to open the saved file for the rest (car#4623).

- Chat now includes a dropped PDF's text in the message, read by a separate helper process that is stopped if it runs too long or uses too much memory; a PDF that cannot be read that way is still sent as its saved file with a note.
