The sign-out happens whatever the outcome; a token that could not be revoked is printed as a warning by the CLI and added to the `warnings` array `auth.logout` already returns, and it stays valid at Parslee until it expires (car#5091).
- The meeting bot now speaks wire protocol 4, accepts `session.auth` only when the reply is an object with `ok: true`, and refuses a handshake that negotiates any other protocol version, naming both versions. At startup it stops waiting as soon as session setup fails, and otherwise waits for the connect allowance plus its setup timeout, so a slow but valid setup is no longer cut short (car#5094).

- `models.register` and `models.unregister` take effect in the running daemon at once. A registered model is usable by agents and `car do` with no restart (an on-device `local` or `mlx` row retires the warm inference worker so the next request reads it), an unregistered one stops being usable, and a row the removed one had displaced (a signed-catalog row, a cached provider-discovered row, or a model directory on disk) comes back. Both replies now carry `live` (whether the running registry changed) in place of the `note` that said a restart was required (car#5150).
- Turning Slack on with `messaging.config.set` while the daemon runs now starts both its inbound and outbound paths, so the next approval prompt reaches Slack without a restart. Enabling it without tokens returns an error that says the tokens are missing (car#5161).
- When an attached agent disconnects in the middle of a chat turn, the host now gets a terminal `agents.chat.event` `error` for that turn instead of silence (car#5159).
- A torn or interleaved row in the middle of heal's ledger no longer stops the daemon from booting. Heal skips the row, copies it aside as `heal/ledger.jsonl.corrupt-<timestamp>`, keeps the valid records, and runs no detection, repair or merge until the row is removed and the daemon restarts; `heal.status` names the file and line. The server guide now says the single-daemon lock is a local advisory lock that does not hold across hosts or on a share mounted without byte-range locks (car#3591).
- Reading Parslee sign-in state no longer writes a credential record that was not there. A read of a store holding neither a record nor pre-multi-login rows (a CLI whose daemon, on another home, answered "no record") returns signed-out without publishing one, and the purely local reads (`auth.status`-style snapshots, the auth generation and completion reads, account and organization listings) never write at all; pre-multi-login rows are still migrated when a credential is actually used or changed (car#5257).

- The dashboard's "Agents working now" no longer counts an actor whose only entries in the last hour are record writes (stored items, source health and the like); it counts the actors behind decisions, the way the morning standup does.

- The three `car-cli` dashboard bridge tests, which execute the generated bridge script under `node`, are now marked `#[ignore = "requires node on PATH"]`, so `cargo test -p car-cli` on a machine without node reports them as ignored instead of failing. CI runs them explicitly with node installed: the per-PR `test` job whenever `car-cli` is in scope, and the tag-time `test` job (car#5078).

- The dashboard's decision ledger no longer lets a slow read of an older day replace a newer one. When a refresh fails, the autonomy and standup numbers say "Showing the last good read; the refresh failed." instead of presenting old numbers as current. When a read of a different day fails, the feed clears the old day's rows instead of showing them under the new date, and says which day could not be read.

- A decision class may carry `standup_agents` (`actor` or `none`), set through `ledger.class.put` or `ledger.put`'s `class` and returned by `ledger.classes.list`. A class marked `actor`, such as a session's tool call, question asked, check-in or handoff record, puts its actor in the dashboard's "Agents working now" even though it is a record; absent means `none`, and older class records keep working. Bookkeeping records still count nowhere.

- A contract CarCoder derives itself now locks the grading helper files its checks run, such as a `checks/verdict.py` with no test-like name, by declaring them as `protected_paths`, so a builder can no longer edit a helper to weaken how its work is graded. A hand-written contract that declares no `protected_paths` keeps the old behaviour, and the daemon log now carries one warning naming each helper it treats as product (car#2190).

- **Dev-lane installs keep their macOS privacy grants.** A new `scripts/dev-sign.sh` signs local builds with one stable, self-signed "CAR Local Dev" identity in the login keychain, so a rebuilt `car-server` keeps the same designated requirement and its Documents, Calendar and other grants survive every reinstall. `car-lane.sh install-local` now refuses an ad-hoc or unsigned binary (exit 4, naming the signing command), stops the lane and waits for its server to exit before replacing anything, keeps the old binaries as `.prev`, restarts the lane in the launchd domain it was stopped from (a lane an older helper loaded in the gui domain would otherwise not come back), and rolls back to `.prev` when the new build does not start and `.prev` is stably signed (otherwise it leaves the lane stopped and says so). `restart` refuses an ad-hoc `car-server`, and `prove` reports which identity signed it. Before this, reinstalling renamed the running ad-hoc server to `car-server.prev`, macOS asked for a new Documents grant, and with the screen locked that unanswered prompt stalled every protected-folder access on the Mac for hours (car#5060).

- **The `regen-daemon-contract` merge driver keeps both sides' hand-written stub lines when regeneration fails (car#5117).** `index.d.ts`, `car_runtime.pyi` and `car_runtime/__init__.pyi` are only partly generated, yet a failed regeneration (a co-conflicting Rust file, a conflicted generator input, a declined params merge, a generator error or a cache timeout) left them holding "ours" alone, so the other side's hand-written lines were silently dropped and rerunning the generators never restored them. The driver now falls back to a three-way `git merge-file` of both sides before it exits 1, so the conflicted file carries both sides' lines with conflict markers where they collide, and the message says so. The fully generated wrappers and the params map keep "ours", because regeneration restores them whole.
- **`car-lane.sh promote` on the stable lane no longer reports success while the `car` and `car-mcp` on PATH cannot reach the new daemon (car#5132).** `prove` now runs `PATH-CLIENT-PROOF` on the stable lane: each PATH client's directory (after following symlinks, so `/usr/local/bin` resolves into CarHost.app) makes the same `fleet show` RPC as `DAEMON-PROOF`. A client that cannot handshake, such as an older CarHost.app after a wire protocol bump, fails the proof with the first error line and the pkg to install for the promoted version, and `promote` rolls back to the previous pair instead of printing `PROMOTION: … proven`. A client missing from PATH is noted, not failed. The search covers the caller's PATH plus `/usr/local/bin`; `CAR_LANE_CLIENT_PATH` overrides it.

- The worktree pool's direct-add guard now follows a HOME the command sets itself. After `export HOME=/p` or a bare `HOME=/p;`, a later `~/pool` is judged as `/p/pool` instead of the hook's own home, and a shell given `HOME=/p sh -c '...'` expands its script with `/p`. A prefix assignment does not change the `~` in its own command's words (`HOME=/p cd ~/pool` is the old home), but leading assignments run left to right, so in `HOME=/p GIT_DIR=~/pool/.git git ...` the `GIT_DIR` is `/p/pool/.git`, as in bash, zsh and sh. A `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_COMMON_DIR` that starts with `~` or `$HOME` is expanded when it is assigned, so a HOME set later does not move it; every word of one `export`, and every argument of `env`, is expanded with the home from before that command. An empty HOME, a value with an expansion the guard cannot read, or a HOME set through `declare`, `typeset`, `local` or `readonly` leaves the home unknown, so a `~` path is judged from every directory the command could run in; `unset HOME` and `env -u HOME` fall back to the inherited home, as bash and sh fall back to the passwd entry. `pushd +N` is read as a stack rotation, not a directory named `+N`. `unset GIT_DIR`, `env -u GIT_DIR` and `env -i` drop an inherited repository selector, so the add is judged from where it runs. A wrapper that runs a shell on a script (`env -i sh -c '...'`, `timeout 5 bash -c '...'`) now has that script judged, with the environment the wrapper hands it; before, such a script was not judged at all. `car codex` now knows that `--remote-auth-token-env` takes a value, so `car codex --remote-auth-token-env X exec ...` puts its `--add-dir` after `exec` (car#4740).

- A request another session or agent sent a person on the Lattice, outside any collaboration, is now one of the person's pending asks. `host.approvals { pending: true }` lists each one CarHost's questions list showed (every pending request without an approve/deny row) as `kind: "request"`, `source: "lattice"`, with the asker, the question, whom it asks and where it came from, oldest first with the other asks, and `collab.wait` counts it. `host.resolve_approval` answers it by its `lattice:` id with `text`, or with a review's `approve` or `deny`, through `lattice.respond`, so the asker receives the answer exactly as before and the request leaves both lists. As with every other ask, only the host client and the signed-in dashboard may answer it; any other session is refused `not_your_ask`.

- Directory reads that organization-bound agents prompt now share one allowance across every organization this CAR holds: at most two a minute, sign-ins included, and never when one would leave the operator fewer than four of the relay's six directory requests a minute. Before, the limit was per organization, so agents in six organizations could spend the whole budget and hold back the operator's next directory read for about a minute. A held-back read is served from the cached copy and tried again on a later call. (car#4872)

- A coder conversation that is still open and has streamed more than 2,000 events no longer loses its earliest messages for a client that reattaches with `coder.discuss.start { resume_id }` and subscribes from 0. When the replay buffer is full it now drops the streamed chunks of replies that have finished first, since each reply's whole text is its own event, and only then the oldest event. The chunks of a reply still streaming go last among chunks, so a client attaching mid-reply can rebuild it until its chunks plus every retained message and other event exceed the buffer; then its oldest chunks go, still before any message. Replayed `seq` numbers can now skip numbers in the middle, and CarHost's "outside the replay window" line can appear after such a skip (car#2154).

- `car doctor` now recognizes `host-model-setup.json`, the record the Windows setup window keeps of a running model download, instead of listing it as not written by this version of CAR. A test now reads the Windows tray's source for every name it writes into the CAR state root and fails when doctor does not know one, as it already did for CarHost on macOS (car#4198).

- Each CAR state root now has its own credentials in the OS secret store, so signing one CAR in or out, renewing its tokens, or reading its status never touches another on the same machine. Before this, a second CAR (`CAR_HOME=~/.car-dev`, such as the development lane) read and wrote the same keychain items as the default `~/.car`: a status check from the second CAR replaced the first one's Parslee sign-in with an empty record and signed it out (car#5244). The default `~/.car` keeps its existing item names, so nothing changes for it. Any other `CAR_HOME` stores its secrets under the service `car@<path>`, starts signed out, and needs its own sign-in and `car keys set`. A directory store already belongs to one home or one caller, so the headless store `<CAR_HOME>/secrets` and a `CAR_SECRETS_FILE_DIR` set for a debug build or test keep their file names.
- `car-lane.sh install-host` now gives the development lane's CarHost its own identity: bundle id `ai.parslee.car.<lane>`, the name `CAR <Lane>` and no Sparkle updates. After proving the download is the release's sealed Developer ID build, it re-signs it with the local "CAR Local Dev" identity. App-scoped tools such as `interceptor macos stream start --app "CAR Dev"` can now pick the lane's CarHost while the stable one runs. macOS asks for each privacy grant once for the lane copy, and later installs keep the grants (car#5236).

- CarHost: when an agent in a collaboration asks you a question, it now opens above the message box. Pick an option (or press its number), type your own answer, or dismiss it, and your answer is posted in the thread for everyone. With several questions open, "1 of 3" steps between them. The message box waits until you answer.

- CarHost builds again: adding a session that is in no collaboration no longer refers to the removed New collaboration sheet.

- CarHost: Collaborate is now a full pane in the main window. Your collaborations are listed on the left with their unread count and when each last had a post, invitations you haven't joined yet are listed first under Pending invitations, and the one you pick opens its thread on the right. Click Collaborate in the sidebar to open it; with no collaborations yet it offers New collaboration. People is now a list beside a conversation: everyone online is listed first, people who are offline are greyed out with "Offline, posts wait for them", and picking someone opens your private conversation with them on the right. Connection details and identity checks are under Connections and identity.

- Open the members list in a collaboration to see who's joined, who's online, and whose invitation is still pending. Invite also picks up sessions started since you last opened it.

- In CarHost, choose an organization, name the collaboration, and add an optional purpose. Invite people after the collaboration opens.

- A question already open in the drawer above the composer no longer also shows in the "Waiting on you" panel beside the thread.

- Agent routing (`declagents.route`, `declagents.route_split`, `discovery.resolve`, `discovery.route_compose`) and memory ranking, in the daemon and in `car reason`, `car skills` and `car dream` when they use the daemon, no longer download the embedding model silently. When it is not installed, routing is refused with an error naming the model and `car models pull <name>`, and memory ranking continues without embeddings and logs that hint once. The explicit `embed` method, `car embed` and the bindings' `embed` still download it on first use; the `embed` method takes a new optional `installed_only: true` that refuses instead (car#3771).
- When CAR raises a turn's output allowance after routing (the default widened to the model's output cap, an automatic thinking budget, or room for reasoning), the raised value no longer exceeds what the model's context window leaves after the input. Automatic thinking is turned on only when that room leaves at least 1,024 tokens beside the answer. Before, a prompt near the window could pass the routing fit check and then be sent a request larger than the window. The caller's own `max_tokens` is never reduced (car#3621).
- A turn larger than Apple FoundationModels' context window now fails with an error that gives the window and the measured turn size, for example "the request uses 10,262 tokens, larger than the 8,192-token context window of foundation-models". Before, the error gave only a fixed reason. The error kind stays `unsupported`. When FoundationModels is the preferred model or a lane default, a turn whose input does not fit its window is routed to another model, so unpinned `car do` turns, whose tool catalog alone is larger than the window, are no longer sent to it (car#4116).

- The Windows `env_clear` test-fixture guard now reads code only. A `readmit_os_env` or `"SystemRoot"` mentioned in a comment, a string or a raw string no longer counts as restoring the environment. An `.env_clear()` that appears only in a comment or string is no longer flagged (car#4634).

- The Windows `env_clear` guard accepts its `// env-clear-ok:` exemption only as a `//` comment. The same text inside a string or a block comment no longer exempts a clear that has no restore (car#4651).

- The Windows `env_clear()` test-fixture guard (`scripts/check-env-clear-windows.py`) now checks every site on its own: each clear needs a `SystemRoot` restore after it in its own block, so one correct fixture no longer excuses an unrestored one elsewhere in the same file (car#4262).

- The Windows `env_clear` test-fixture guard now reads a char literal with `_` in its Unicode escape (`'\u{4_1}'`). Before, such a literal threw its lexer out of step, so an unchecked `.env_clear()` after it was missed (car#4669).

- External-agent detection no longer reports a just-installed or just-updated CLI as `not_executable` when it catches the binary still open for writing (Linux `ETXTBSY`, "Text file busy"). The version probe now waits that out for up to its 2 s budget, and a file still busy after that leaves the CLI listed with no version instead of condemned (car#4757).

- A failed listing of the held Parslee logins now withdraws the boot login's devices as well as the other logins'. Before, it withdrew them only while the credential-authority hint was unknown, so a removal whose hint was never published, followed by a credential store that kept failing, left the removed boot login's devices trusted indefinitely. The next listing that shows the boot login still held restores them (car#2734).

- In My reports, a report that cannot send now has Export and Remove buttons, and Export from the confirmation saves the report exactly as it was saved on this Mac instead of collecting diagnostics again.

- Signing in again with an account My reports already lists now refreshes the list, so a report held for that account stops saying it cannot send.

- My reports now shows a date and the report's triage progress ("In triage", "Fix in progress", "Fixed & deployed") for reports filed from another Mac or no longer saved on this one, instead of "Saved on this Mac".

- `sync.fence_check`, the dispatch fence, now reads the Parslee lease coordinator on the blocking pool like the other relay calls. Before, it was the one relay-reaching sync call still made on an async worker (car#4666).

- **Python binding: the stderr log no longer prints credentials at `RUST_LOG=trace`.** The tracing subscriber the Python binding installs (car-ffi-common's `ensure_tracing_subscriber`) now applies the same credential redaction and transport-crate DEBUG ceiling as `car`, `car-server` and `car-mcp`, so WebSocket frames carrying daemon or Parslee tokens are not printed. The `warn` default and the leave-an-existing-subscriber-alone behaviour are unchanged. New `car_telemetry::try_init_stderr` is the entry point for embedded callers (car#5131).

- On a `core.autocrlf=true` checkout (the Git for Windows default), Foreman's captured patches are now line-level, so two subtasks that edit different lines of one file no longer report an integration conflict. The capture used to force `core.autocrlf=false`, which compared the stored LF blobs with the CRLF working files and made every hunk whole-file (car#5066).

- Foreman now keeps the deletion side of a rename that git reports in the worktree column of `git status` (for example after `git add -N`), and no longer panics on a non-ASCII rename source path.

- Added a TLA+ model of collaboration history replay
  (`car-rs/formal/collab-history`) and `scripts/verify-formal-collab-history.sh`.
  It checks every order, up to a small size, of invites, joins, adds, removes,
  leaves, rotates and one erasure checkpoint, as replayed by a full device, a
  partial device and a fresh device. Properties: devices agree and never stop
  on honest histories, a removed owner cannot restore its agent, an erased
  person is never listed, and epochs only grow. Broken controls prove each
  property can fail.

- A reasoning effort (`params.reasoning_effort`, a bare `budget_tokens`, or an agent's saved `inference.reasoning_effort`) now reaches Google, Vertex and Bedrock instead of being silently dropped (car#2663). Gemini 3 and later receive `generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel` (Gemini 3 Pro, which has no medium level, gets `high` for `medium`). Gemini 2.5 receives `thinkingBudget`: 2048 / 8192 / 16384 / 32768 tokens by effort, clamped to the model's range and kept below `maxOutputTokens`. Bedrock Claude receives the Anthropic thinking shape in `additionalModelRequestFields`: adaptive thinking with `output_config.effort` on 4.6 and later, and on older models a thinking budget kept below `maxTokens`. On Bedrock, temperature is left off while thinking is on, a forced `toolChoice` sends no thinking, and `reasoningContent` is parsed as thinking and replayed ahead of `toolUse` on the next turn. Gemini thought parts are never read as answer text. Because these models spend reasoning out of their output limit, the runner now adds the reasoning budget to `max_tokens` for them, capped at the model's catalog limit. Gemini models before 2.5 and Bedrock models that are not Claude still take no reasoning control. The new `car_inference::reasoning_control_applies(protocol, model)` reports which models take one.

- The built-in model catalog gains `openai/gpt-6-astra:latest` (OpenAI Responses API, `OPENAI_API_KEY`). Its id, limits, effort levels and prices come from OpenAI's model reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra): 922K maximum input tokens (recorded as the context length, the same convention as the `gpt-6.1-sol` row; the full window is 1.05M), 128K output tokens, text and image input, and $10 input / $1 cached input / $12.50 cache write / $50 output per million tokens. Prompts over 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the whole request; the row carries that as a `pricing_tiers` entry ($20 / $2 / $25 / $75), so a cost estimate without a per-request prompt size is flagged as an estimate. OpenAI offers effort levels low, medium, high, xhigh and max; CAR sends low through xhigh, because `max` has no `ReasoningEffort` variant. The row carries no `public_benchmarks` entry because CAR has no car-judged measurement for it yet. Installed CARs see the row once a signed catalog is published from `main` (car#4899).

- On Windows and Linux, `mail.mailboxes` through Microsoft Graph now names, in `reason`, each folder whose unread or total count Graph did not return as a number, instead of showing those folders as `0` with no note. A folder Graph reports as empty is still a plain `0` (car#4018).

- The daemon's built-in file tools under CAR's protected-file guard open the exact file the guard approved. The guard judges the path with every symlink resolved. The open walks that path one folder at a time without following a symlink, and the file (or, for a new file, its folder) must be the same file it was when the path was resolved. So a symlink, hard link or folder swapped in after the check is refused instead of followed to a credential or authority file. A file that already had a second name (a hard link) when the path was resolved opens like any other, and the guard judges it. A new file is created new, never opened if the name appeared after the check, and a folder the write creates is entered only while it is empty, so a folder with files in it renamed into its place is refused. Two writes creating files in the same missing folder at once can see the second one refused as changed once the first has put its file there; a retry succeeds. A write truncates only after these checks. A write through a symlink to a missing file still creates that file, and the guard judges the file. A folder that grants search but not listing is still walked. `grep_files` reads each file the same way and leaves out one that changed under it. The no-follow walk is Unix only (car#3451).

- `CAR_HARDWARE_PROFILE_JSON` can now state `available_ram_mb`, the memory free right now. When a profile sets it, local-model admission uses that value instead of reading the host. A profile that leaves it out still reads live memory. The spend-path WebSocket tests state a machine with this field, so their local speech rows no longer fall through to ElevenLabs on a busy host (car#4550).

- Test reliability: the headless `coder.start` reattach test waits `LOADED_WAIT` for the result, not a fixed 10 s, so a slow machine no longer fails it (car#4496).

- **Breaking: wire protocol 4.** `car selfheal` and `car heal` are now one feature, `car heal`, on by default with no configuration. It detects a defect in CAR's own runtime, fixes it with any capable model under a daily budget (`[heal] daily_budget_usd` in `~/.car/config.toml`, default 5 USD, charged to `car:heal`), has the fix judged by an independent review panel (at least two seats from vendors other than the coder's), queues it on the merge queue once every required check passes, and reports it healed only after a daemon build containing the merge runs three ticks and 24 hours without the failure coming back. A recurrence reopens the defect; three failed rounds escalate to a person. `[heal] enabled = false` is the one off switch. The `selfheal.status`, `selfheal.detections`, `selfheal.dismiss`, `selfheal.fix` and `selfheal.run` methods are removed and answer "method removed; use heal.*"; use `heal.status`, `heal.detections`, `heal.dismiss` and `heal.run`. `heal.status` now returns `state` (`off`, `blocked`, `idle`, `working`, `awaiting_merge`, `verifying` or `escalated`) and exactly one `reason`. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` and `PROTOCOL_VERSION_MIN` are both 4, so a client or daemon that speaks only protocol 3 no longer connects; upgrade the npm/PyPI package with the daemon. `heal.toml`, the `[selfheal]` config section and `CAR_SELFHEAL_INTERVAL_SECS` are no longer read (a present `heal.toml` or `[selfheal]` produces a config warning); move targets to `[[heal.target]]` / `[[heal.org]]`. State moves from `~/.car/selfheal/` to `~/.car/heal/`, migrated once at startup. Owner decision 2026-11-19. `car info --json` reports this as `heal` / `heal_unavailable_reason` (was `selfheal` / `selfheal_unavailable_reason`). The `[unattended]` model section is gone, and so are the `[selfheal]` keys `auto_fix`, `max_concurrent`, `max_per_day` and `max_rounds_per_key`, with no replacement: the daily budget and escalation after three failed rounds bound the work instead. `car selfheal fix` has no replacement, since heal repairs on its own; `car heal list`, `show` and `dismiss` replace `car selfheal list`, `show` and `dismiss`. A repair round fixes up to five related defects in the same crate in one session and one pull request, which lists every key it closes; it runs `scripts/ci-local.sh --preflight` (regenerating capabilities, daemon wrappers and the wire schema first when the change touches those surfaces) before pushing, leaves the crate's tests to the merge queue's required CI checks, records the contract before and after the fix in the pull-request body, brings a pull request that main overtook up to date and queues it again, confirms queueing through the merge queue itself, and verifies rather than recodes a defect a commit on main already names. When the merge queue drops a heal pull request, heal reads the failed tests of that merge-group run and of the other queue entries: a test outside the change's diff that also failed elsewhere is a flake, so the pull request is queued again once without a failed round and the test is recorded as its own `flaky_test` detection keyed by its name (a new `heal.detections` kind). With a CAR worktree pool in the source checkout, a repair session works in a leased slot that heal releases as soon as the round fails or its pull request merges or closes; `heal.status` work entries gain `slot` and `issue`. Every test a fix adds or changes is run with the fix's source reverted and must fail there ("test does not catch the defect" otherwise), and with the fix, and both outputs go in the pull request body. With `scripts/ci-scoped-test.sh` in the repository, the touched crates' tests run on CI for the pushed branch before auto-merge is armed; a red run closes the pull request. The replay contract now runs one local cargo invocation. A repair round never sends a diff or pull request body the store-aware redactor would change, and the coder's shell, the contract checks and heal's tool check share one PATH, the login shell's merged in. A defect with no runtime contract escalates to a person through a redacted issue labelled `needs-human` (created when missing; `[heal] human_label` overrides) and assigned to `[heal] escalate_to` or the `gh` login, and `heal.status` names the issue. `enabled = false` turns detection off too, and its status reason says so. On a repository without a merge queue, heal arms plain auto-merge (`--squash`) only when main requires status checks, and otherwise refuses. A local-only round names a local panel seat as the coder session's independent auditor, so it can deliver. Review fixes: nothing a repair round produced is pushed before it passes the redactor (refreshed branches included), and the watch-it-fail run is local and never pushes; the preflight, the generators and local test runs are sandboxed like contract checks, and `scripts/` and `.github/` are protected paths; a pool slot is cleaned only while heal still holds its lease; a round cut off mid-way is retried and its slot freed; a failure after delivery closes the pull request and the retry uses a fresh `-r<round>` branch, while forge errors only wait; one tick runs per host (`<CAR_HOME>/heal/tick.lock`), an observe-only daemon never starts heal, and a daemon without its own spend meter is blocked rather than reporting 0 spent; a refreshed branch reruns the watch and scoped CI before auto-merge is re-armed; scoped CI that cannot run refuses auto-merge; only queue entries without heal's commit count as flake siblings; a test that does not compile without the fix is reported as not shown; a defect counts as fixed on main only through a `Heal-Key:` trailer on a non-revert commit with its checks passing; a batch member already passing on main is dropped and reported `already_passing`; seed fields are restricted to a safe charset; the hand-in claims are migrated to `<CAR_HOME>/heal/`. A delivered pull request no longer holds a worktree-pool slot (a refresh leases its own); a round cut off three times in a row escalates with "interrupted 3 times"; auto-merge also requires that the session ended with the runtime's own contract. Second review fixes: heal's scripts and tests run with the contract checks' environment scrub (no provider key or `GH_TOKEN`), a private credential-free Cargo home, and no network for anything that builds the model's code; heal is blocked with its own reason where the OS sandbox is unavailable, and always on Windows; auto-merge is turned off before a refreshed head is pushed and re-armed only after that head passes its checks; a CI run that never happened, a busy machine, and a failed fetch or push are waits, never failed rounds or closed pull requests; a pull request is recorded the moment it opens, so an interrupted round resumes it, and an open one on any of the occurrence's branches is attached to; a close that fails is tried again; every comparison uses the round's base commit, not a moving `origin/main`; the coder's own commits and their messages are read and redacted like the rest of the change, and a commit names `$CAR_HOME` rather than the state root's path; the tick lock records the holder's start time and appears atomically; a daemon on its own `CAR_HOME` discovers no checkout unless `[heal] source_checkout` names one; a conflict in a hand-maintained stub, and a pull request a person closed, go to a person without a new pull request; a repository without a merge queue is decided by the pull request's own checks; a refresh slot's local branch is deleted. Third review: every repository step heal runs is offline, with a Cargo home of its own per call, and dependencies are fetched only on a pristine checkout of the base commit; a change to what a step runs or configures, or to a dependency, runs nothing (a dependency change goes to a person); every request to a remote model passes the outward redactor first, and a refused one sends the defect to local models; every process heal starts is bounded and stopped with its process group, and the forge client is reached only through a bounded adapter; every non-terminal state has an age, and one held past 24 hours (or three deferred deliveries) is told to a person with an issue; a deferred delivery resumes from the approved change without paying the coder again; auto-merge is armed only on the head heal pushed whose change is the reviewed one (another's push goes to a person); the preflight's offline mode (`CAR_CI_LOCAL_OFFLINE=1`) skips cargo-deny with its reason; a filesystem without hard links blocks heal with that reason.

- Heal never merges over a person's stop. `Parslee-ai/car` requires no review, so before heal arms auto-merge, and on every tick while a heal pull request is armed, it reads the pull request's labels and reviews. A `needs-human`, `do-not-merge` or `hold` label, or a request for changes that the reviewer has not since replaced with an approval or had dismissed (a later comment-only review does not lift it), keeps heal from arming. If the pull request is already queued, heal takes it out of the merge queue, turns auto-merge off and escalates to a person. Heal never re-arms that pull request. Closing the pull request still declines it outright.

- The model upgrade check and adding a model from a Hugging Face repo id now honor `HF_ENDPOINT`, as model downloads already did, so a mirror or private hub works for all three.

- The policy hook can run the credential inspector CAR's own assistant runs. A policy file with `inspectors = ["credential_access"]` makes `car policy-check-hook` (and the `policy_check` MCP tool) deny calls that read SSH keys or cloud credentials, use a keychain tool, dump the environment or expand a credential variable. That covers Claude Code `Bash`, `Read`, `Write` and `Edit` calls, and CAR's own `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file` and `grep_files` named directly. Credential paths match in any letter case (`~/.SSH` is `~/.ssh` on macOS). A file tool's path is also judged with its symlinks resolved, relative to the call's working directory, through missing folders and links to missing files; a path whose destination cannot be worked out is denied, and a `~`, `$` or `%` path is also judged as the literal name under the working directory. The inspector is off unless named, and an unknown name fails to load. The inspector and the shell segmenter it reads commands with now live in `car-policy`, one definition shared with the assistant, which gets the same letter-case and resolved-path matching (car#3410).

- The `host.events` reference now matches the shipped wire shape: the reply is a bare `HostEvent[]`, newest first, not `{ events: HostEvent[] }`. The daemon is unchanged. A client written to the old docs read `result.events`, got nothing back, and treated every reply as "no events" (car#5051).

- The car-server `host_restart` tests that occupy a reserved port now hold it from the moment it is reserved, through a new `reserved_ports::held` test helper, so another socket can no longer take it before the test's own bind and fail the test with `AddrInUse`. Test-only; no behaviour changes. Fixes #5139.

- Tests: the daemon-restart approval tests start their daemon again on a fresh port pair when another program on the machine took its WebSocket or dashboard port before the daemon bound it, instead of failing the run (car#4926). Any other startup failure still fails with the daemon's own error.

- An OS certificate store holding no readable certificate no longer crashes CAR's A2A client, A2A push delivery, the Slack channel, the voice speakers and ElevenLabs speech-to-text, connector OAuth, or fleet subtask dispatch, and no longer fails every web search and fetch. Each of these HTTP clients now falls back to the built-in public CA roots and logs one warning naming the client; calls to endpoints signed by a private or corporate CA fail until the store is repaired. Rust embedders get the same fallback from `car_inference::tls_client::build_client_with_degradation` (car#3694).

- Claude Code sessions with the CAR plugin are woken when a colleague's message arrives while they sit idle at their prompt. A background `Stop` hook (`car peer-inbox-wait`, Claude Code's `asyncRewake`) starts a turn when the session's count of waiting peer messages or private messages rises. It shows Claude only the counts, reads one local file, and keeps whatever the person had half typed. Part of car#4263; `car codex` sessions are not covered yet.

- Idle Claude Code and Codex sessions in a collaboration are woken by CAR, with no watcher of their own (CAR-982). The session's collaboration server wakes it within seconds for a question asked of it, an @-mention of it, a reply to its own post, private mail and peer mail, and every 15 minutes while other unread posts wait; never twice for the same mail, never for its own post, and a reply chain between two sessions stops at the car-peers hop limit. The wake line names the collaboration's title and what waits, never a message. Claude Code is woken through the plugin's `car peer-inbox-wait` hook, which now follows the server's decision instead of raw counts; `car codex` sessions through `thread/queue/add` sent straight to the session's own app server: `car codex` now starts `codex app-server --listen unix://<run>/<id>.codex.sock` with the session's configuration (hooks, MCP servers, brief, trust, `--add-dir` as writable roots) and attaches the TUI with `--remote`, so a wake starts a turn at once instead of waiting up to 10 s for Codex's poll of its shared queue. Non-interactive modes (`car codex exec`, ...) and `CAR_WAKE=0` keep Codex's embedded server, with wake off. `CAR_WAKE=0` turns it off for a session.
- `collab.wait` with `by_sender` lists two more kinds of need for a collaboration: `reply`, an unread post replying to one the caller wrote, with `depth`, the length of its reply chain; and, for a session, a `mention` of the session's own name.

- `infer` and `infer_stream` now refuse `video_path` and `audio_path` content blocks from a session bound to a supervised agent, on every platform. (A worker session was already refused them by the worker gate; `infer` now checks workers too, as a second layer.) Such a block names a file on the daemon's host, and the daemon stat'd it for the token estimate, whose size changed how much of the prompt was truncated. That let an agent walled away from the file learn whether it exists and how large it is. The refusal comes before an inference id is assigned or anything is dispatched or billed. Its message is fixed, never names the path, and is the same whether the file exists or not. Agents send `video_base64`/`audio_base64` or a URL instead. Host, operator and CLI sessions are unchanged (car#3305).

- `infer`, `infer_stream` and `classify` take an optional `attempt_id`, an opaque id the caller mints (1 to 128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`). The daemon writes it on the spend-ledger row of every call the request makes, and `events.query { agent, data_matches: { attempt_id } }` returns exactly that request's bills, whatever order parallel calls settled in and however often it is read. The reply then carries `attempt_id`, `call_ids` (the calls it was billed for), `pending_call_ids` (calls whose bill is not written yet) and `settled` (false while work the request started, such as a backend after a deadline or cancel, could still add a bill). A failure keeps its code, message and `data.kind`, and adds the same fields with `billed` and `dispatched`; `dispatched: false` means nothing reached a provider and nothing was billed, and `null` means not known yet. Requests without `attempt_id` are unchanged. NAPI `infer`/`inferTracked`/`classify` and Python `infer`/`infer_tracked`/`classify` take a trailing `attemptId` and a keyword-only `attempt_id` (car#4797).

- `car models remove` now removes an adopted model whose folder was deleted or moved. CAR manages an adopted model as a link to its folder, and once the folder was gone, removing the model failed with a bare "not found" error. Removal now checks the link against the adoption receipt even though nothing is at its end, including when the folder's parent was deleted too, and deletes only the link. A link pointed at any other path is still refused. `car models pull` on an adopted model now also checks the folder behind the link, so an unreadable `config.json` there is reported as damage, with the remove-then-pull steps, instead of a completed pull that fails at load (car#4980).
- Claude on Bedrock before 3.7 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Haiku and older) no longer receives a `thinking` field, which those models reject. They have no extended thinking. A reasoning effort or `budget_tokens` asked of one of them is now dropped, the request keeps its `temperature`, and a saved declarative-agent effort is reported as having no effect there. Claude 3.7 and later on Bedrock are unchanged (car#4985).
- `fleet.composite` with `include_remote: false` (`car fleet show --local`) no longer hangs behind a slow mlx-vlm availability probe. The probe's `mlx_vlm.generate --help` and dependency check now share a 10-second budget, and a probe past it is killed and reaped. mlx-vlm then counts as unavailable, with a message saying the probe timed out rather than that mlx-vlm is not installed. While one caller refreshes the cached answer, other callers get the last answer (or "unavailable" before the first one) instead of waiting. The inventory lists models on a blocking thread (car#4945).

- A declarative agent saved with a reasoning effort on a model that takes no reasoning control CAR sends (a Gemini model before 2.5, a Bedrock model that is not Claude, Claude on Bedrock before 3.7, a non-reasoning OpenAI model, the `parslee/*` lanes, on-device models other than gpt-oss on vllm-mlx) is no longer shown as if the effort applied. `declagents.get`, `declagents.list` and `agents.list` add response-only `inference.reasoning_effort_applies` (never saved to `declagents.json` or the fingerprint), and CarHost shows "Reasoning effort: High (no effect on this model)" in the Agent Builder and in Chat's pinned-model help. `car_inference::saved_reasoning_effort_applies` answers the same question for a catalog row (car#2663, car#1989).
- Model downloads on Windows check free space before they start. `GetDiskFreeSpaceExW` now reads the volume's free and total space, so a pull that won't fit is refused with the same "not enough disk space" message Unix gives, and the engine's disk figures are present on Windows (car#5157).
- On Windows, cleaning up an interrupted model install compares each file's and its folder's NTFS file identity (volume serial number and file index), read without following links, at the moment it deletes. A same-size replacement with a copied last-write and creation time, or a folder re-created with the old creation time, is no longer deleted as CAR's; when the identity cannot be read the delete is refused (car#4721).
- whisper.cpp transcription keeps a loaded model resident and reuses it for later requests to the same model, instead of reloading it from disk on every call. It is held in the engine's model cache under the shared model budget, charged once as resident and released by the same idle eviction as other cached local models (`CAR_INFERENCE_MODEL_IDLE_SECS`), and a model removal evicts it (car#5156).

- `classify` on a TypeSafe (Jev) row now tells its failures apart by `error.data.kind`, on the same `-32603` code: a TypeSafe 5xx, 408, 425, timeout or transport failure is `transient` and a 429 is `rate_limited`, both safe to retry; a rejected stored key is `auth_rejected` (401/403) or `quota_exhausted` (402), which names `car keys set <key>`; a missing key stays `auth_rejected` and an unknown row stays `model_not_found`. Before, every TypeSafe HTTP failure was `failed`, so a caller could not tell a Jev outage from a configuration fault without reading the model list (car#4555).
- A Parslee 401, 402 or 403 on a managed chat, stream or System One request, and a 403 from the Parslee org lookup, is now an account failure (`auth_rejected` or `quota_exhausted`) and is no longer booked against the model's health or counted by its circuit breaker. That includes a 403 when token renewal is unavailable and a retry rejected again after a successful renewal. A 401 still tells you to run `car auth login`; a 403 still says that signing in again does not change access (car#3936).

- A failed inference says what kind of failure it was, not only in prose. The daemon's `infer` error carries `data.kind` (`rate_limited`, `auth_rejected`, `quota_exhausted`, `model_not_found`, `timeout`, `transient` and the rest, with `data.status` when the provider sent one). Node's `inferTrackedWithRequest` rejects with `.code` and `.data`; Python's `infer_tracked_with_request` still raises `RuntimeError` with the same text, now with `code`, `data` and `spend_refused` attributes. Both packaged agent loops put `{ kind, code, status? }` on `outcome.error` (`unknown` when the failure carried no kind) and on the failed step's evidence, and `runs.complete` stores it, so a caller can retry a rate limit and stop on a rejected key without parsing the message (car#1695). The packaged loops' failure text changes with it: a failed inference's summary reads `inference failed: <message>` with stop-reason evidence `infer_tracked error` (Python's said `RuntimeError: <message>` with `exception`), and Node's rejection message is the daemon's message without the `<code> ` prefix, which is now `.code`.

- When a remote model's stream setup fails, the local last resort now reads free memory through the local admission coordinator's live probe, the same reading admission makes when that model is dispatched, instead of probing the host separately. The filter and admission can no longer disagree about whether an installed local model fits right now (car#4549).
- The maintenance pass's curated auto-upgrade now judges whether the replacement fits on the hardware the pass was given rather than re-detecting this machine, so a stated hardware profile decides the verdict (car#4548).

- A slow mlx-vlm availability probe or account discovery no longer holds up requests. The routing snapshot built for a request refreshed mlx-vlm availability inline on an async worker whenever the cached answer was stale, so a slow `mlx_vlm.generate --help` parked that worker for up to the probe's 10 s budget, and every request scheduled on it waited, including `infer` calls pinned to a remote model. The probe now runs on its own thread (`car-mlx-vlm-probe`), and routing uses the last answer while it runs. The engine starts the first probe when it is built. Until that probe answers, adaptive routing does not pick an mlx-vlm model; a request that names one is still dispatched and checks the runtime itself. `accounts.list` and `accounts.open` now run on the blocking pool, and the macOS `swift -e` account script, which had no deadline, now has a 60 s budget: past it, the script and the `swift-frontend` it started are killed, and `accounts.list` returns a `backend` error. Probes also no longer leave reader threads behind. A probe child now leads its own process group, and its output is read without blocking on the calling thread. When the child exits and a background process it started still holds the output open, that process group is killed after a short grace (car#5042, car#5021).

- Lab branch checks no longer end a clean check with exit 124 when launchd starts one of macOS's own per-user agents (`distnoted`, `cfprefsd`, `lsd`, `secd`, `trustd`) again as `car-check` after the final sweep. Only a process at that exact path whose parent is launchd is passed over; anything else the check user still runs ends the check with 124 as before (car#4856). The check user's folder from before car#4539 is now removed by the first clean check after an upgrade and by `clean --all`, unless `CAR_REMOTE_CHECK_USER_BASE` points at it (car#4889).

- Branch checks can run on the release lab Mac. `scripts/lab/remote-check.sh start <branch> '<command>'` fetches a pushed branch on the lab, queues it first come, first served (one at a time: one check already peaks near 11 GB of the lab's 16), and runs the command detached as a separate standard account, `car-check`, with its own Rust toolchain and cargo target. That account cannot write the Homebrew tools the release account runs, enter other home folders, or open forwarded SSH agent sockets, and every process it has is ended before the next check starts, so nothing a check starts outlives it. The account is a one-time setup on the lab, and admission refuses until it exists and is walled off; `status`, `wait`, `fetch` and `clean` follow it. Admission reads the clock, the release account and free disk before anything is written, and a release-busy refusal names when the release started and when to retry; every phase after it runs under one guard that stops it within seconds of the 01:00 to 08:00 window around the nightly, a release build, or the disk floor, and removes what the run wrote. It leaves the release account, launchd jobs, schedule and toolchain pins alone. See "Branch checks on the lab" in `docs/release-lab.md`.

- Release lab: every run record now stores `source_revision`, the full SHA of the lab checkout's `HEAD` when the run started (or `unknown`), so a run that fails in its plan step still says which code it ran. `car-release status` prints `source revision:` and `planned commit:` at the end of each run's Status facts group, and `car-release log` prints `Source revision:` and `Planned commit:` after its `Run:` line. `commit` keeps meaning the planned release commit (car#5071).

- The release lab now updates its own scripts to `main` at the start of every nightly and promotion, before it takes the run lock, so a merged lab fix takes effect without anyone running `car-release update main`. A failed update or health check restores the previous commit, prints `WARN self-update failed at <step>; continuing on <commit>` and starts the release on the previous scripts; a held lock skips the update with a warning. Each run's log and record name the scripts commit it used and the update run (car#4717). The 03:30 scheduled nightly waits for an operator's update run to release the lock and then starts, as it already did for a promotion, instead of logging that a run is active and skipping the day.

- Repeated `car-release status` reads no longer each run the promotion preflight. Before, every read ran it live for each recent nightly, and each run made about ten GitHub reads. On 2026-11-12 status took 260-285 s, and most of Link's reads timed out. Status now keeps each nightly's `promotable:` answer for up to `CAR_LAB_STATUS_PROMOTABLE_TTL` seconds (default 600; `0` checks live every time; anything other than a whole number up to 999999 falls back to 600). A reused line ends `(checked <N>s ago)`. An answer is reused only while the repository, the UTC day, the run records, the active run and the nightly's release assets are unchanged, so a lane attaching or a run starting, stepping or finishing makes the next read live. The first read after the window or after such a change still runs the preflight live. An answer from a failed or timed-out GitHub read is printed but never reused. `car-release promote` still runs the preflight live (car#4398).

- On Linux, when the kernel cannot confine an agent, its refusal now points to a check that works inside a container: the daemon log's start line, `agent wall: Landlock ABI <n>` or `agent wall: no Landlock (...)`. It used to say to read `/sys/kernel/security/lsm`, which most containers do not mount, so an operator could conclude Landlock was missing when it was on. That file is now named only as a fallback for hosts that mount securityfs. The advice also follows what CAR measured: a kernel whose Landlock ABI is below 3 is told to upgrade the kernel or host image, a kernel with Landlock switched off at boot is told about the `lsm=` boot parameter, and a kernel or seccomp profile without the Landlock syscall is told to ask the provider (car#3362).

- **Stable lane `promote` installs again: it no longer depends on the Daily Continuity newsroom.** `car-lane.sh promote` had refused every install with `NEWSROOM-PROOF: refused before install`, because it required the newsroom's daemon-identity record to name the candidate binary before the swap, and that record can only name the binary already installed. `promote` and `prove` no longer read the newsroom record at all: the precheck, the post-restart `NEWSROOM-PROOF` and the `LANE_NEWSROOM_RECORD` setting are gone. The signature checks, the nightly build check, `DAEMON-PROOF`, the calendar proof, the running-agent proof and rollback are unchanged (car#4707).

- **`car-lane.sh install-release` and `promote` install a published nightly.** A tag such as `v0.65.0-nightly.20261116.7` used to be refused with `SIGNATURE-PROOF: refused release … (version mismatch …)`, because a nightly's binaries report the base version (`car 0.65.0 (build 20261116-ce83338)`), never the tag. The lane now reads the tag's commit and build ID from its public car-releases release record, with an anonymous request that sends no credential and never touches the Keychain, and installs only when `car`, `car-server` and `car-mcp` each report the base version with that commit's build stamp. A nightly from another commit, without a stamp, with another base version, or with no readable record is refused with exit 4 and nothing installed. The `car-mcp` repair for a seed that has none now works for a nightly too. Stable releases, the signature checks, the proofs and rollback are unchanged.

- `scripts/car-lane.sh` now runs `install-plist`, `install-local`, `install-release`, `promote`, `restart` and `stop` one at a time per lane. A `restart` from another shell while `install-local` had the lane stopped could start the old server, which the install then renamed to `.prev` while it ran (car#5073). The second verb now prints `waiting: <verb> pid <n> holds <lane>` and runs after the first finishes, or exits 1 after 300 seconds. A lock left by a holder that is no longer running is taken over.
- The lab's remote check no longer starts beside an earlier runner's check that took the slot lock just after the check's turn came. It logs `== waiting: legacy-check: ...` once and waits, and `status` keeps showing it queued (car#5038).
- `scripts/test-release-detach.sh` waits for the detached bootstrap's own marker or exit, not a 60-second wall clock. A bootstrap that exits early now gives one failure with the tail of its log, instead of three unexplained ones. A piped run also no longer holds the pipe open for 30 seconds after the test ends (car#5034).

- **`car-lane.sh install-host <version>` installs a published release's CarHost.app on a development lane (car#5233).** It unpacks the release's `CAR-Host-darwin-arm64.zip` (never the `.pkg`) into the lane's folder, checks the whole bundle's Developer ID seal, its version and its bundled `car-server`'s version and nightly build ID, and opens it with the lane's `CAR_HOME` and port, so a nightly can be walked in CarHost beside the stable app without promoting it. It refuses the stable lane and any destination under `/Applications`.
- **`car-lane.sh install-release` stops a running lane before it swaps binaries, then starts it again (car#5060).** It used to rename a running `car-server`'s executable, which can raise the macOS Documents prompt that stalls a locked Mac. A lane that was not running stays stopped; `promote` restarts as before. The nightly version gate reported in car#5234 was already fixed by car#4692; the refusal came from an older copy of the script.

- Removing the last project from `car board reconcile` now closes the incident it left open on its board. Before, the reconciler stopped as soon as no project was watched, so that incident stayed open forever.

- **Tests:** the two `car-inference` late-cost unit tests that still built a `reqwest::Client::new()` now use a client that does not load the native root store, so they no longer panic on a host whose certificate store is empty (car#3694).

- **Lattice org calls on a CAR signed into several orgs use your default organization.** `lattice.org.*`, `lattice.directory` and org connection offers that name no `org` now pick the same organization `car auth resolve` and collaboration calls do: your default organization, else the signed-in login's. They refuse only when neither names an org this CAR serves, and the refusal says how to set a default (`car auth default-org <organization>`), instead of "name one with `org`" (car#5231).

- A lattice node joined through `car-mcp --local-peers` stops being listed as available once its forwarder has been silent for 15 minutes, so a killed `codex exec` no longer leaves a node that mail can never reach. The session's next request brings it back. A running forwarder pings once a minute, so a session that is only idle stays listed and keeps its claims. A client connected straight to the daemon's `/mcp` (Cursor, Codex by URL, Claude Desktop through mcp-remote) and a CAR Coder run's node stay listed as before.

- A session the person started with `car claude` or `car codex` no longer counts mail held for the person that another such session may take as its own. `lattice.inbox` still returns that mail to whichever launcher session reads first, but counts it only in `held_for_person`, not in the session's `unread`, and the collaboration MCP server's idle wake no longer announces it. So the waiting-message count the prompt hook reads, idle wake and `inbox_waiting` no longer announce a stored message that a sibling session then takes, which left `peer_inbox` empty (car#4968). Mail that names the session, or a session whose place it took, still counts as its own.

- **A walled Linux agent's start now records the Landlock wall it enforced (car#3277).** `agents.list` rows carry `wall?: {kernel_abi, enforced_abi, signal_scope, abstract_socket_scope, pathname_socket_right, gaps}` while a walled run is up, taken from the ruleset the start built rather than a second kernel query. The same record is written to the agent's start record and to each worker's `worker-starts.jsonl` row, and the daemon logs it per agent and run. Below Landlock ABI 6, `gaps` and the daemon's `agent wall:` start line also say that a process which leaves with `setsid` before the agent kills its init survives stop (car#3364, still open). The field is absent off Linux, for an unwalled or adopted process, and after a refused start. The hostile-probe baseline (`isolation_probe`) prints the probe agent's own `wall` beside the door table and fails on Linux when it is missing. For Rust callers, `car_registry::workers::record_worker_start` takes the record as a new fifth argument.
- **The walled-agent default-deny now records its `host.resolve_approval` refusals in the host event ledger (car#3607).** It covers every walled agent except a worker, whose session the worker gate answers first: on Linux every other supervised agent, and on a Mac an orchestrator. It emits `approval.resolve_refused` with `reason: "walled_agent_default_deny"`, attributed to the refused agent and carrying the caller's `approval_id` and `resolution` (strings only, cut to 256 characters). No row is looked up. The refusal's error code and message are unchanged.
- **Docs: Landlock ABI 6 starts at Linux 6.12, not 6.10 (car#3324).** The orchestrator-workers design now names the below-ABI-6 signal and pid-observation exposure as exception E4 to I5, so the "complete set" of exceptions is E1 to E3, plus E4 on hosts below ABI 6.

- Each nightly now runs its published Linux files on Linux. A new `smoke-linux-archives` release job runs `car --version` and `car-server --version` from `car-linux-x64-gnu.tar.gz` and `car-linux-arm64-gnu.tar.gz`, and the standalone `car-server-linux-*` binaries, in Ubuntu 24.04 containers. It also loads `car-runtime.linux-arm64-gnu.node` in a Debian 13 container. Every reported version must match the tag and its build ID (car#3862).
  - **Emulated arm64.** The arm64 checks run under QEMU on an x64 runner, not on arm hardware.
  - **Gates nothing yet.** A failure turns the nightly's run red but does not hold back publication, catch-up or promotion.
  - **What is still untested.** `DISTRIBUTION.md` now lists which distributions each nightly install test runs, and which Linux files no test runs. `scripts/smoke-linux-archives.sh <tag>` runs the same checks locally with Docker.

- On Linux, an untrusted coder session's model shell and its contract and baseline checks can no longer read or write the operator's credential stores (`~/.aws`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.config`, `~/.docker`, `~/.gnupg` and the rest of the list the independent verifier's shell is already denied), and they lose `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, as on macOS since car#2593. Each store is covered by one mount, however many entries it holds, and the session worktree and git's XDG configuration are bound back beneath it, so git and a repository kept under `~/.config` keep working while `git/credentials` stays denied. A symlinked store entry is denied at its target, and a command is refused while a file in `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker` or `~/.azure` has a second hard link. A denied file reached by two spellings (a GNU stow `~/.config/git -> ~/dotfiles/git`) is now bound once, which fixes sandbox setup failing with exit 125. Trusted sessions keep their access (car#3690, car#4223).
- Linux now has an end-to-end test of the coder check refusing to run while a protected file has a second hard link (car#4082).
- On Linux, the verifier's `run_check` no longer gets the shared `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` as write roots. A check writes its private `$TMPDIR`, where here-documents and a bare `mktemp` land, and a write to a fixed `/tmp` name fails (car#4210).

- Linux: CarCoder now checks whether its sandbox can start for each sandbox policy separately, instead of once for each network setting. Before, the first policy checked in a process decided for every later policy with the same network setting. One policy that could not set up made every other policy unavailable, and one that could made a failing policy look available. Only a policy that started is remembered, up to 1024, so a failed policy is checked again on its next use (car#2850).
- Linux: a network-denied CarCoder command no longer runs without localhost when loopback cannot be enabled. Before, a failed `ip link set lo up` was ignored. On a host without iproute2, a check that talks to a service it started on localhost then failed as if the code were broken. Now the sandbox stops before the command runs, with exit 125 and `car: secret sandbox setup failed: loopback could not be enabled (iproute2 'ip' missing or failed)`. A contract check that ends this way, or with any other sandbox setup failure, is reported as an infrastructure failure: the verifier's round ends as Infrastructure rather than reading it as a failing check. Install iproute2 to fix it (car#2025).

- Move non-required Mac-runnable workflow checks into local CI, including public documentation, Apple builds, a local daemon-client reachability check and published release verification.
- Raise the local reachability check's open-file soft limit up to 65,536 within its subshell to avoid macOS's default 256-descriptor limit.
- Keep the uncached Linux clean-build job hosted; refresh local CI refs before comparison and release checks, and bound Python wrapper retries.
- Preserve full clone history when local CI refreshes main, and refuse release-lab suites when the shared clone is shallow.
- Preserve differing local tags during release checks and name the repair command when shared clone history is shallow.

- A Mac whose HostName is unset now names itself by its LocalHostName (`scutil --get LocalHostName`) instead of the DHCP or router-assigned name such as `Mac.localdomain`. That name is used for the mDNS advertisement, the endpoint published on the synced oplog, the work board's device field and `car fleet show`. Two Macs on one network no longer share a name, and a Mac keeps its name when it changes networks. A Mac with HostName set keeps its current name, and other platforms are unchanged. On upgrade an affected Mac's name changes once: update any saved `<node>@<old-name>` address, such as a `notify` recipient in `heal.toml`. Matching a device that moved to a new address by its identity rather than its URL is still tracked in car#4918 (car#4866).

- `mail.send` (and `car mail send`, the assistant's `mail_send` tool and the Node/Python `mail_send` bindings) on the Mail.app backend no longer reports `sent: true` just because Mail accepted the message. After the send, CAR looks for a new message with the same subject and To addresses in Mail's Outbox, or in the sending account's Sent mailbox through Mail's Envelope Index (Full Disk Access), looking again 5 s after each look ends, for 120 s. If one turns up, the result is `sent: true` as before. If the last look read Sent and the message wasn't there, the result is `sent: false` with a `send_unconfirmed:` reason saying it may still go out and to check Outbox and Sent before sending it again; the assistant's `mail_send` fails with that reason. If Sent couldn't be read, the result stays `sent: true` with a `send_unverified:` reason, so a send that only lacked confirmation isn't sent twice; when the Envelope Index can't be read before the send, CAR looks only at the Outbox, for 15 s. A confirmed send returns once the message shows up (within 24 s on the measured account); the worst case is about 3 minutes, and the daemon client now waits 300 s for `mail.send` (the approval prompt plus the send) and the daemon gives it at least 210 s whatever `CAR_HANDLER_TIMEOUT` says. Drafts and sends Mail refuses are unchanged (car#4582).

- `mail.send` on Mail.app (and `car mail send`, the assistant's `mail_send` tool and the Node/Python `mail_send` bindings) no longer reports `sent: true` for a send CAR could not check, for example when the daemon has no Full Disk Access, the Envelope Index stays locked, or Mail does not say which account sent it. Such a send is now `sent: false` with its `send_unverified:` reason, and the result carries a new `delivery` field, `"confirmed"`, `"unconfirmed"` or `"unverified"`, so a caller can tell a send to check from a confirmed one without reading the reason text. The assistant's `mail_send` call now fails on an unverified send, and the reason tells it to check Mail's Sent before sending again (car#4857, car#4842).

- The daemon-native MCP `peer_message` tool now resolves `to` the same way `agents.message` does. From an org-bound MCP session, a session's stable name, an earlier holder's id, a seat key and `inbox:<org>` used to fail with "no peer named …"; they now reach the same place as through `agents.message`, and mail for an ended session is stored for the session that takes its place with `session_ended: true`. A bare name that is both a peer's address and another session's stable name is now refused on this path too, as `agents.message` refuses it (car#4912).

- MCP `skill_list`, `resources/list`, `resources/read` and `completion/complete` take an optional `tenant_id`. On a memory bank shared by several tenants, a scoped caller now sees only its own tenant's skills and facts. Another tenant's fact or skill URI is not listed and reads as not found. A non-string `tenant_id` is refused rather than read as unscoped. Callers that send no `tenant_id` see no change. The caller supplies the value: it scopes results and does not authenticate (car#4916).

- On the daemon's MCP HTTP endpoint, an `X-Car-Tenant-Id` header now binds the request to that tenant for `skill_list`, `memory_update_status`, `resources/list`, `resources/read` and `completion/complete`. A request that omits `tenant_id` is scoped to the header's tenant instead of reading every tenant's memory, a body `tenant_id` may only restate it, and a different one is refused (`-32602`, or `isError` from a tool). A header that is not valid UTF-8 or contains `:` is refused rather than ignored, and so is a body `tenant_id` containing `:`. Requests without the header, and the stdio server, keep the optional `tenant_id` filter. Embedders get the same binding through `car_mcp::Server::handle_scoped` (car#5037).

- The meeting bot now authenticates its daemon connection with `session.auth` and negotiates the wire protocol with `server.handshake` before it reports the connection up, and repeats both on every reconnect. It used to send the token only as an upgrade-time `Authorization` header, which the daemon's WebSocket ignores, so an auth-enabled daemon refused its first call. The token comes from `--auth-token`, then `$CAR_AUTH_TOKEN`, then the daemon's token file, and a refusal is printed as the reason the session did not come up (car#4053).

- Conversation context keeps turns in the order they arrived when two turns carry the same timestamp.
  - **Interruptions are filtered from the right turns.** Turns stamped within the same clock tick used to be read newest-first, so an interruption's "hold on" and "back to" markers swapped places and a context could keep an off-topic aside or drop the question it interrupted. (car#4099)

- `memory.query`, NAPI/PyO3 `query_facts` and MCP `memory_query` now match by meaning when the memory has an embedder attached: a fact that says the same thing in other words is returned, and its `score` is the higher of its word match and its similarity to the query, still a 0–1 match strength. Each row carries a new `path` field, `"semantic"` or `"words"`, naming which served the query; with no embedder, or when embedding fails, the query falls back to words and never errors. The daemon's own memgines do not attach an embedder yet, so queries through the daemon still report `"words"` (car#3843; car#4803 tracks the daemon).
- New MCP tool `memory_peek` (`readOnlyHint: true`) returns the decision `memory_intervene` would make without recording it, so a read-only caller can ask for a proactive reminder without changing any counter. MCP `memory_query` and `skill_find` take an optional `tenant_id` (bound by the daemon endpoint's `X-Car-Tenant-Id` header), and a tenant-scoped query never returns another tenant's fact, including one reached through graph edges (car#3227).

- `car models pull` no longer reports a model complete when its cached `config.json` is not a JSON object, and it replaces that cached config with a fresh download instead of linking the bad copy again. The load-failure self-heal now treats such a config as corrupt and removes it and its Hugging Face blob; `car doctor --repair` does the same only for a model it is already repairing for a corrupt weight file, because `car doctor` still judges a model by its weights alone and reports one whose only fault is its config as healthy. Valid JSON holding the wrong values is still not detected. For a model CAR installed, `car models pull` now reports a link to a pruned Hugging Face blob or an unreadable config as damage. The error names the file and says to run `car models remove <model>`, then `car models pull <model>`, and `car models remove` now works on such an install instead of stopping with a bare I/O error. Recording or adopting a folder that already has such a link is still refused. The in-process MLX loader's config errors name the full path and give the same steps. Two cases still stop `car models remove` on such an install: a whole snapshot or repo folder was pruned rather than one blob, or `car doctor --repair` (or a failed load self-heal) already removed a link from the CAR-installed folder, which leaves it no longer matching its install receipt (car#3930, car#3937).

- A multiplayer `submit` or `merge_check --push` that stops at its time limit no longer pushes afterwards. The call's error now matches what happened: if the limit arrives before the push starts, nothing is published and you can submit again; if the push has already started, the call waits for it and reports its real result (car#4081).

- Internal: 27 places where the comment cleanup removed meaning now carry it in names, named constants or small helpers instead (car#5056). No behaviour change.

- CarHost: opening a Needs-you item now takes its macOS banner down even when the banner's delivery (waiting on notification permission or Notification Center) finishes after the item was opened. Banners go up and come down in the order CarHost decided them, so a withdrawal can no longer run before the delivery it takes down and leave the banner showing (car#4891).

- CarHost now marks and announces a handoff or assignment that the same person sends again after the first was opened, instead of leaving it suppressed as the old ask. The Needs-you key now includes the ask's `at_ms`, so after upgrading, an ask that was already opened is marked once more. (car#4893)

- Nightly builds no longer upload to PyPI; stable releases publish every wheel to PyPI as before.
  - **Installing a nightly with pip.** Use the command in the nightly's release notes, for example `pip install --no-index --find-links https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car-releases/releases/expanded_assets/v0.64.0-nightly.20261115.2 car-runtime==0.64.0.dev2026111502`. `pip install --pre car-runtime` stops finding new nightlies. Nightly dev releases already on PyPI stay there.
  - **Why.** PyPI caps the project's size and has no way to delete releases. Nightly dev releases had used a third of the cap, and v0.64.0's Windows wheel was refused for size.
  - **Release checks.** The post-release pip smoke test installs a nightly from its `car-releases` release on macOS, Linux and Windows. On a lab nightly, the pip catch-up marker now means those three installs passed.

- CI and `scripts/ci-local.sh` now fail a change that adds a banned comment to
  Rust under `car-rs/crates/`: a `//` or `/* */` comment, a `///` doc on
  an item that is not bare `pub`, or a review-provenance label. Only lines the
  change adds are read, so a comment on a line the change leaves alone never
  fails; one the change rewords, rewraps or copies is read as new. Docs on
  bare-`pub` items, docs clap, schemars and PyO3 turn into output, `//!` module docs, the
  markers scripts read, licence headers, and `// external: <what the foreign
  thing does>` for behaviour a dependency forces on us are kept. Run it as
  `scripts/check-no-new-comments.sh`; the rule is in
  `scripts/lib/no_new_comments.py`.

- The Office file tools (`read_office_file`, `append_spreadsheet_row`, `fill_word_template`) now refuse a OneDrive or iCloud file that is stored only in the cloud and not downloaded to the computer (a macOS dataless placeholder, or a Windows Files On-Demand placeholder), with a message that names the file and says how to download it, instead of failing silently. Nothing is read or written (car#2773).

- On Windows, an Office or confined-folder save now holds every folder from the agent's working folder down to the destination open for the whole save, so none of them can be renamed, moved or replaced by a junction while it runs. Each held folder's real location is checked against the working folder before anything is written, and a folder already swapped for a junction to somewhere else is refused with "changed while it was being saved" and nothing written outside. New folders the save creates are held the same way (car#3061).
- On Windows, a save now refuses when another program replaced the file after CAR first read it, by comparing the file's volume and file index rather than only checking that a file is still there. The other program's save is kept. A replacement that lands between that check and the final rename is still not caught, the same window as on Linux (car#4035).
- `append_spreadsheet_row` now also refuses when an Excel extended (x14) conditional format over the new row applies a number format that can hide the value, such as `;;;`. Extended rules that only change colours, icons or data bars still append. It also refuses, for both `.xlsx` and `.csv`, a number too small (below 2.2251E-308) or too large (above 9.99999999999999E+307) for Excel to keep, instead of saving a value Excel shows as 0 or cannot hold (car#2748).
- The `run_applescript` tool description now tells the assistant to use an app's own scripting dictionary before System Events UI scripting, to make read-only checks before any write and never change an existing note's body unless asked, and that Notes tags and Smart Folders cannot be scripted, so it should say so and offer folders (car#2019).

- Saving an Office or CSV file no longer overwrites a save another program made a moment earlier, and no longer drops Finder tags silently.
  - **A concurrent save is kept.** On APFS and HFS+, CAR swaps its new file into place and keeps the swap only if the file it replaced is the one it opened. Otherwise it puts the other program's file back and reports that the file changed while saving.
  - **Lost attributes refuse the save.** If CAR cannot copy a file's extended attributes (Finder tags, quarantine), the save fails and the file is left unchanged.

- Organization admission now honors a `Retry-After` given as an HTTP date, not only as a number of seconds. A date-form answer was read as no instruction, so CAR retried within a second and remembered the context as busy for only the 15 s default; it now waits until that date, within the same 300 s ceiling (car#5106).

- An organization-bound agent's board write no longer finishes a stranded board-key rotation. Finishing it reads the org's device directory from the relay, which spends the operator's shared directory quota. The agent's write now lands on this device's copy of the key, and the other devices' copies wait for the person's own CAR. A write made while a rotation is still due, right after someone left, still reads the directory now for any caller, because the board takes no write until the next key is stored (car#4779).
- A re-key registration demand is no longer dropped when a sign-in activation is already pending. It stays raised until that activation finishes. If the activation installed a session, the re-key only arms the certificate pass, with no extra credential read. If the activation failed for good, the re-key makes its own capped attempt, so a failed sign-in retry no longer leaves a re-keyed device unregistered (car#4778).
- A lost `sync/device-id` no longer turns Parslee sync on for a journal with local-only history. `car sync enable` now records the owner's choice as the `parslee-sync-enabled` file. A sync root with no `device-id` but another device id's oplog folder stays local and names `car sync enable`. An enable made on an older build, which only moved the id aside, still counts (car#4759).
