The `Command` debug form of a token is checked on Unix only, where `Command`'s debug output shows its environment. The brute-force collab-history guard walk runs on Linux only.
- **Heal stops a timed-out git's whole process tree on Windows.** `git` there is a launcher that starts the real git as its child; at the wall only the launcher was killed, so the real git kept running and held the output pipes, and the wait for them never ended (the Windows heavy-tests job hung on `a_fetch_that_never_answers_is_stopped_and_the_tick_ends` until its timeout). Each heal process now runs in a Job Object that is terminated at the wall, as the Unix process group is.
- **Fleet build jobs find the MSVC linker on Windows.** The worker clears a job's environment and kept only a short list, which lacked the variables MSVC discovery reads (`ProgramFiles(x86)`, `ProgramData` and the rest), so rustc fell back to the first `link` on PATH, Git's coreutils one. The worker now passes Windows' standard system locations through.
- **car-server-core's Windows tests pass.** Fixtures enrolled `/bin/sh` (not absolute on Windows) and a launcher pid of 1 (alive only on Unix); the heal end-to-end rounds that run a builder, which CarCoder refuses without write confinement, and two heal tests that execute shell-script stubs run on macOS and Linux only.
- **Every Windows CI job fits its budget.** car-server-core's nextest run is its own job (`windows-integrations-server-core`), `windows-build` leaves the brute-force collab-history guard walk to Linux as `windows-integrations` does, and the prerequisite witness gives each car-server-core rebuild 45 minutes instead of 20 (it had never completed).
- **Ended sessions end on Windows.** The daemon's process check (`peers::process_exists`) answered "alive" for every pid on Windows, so a session whose launcher had exited never ended and a successor could not take its seat or name. It now asks Windows (`OpenProcess` and the exit code), through car-sandbox's existing `pid_is_alive`.

- `car worktree hook` on Windows no longer lets a default-branch fetch run untracked. When the fetch cannot be placed in a job object, the hook now says so on stderr, stops the fetch at once, and bases the worktree on the origin ref already present or the local HEAD. Before, it waited out the 5 s timeout and then killed only `git` (car#3747).
- Windows CI now runs the plugin's POSIX fallback hook under Git for Windows' bash with Windows-spelled paths. The tests cover WorktreeRemove of a clean tree, SubagentStop keeping uncommitted work, and refusal of the main checkout, of a tree outside `.claude/worktrees`, and of a symlink or junction in a tree's place (car#4046). They also cover an unreachable origin whose ssh transport hangs (car#3740). The hook finishes shortly after the 5 s fetch timeout and no transport is left running. That cleanup comes from Git for Windows' own kill of `git.exe`, which matches children by parent pid alone, so car#3740's requirement that only the fetch's own descendants be reached is still open.

- When the daemon refuses a client older than its wire protocol, the `server.handshake` refusal now says what to restart for each kind of client. For the collaboration bridge (`car-mcp`) in a Claude Code or Codex session, restart that session or reconnect the plugin's MCP server. For CarHost, quit and reopen it. For an npm or PyPI app, install the daemon's own version, still pinned (`npm install car-runtime@<version>` / `pip install -U car-runtime==<version>`), and then restart the app. Before this, the refusal told a `car-mcp` session to install the npm or PyPI package at the version it already ran. The refusal also names the daemon's build ID next to its version (`car-server 0.65.0, build 20261123-93ff004`), and the client's own handshake error names its build ID, because a wire-protocol change can ship without a version bump. The `protocol version mismatch:` prefix and the `-32006` code are unchanged (car#5130).

- An orchestrator can cap each label's workers on their own: `[workers.spend] per_label = { tenant = [ { usd = 5, per = "day" } ] }` installs instead of being refused. A label at its cap refuses that label's workers' model calls (`budget reached until <time>`, the shared refusal) and asks the owner once per label and period, while the orchestrator's other labels' workers keep running. The request names the orchestrator and no label value.

- `car worktree release` no longer strands a slot when it cannot finish. If locking the parked slot or removing its lease fails, the slot goes back on the branch it was on, unlocked and with its built-head marker as acquire left it, so you keep working in it without acquiring again; before, it was left detached on the pool base and locked while still leased to you (car#4777).

- A subagent's stop now releases only its own worktree pool slot, and never one a process still works in (car#5023, car#5024). Two ways a slot was handed to another agent while its holder was still working in it are closed.
  - **A workflow stop is bound to the stopping agent.** A workflow subagent's slot (`wf_…`) used to be found from the stop's `cwd`, so a nested workflow child that ran in its parent's slot freed that slot when it stopped, and so could the stop of anything that ran inside a session-chosen lease shaped like `wf_…`. The slot is now the `worktreePath` Claude Code records for that agent (with `spawnedWithWorktree: true`) in the `agent-<id>.meta.json` beside the stop's `agent_transcript_path`. A child with no worktree of its own releases nothing, and a missing or unreadable meta releases nothing. Outside the pool, the Rust hook and the plugin's sh fallback remove a workflow agent's clean `.claude/worktrees/wf_…` tree on the same rule. A workflow agent whose stop arrives from outside its slot now has that slot released instead of left leased.
  - **A stop leaves a slot a process still works in.** `SubagentStop` also fires when a background subagent only ends a turn, for example with a test still running, and that stop released its clean slot. Every `SubagentStop` release, of an `agent-<id>` lease or a `wf_…` one, is now refused while any process other than the hook and its ancestors has its working directory in the slot, or when that cannot be told (`lsof` on macOS, `/proc` on Linux). The lease then stays until a later stop, `WorktreeRemove`, or the end of the session. `car worktree release` and `WorktreeRemove` are unchanged.
  - Still open: a background subagent that ends a turn with nothing running in its slot, and is woken later, has its slot released at that stop. Every agent shares one Claude Code process, so nothing tells it apart from a finished one.
  - The pooled stop path runs in `car worktree hook`, so it takes a `car` build that contains both #5015 and this change: the plugin hands every event to whatever `car worktree hook` is on `PATH`, and an older one keeps its old rule.

- A workflow subagent's worktree is given back when it stops (car#3869). Claude Code names a workflow subagent's worktree `wf_<run>-<step>-<n>`, not after its agent id, so `SubagentStop` never found its lease and every workflow run left its slots leased (or, outside the pool, its `.claude/worktrees/wf_…` trees on disk).
  - **Pool on:** a stop with `agent_type: "workflow-subagent"` releases the slot its `cwd` is in, only while that slot's lease is exactly `<session>/wf_…`, and only when the slot is clean; a dirty slot stays leased with its work, and a branch with commits the base lacks is kept. A lease held by the session itself, by another session, or for a name the session chose (`claude --worktree`, `EnterWorktree`) is never touched.
  - **Pool off:** the same stop removes the clean `wf_…` tree its `cwd` is in, with its branch, in the Rust hook and in the plugin's sh fallback.
  - `car worktree release` without `--force` now refuses a workflow subagent's slot (`<owner>/wf_…`) as it refuses an `agent-<id>` one.
  - A subagent that ends on an API error can still keep its slot leased; that half of car#3869 is open.
- `scripts/build-wire-schema.sh` resolves relative output paths against the directory it was run from (car#5009). It used to `cd car-rs` first, so a relative path landed under `car-rs/` (a path such as `car-rs/crates/...` became `car-rs/car-rs/crates/...`) and the committed schema silently stayed as it was. It now also refuses a path whose parent directory does not exist.

- Every copy of the `zip` crate in CAR is now 9.6.1. The vendored candle-core moved off the yanked zip 7.2.0, so the local model-weight loaders (`.npz`/`.pth`) get the fixes for RUSTSEC-2026-0545 through 0548 along with the Office-file tools (car#4768, car#2885).

See the [release notes][v0.65.0].

## [v0.64.0] — 2026-11-15

### Changes

- Coding assistants are one table, and Gemini CLI and Pi sessions can enroll.
  - **One list.** `car_external_agents::AssistantKind` names every coding assistant CAR knows: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi and Parslee Core. Its descriptor holds the binary, session id prefix, display name, how the assistant loads CAR, how its process and any multi-session host (the ChatGPT app's `codex app-server`) are recognised, and its hook points. Session enrollment, `car session-enroll`, the abandoned-session sweep, the collaboration server's parent recognition and the worktree pool's app-server check read it instead of their own lists.
  - **Gemini CLI and Pi sessions enroll.** With `car-mcp --collaboration` in their MCP config, a plainly started `gemini` or `pi` session gets a `gemini-session-*` / `pi-session-*` identity, the board and peer tools, its project's Lattice and abandoned-session cleanup. CAR installs no hooks in either yet and has no `car gemini` / `car pi` launcher; see the plugin README for why.
  - **CarHost names Codex sessions.** A Lattice request from a Codex (or Gemini CLI, or Pi) session now reads "A coding session", as a Claude Code one did, instead of showing its agent id.

- The CAR plugin in Claude Code and Codex follows the installed release however CAR was updated.
  - **First run of a new version re-pins the plugin.** CarHost's Sparkle update and the .pkg installer replace the binaries without running `car update`, so the plugin stayed on the previous release and its fixes never reached a session. The first `car` command of a new version (including the plugin's own hooks) now starts the refresh in a detached background process and records the outcome in `<CAR_HOME>/doctor/assistant-plugins.json`. It runs once per version. A refresh that did not settle is retried at most hourly, and a settled one is checked again daily. No marketplace is removed unless the release's tag can be reached on the repository. The refresh never runs under a `CAR_HOME`, `CODEX_HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` of its own, from a binary inside a Cargo target directory, or from a supervised agent. Its log is `<CAR_HOME>/logs/assistant-plugins.log`. `car update` records the same stamp, and under a `CAR_HOME` override it now leaves the person's assistants alone, as it already did for the `car-mcp` PATH link.
  - **Codex's marketplace add no longer "did not finish".** `codex plugin marketplace add Parslee-ai/car@vX.Y.Z` makes a full clone of the repository. That took 150 s on 2026-11-14, and every plugin call was capped at 60 s. Calls that add or install now get 15 minutes. Both output pipes are read while the call runs, so a call that writes more than a pipe buffer no longer stalls. A call past its bound is ended together with the `git` it started.
  - **The plugin is refreshed in the assistant `car claude` starts.** The binary is now resolved the way `car agent external` resolves it: the `CAR_CODEX_BIN` / `CAR_CLAUDE_CODE_BIN` pin first, then the first runnable match on `PATH`. A plain `PATH` walk had ignored the pin.
- A Claude Code session bound to one org, in a repository whose `.car/config.toml` now declares another, is told to restart. A session binds its org when it starts, so a session started before the repository named its org kept posting to the old org's board. `car peer-inbox-hook` now compares the two on each prompt and at session start, and adds a line to the session's context naming both orgs and asking the person to start a new session. It reads only the session's credentials file and the repository's config.

- `car board comment <id> <text> [--org <org>]` lets the operator comment on any item on their boards. Org-bound sessions cannot see a personal-scope item, such as one a ChatGPT-app Codex thread wrote with no org binding, so a comment from the operator is how to reach that thread. A comment never changes the item.

- Save approval resolution, dismissal, disconnect reaping, withdrawal and hidden-row creation in one floor-journal revision. Stamp the resolver before saving; append to the resolution audit journal only after the commit and `approval.resolved` event. Failed saves restore the previous floor and approval ledger, return an error, and publish neither an approval event nor an audit decision, so a restart cannot lose an owner decision between writes.
- Reuse restored Lattice review mirrors without replaying approval prompts, recreate missing legacy mirrors, and remember restored rows so a later TTL sweep does not prompt the same review again in that daemon process. Saved channel decisions still reach the Lattice asker once after restart.

- Fix CAR-651: retain resolved approval rows across daemon restarts for 24 hours from their original resolution time, preserving the answer, daemon-stamped `resolver` (`principal` and `transport`) and presentation choice. Disconnect-reaped rows omit `resolver`. Dismissal survives subsequent restarts, and restoring a decision does not announce it again.

- Mark received iMessage daemon self-echoes with `own_echo` before messages.read, host inbound events and the owner floor consume them. Persist a send log of final transport text, recipient, send time and correlated sent ROWID/GUID; match each daemon send once within the configurable 5-second default across restart. Preserve owner iPhone replies with their own sent/received twins, including `A0 approve`, and retain the closed approval grammar (CAR-919).
- Route floor questions, approval prompts, test sends, outbound adapters and direct Messages sends through durable logging. Correlate only new ROWIDs in active chats outside the send-log lock. Atomically compact `messages-send-log.json` at startup and on use: keep send ID, recipient, exact text, time, pre-send ROWID, confirmed status, sent/echo identities and reader cursors for up to 24 hours while unmatched, or the configured window plus 60 seconds after matching; cap at 500 oldest-first sends (CAR-919).
- Preserve positive own-echo judgments in a durable per-row identity index across restart, history reads and send-log expiry/eviction, so a floor-send echo first read after 120 seconds or two hours cannot answer its own question. Instrument SQLite and transport lock boundaries in test builds (CAR-919).

- CarHost fixes: question privacy, approval outcomes, sign-out warnings, chat order, model removal, and test scratch files.
  - **Questions of unknown origin keep their text out of notifications** (car#4493). A question from a legacy `peer:<key>` sender, which carries no remote CAR name, was treated as asked on this Mac, and its text went into the notification banner. CarHost now follows the daemon's `origin`: only `local` is local, and `unknown`, `device` without a name, and another owner's question without a remote name are labeled as from an unverified or another owner's CAR, with the text kept inside the app.
  - **A replaced turn's approval card shows "Outcome unknown"** (car#4241). If you approve a card and then send again before the agent confirms, the daemon closes the old approval as `unknown`. The old turn's saved card now says Outcome unknown instead of Expired or Not confirmed, on disk and after relaunch, and it gets no buttons back.
  - **Settings shows the sign-out warning while another account stays signed in** (car#4312). Removing one of two Parslee logins while its device certificate can't be revoked now shows the warning in Settings even though the other login keeps you signed in.
  - **Viewing a chat no longer moves it to the top of Chat history** (car#3880). Only a new message or a change to the chat's goal, tasks or folder counts as activity. Opening an old chat and switching away leaves it in its place.
  - **Remove from CAR asks first** (car#2725). Removing a local model now opens a confirmation that names the model and its size and says it can be downloaded again. It doesn't promise the space back, because shared Hugging Face files may stay on disk.
  - **CarHost tests clean up their temporary files** (car#4505). Each test process works in one `CarHostTests-run-<pid>` folder in the temporary directory, removed when the process exits. The next run removes the folder of a process that died. A test fails if any CarHost test writes straight into the temporary directory.

- When a change reaches `car-server-core`, CI's merge-queue `test` job now builds the whole workspace, which keeps the restored build cache and the same feature resolution, and runs only the selected crates' tests through a nextest package filter. The first real scoped run, #4485, selected 40 crates through `car-inference`. With `-p`, it compiled about 90 s longer than a full run and still ran 86% of the tests. Changes that don't reach `car-server-core` keep the smaller `-p` build.

- CI's merge queue now builds and tests only the crates a change can affect. That means the changed crates, everything that depends on them, and the crates whose tests read files outside themselves. A change confined to dated docs or changelog fragments runs no Rust build at all, where it used to wait on the full ~20-minute suite. Every other path outside the Rust workspace, and any doubt, still runs everything, as do tags and the nightly.

- Coder fixes from batch #4121 (second lane).
  - **A pending no-change finding survives a daemon restart.** Opening the session (`coder.subscribe`) restores its finding gate while the retained worktree still sits at the session's start commit, so `needs_you` reads `finding` again and `coder.approve_merge` with `accept_finding` or `approve: false` resolves it (car#4170).
  - **A silent check on a Docker or VM substrate ends as a red timed-out check.** A remote substrate returns output only when its command ends, so a check with a silence window is stopped at that window and reported `timed_out` and `silenced`, as a silent local check is, instead of hanging until the session watchdog fails the whole session as stalled (car#4276).
  - **The verifier judges a differential check against the baseline.** A `run_check` probe of a check with a `differential` now holds its before/after claim against the session's baseline capture, as the builder's gate does, so a regression the differential exists to catch cannot back a PASS (car#4232).
  - **A session's tools share one rate-limit budget.** Every executor of a coder session, and the verifier's re-runs of an agent's scenarios, draw from one load of the operator's `.car/policies` rules, so a `rate_limit_tool` cap counts the build and its verification together (car#2757).
  - **An unreadable mini-swe-agent trajectory is scored when the worktree moved.** It is now its own `InvokeError::UnreadableTrajectory`. The coder leaves the run out of scoring only when the worktree is provably untouched since the run began; otherwise the contract judges what the agent left and a red result is a scored loss (car#4103).
  - **A named slow unattended coder is warned about.** A coder named in `heal.toml` whose measured decode speed is below the 50 tok/s floor still runs, and the sweep logs a warning naming the model and the floor (car#4278).
  - **A recycled pid no longer keeps a crashed run's builder home.** Boot reconciliation reclaims a contract-run builder home when the live process now holding its pid started after the home was made (car#4235).
  - **macOS: a hard link out of a small credential store refuses an untrusted check.** For a repository that is not trusted, a regular file inside `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker`, `~/.azure` or `~/Library/Keychains` that has a second hard link refuses the check, as a protected file with one already did: the store is hidden by path and Seatbelt cannot deny a file by identity. The large application homes (`~/.codex`, `~/.claude`, `~/.config`) are still denied by path but not walked (car#4228).

- CarCoder contract checks and folder agents: fixes from batch #4121.
  - **A cache-local `TMPDIR` works on macOS.** A contract check keeps its host's `TMPDIR`, and a bare `mktemp` there was refused when `TMPDIR` pointed outside the system temp folder. That folder now gets the same `tmp.<random>` grant as the system one, and nothing else in it is writable (#4488).
  - **A folder agent's run no longer recreates its deleted working folder.** An agent made with Build an Agent whose working folder was deleted after its build now fails its run with "this agent's working folder … no longer exists", instead of running against an empty folder made in its place. Opening the folder is one step, so a folder deleted between a check and the open is refused too (#4246).
  - **Fewer checks are mistaken for output assertions.** A Python `assert (x == y, "msg")` asserts a tuple and is always true; text inside a Python triple-quoted string is not code; and a `/…/` regex literal in a Node, Ruby or Perl `-e` program is data. None of these counts as a check that asserts output any more (#4274, #4236).
  - **"Cannot run" reads the command that actually ran.** `env FOO=1 pnpm test || exit 1` on a machine without pnpm, and `python3 -I -m pytest` without pytest, are now checks that cannot run rather than red tests. A check that only prints `python3 -m some_module` launches no module, so the interpreter line its own subprocess prints stays a red test (#4274, #4236).
  - **Several heredocs on one line are checked for broken quoting.** An open quote outside them, or a later heredoc whose delimiter never comes, is reported as broken quoting (#4274).

- The Codex CLI backend rides out a transient `ETXTBSY` when it starts `codex` (both a run and the `codex login status` probe), using the same bounded retry the vLLM-MLX pool already used. On Linux, a fork on another thread right after the binary was written could make the exec fail with "Text file busy" even though nothing was wrong; a fault that persists past the ~190 ms ceiling is still reported, with its error kind intact.

- Fix Codex collaboration startup: find a matching `car-mcp` beside the CLI or on PATH, install and update the adapter with lane binaries, and declare Codex plugin inbox and board hooks. Plain Codex sessions receive inbox notices after users trust those hooks.
- Keep the preflight gate free of Cargo builds when checking the conversation-floor model.

- Codex sessions not started by CAR work better with it.
  - **Stale identities are cleaned up.** A Codex thread's self-enrolled identity now ends when its collaboration server exits. Before, the sweep also checked the assistant process, and in the ChatGPT app that is the Codex app-server, which runs every thread and never exits. So 25 of 27 `codex-session-*` records outlived their servers by days. A pid recycled to an unrelated process no longer reads as the launcher. Older unmarked records are removed only when their launcher is gone or no longer CAR and their assistant is such an app-server.
  - **Threads without hooks learn about mail.** Every collaboration tool result other than `peer_inbox` and `collaboration_status` now carries `inbox_waiting` (a count, never message text) whenever mail waits, so a thread whose hooks don't run is told on its next CAR call.
  - **`car codex` works in a worktree-pool slot.** Started in a linked worktree, it adds the repository's common git dir as a writable root (`--add-dir`), so the session can commit and push from the slot.

- A stable release cut on a Mac now regenerates the published CLI reference from the `car` it just built in `dist/darwin-arm64/`, instead of failing the docs step when the committed CLI.md is from the previous version.

- A child git command no longer inherits git configuration carried in the environment. `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` and each `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>` are removed with the other repository redirects, since any of them can set `core.worktree`. Fixes #4328.
- Writing an agent's key no longer fails on a temp file a crash left behind. Each write uses a temp file of its own and removes it if the write fails, and only a bare 404 from the account service means the call is not supported, so a 404 that names an error is a refusal. Fixes #4343.
- A bead handoff flushes its directory after writing the journal and after each bead rename, so a power loss cannot lose the journal's name. Fixes #4359.
- Mail's per-message fallback no longer matches rows to a bulk Message-ID list it has not verified. Fixes #4363.
- `session.auth` latches a session whose agent the supervisor no longer knows, on the Mac as it already did on Linux. Fixes #4356.

- A Gemini CLI session started plainly now enrolls even after Gemini relaunches itself with a larger heap (`node --max-old-space-size=N gemini`). That relaunched process is the one that starts `car-mcp`, and CAR did not recognise it as Gemini CLI before.

- Tests: the daemon-restart approval tests wait for the WebSocket handshake itself instead of a bare TCP probe, and report the daemon's own error if it exits during startup (a probe-then-refused race failed the 20261114 nightly).

- Release lab operators can ask for a same-day nightly with `car-release nightly --now`, and preview it with `car-release nightly --now --dry-run`.
  - **A fix that missed today's nightly ships today.** `--now` cuts the newest fully green commit after today's nightly as the next same-day version (`vX.Y.Z-nightly.YYYYMMDD.2`, then `.3`), through the same steps, verifier and `Build-Id`/`Built-By` trailers. With nothing newer it answers `no nightly due` and builds nothing. Its run record carries `"ad_hoc": true` and `"request": "nightly --now"` beside the starter.
  - **The scheduled nightly and a plain `car-release nightly` still cut at most once a day.** Link's plain `nightly` still re-cuts as before.
  - **A retry no longer reports the day's first nightly as done while a later same-day cut is unfinished.** It resumes the newest unfinished cut that was tagged instead, even when a still later attempt stopped before tagging.
  - **Operators must refresh their installed client** (`cp -fL scripts/car-release ~/.local/bin/car-release`) to get `--now`; a lab update alone does not change the copy on a laptop.

- Stable promotion is lab-only, and the lab's record of a stable reaches `main` even when `main` has moved.
  - **The laptop promotion path is retired.** `scripts/release.sh` (including `--channel stable`) and `scripts/release-bootstrap.sh`, foreground and `--detach`, refuse any stable version before any git, gh or Azure call, detached launch, release log or build, and print `car-release promote <nightly>`. A laptop nightly is unchanged. The laptop path's bump pull request was one commit on the nightly, so it conflicted once `main` changed a manifest (car#4528).
  - **The lab's bookkeeping pull request uses its own branch, `lab-bookkeeping/<stable>`.** It never finds, reuses, force-pushes or closes a `release/<stable>` branch or pull request the laptop path left behind. A stable whose record already merged under the older name (v0.62.0) still counts as recorded.
  - **A queued bookkeeping pull request is pending, not recorded.** Every attempt checks that the record still merges into the current `main`. When `main` moved onto a manifest it stamps, the attempt rebuilds it on that `main` and pushes it as a fast-forward of the same pull request. `bookkeeping.log` ends with `RECORDED <stable>` once it merged and `PENDING <stable>` while it waits.

- Fixes in five leaf crates: revocation-list lifetime, conversation-client errors, iMessage echo matching, GRPO reporting, and credential detection.
  - **A revocation list lasts until its issuer's `exp`.** `device_cert::verify_revocation_list` no longer refuses a signed list whose `exp - iat` is over an hour (`lifetime_too_long`). Its freshness for sealed collaboration content is `iat <= now < exp`. Contact admission still needs a list issued within the last hour (`RevocationList::is_fresh`, unchanged) (#4441).
  - **The conversations client no longer reads a 404 as "no such conversation" unless the backend's error code is `not_found`.** A 404 with another code is a `Refused` carrying that code. A 404 with no code, such as a proxy's page, is an `Http` error with an unknown outcome. A page cursor that is not a string or a number is now an error, where it was read as the end of the list. So is a cursor `list_all` already received, at any distance; before, a cycle made it list forever. An authority with a query, fragment or credentials is refused rather than rewritten (#4423).
  - **iMessage echo matching keeps a sent row that has no handle.** Before, a send addressed by phone number whose row Messages stored without a handle could be skipped by a read that ran before its received copy arrived. That copy then read as the owner's own message. Only sent rows whose text matches a send CAR made are kept (#4506).
  - **GRPO reports zero score from grader credit.** `car-harness-train grpo` now counts a reply as zero score only when it earned no grader credit, which is what its reward uses. Partial credit without a pass no longer counts as a failure in `failed_or_zero_rate`. An `--out` directory that already holds a run (`samples.jsonl`) is refused, so two runs' samples are never mixed under one report (#2971).
  - **Credential detection.** "bearer" followed by auth prose is no longer read as a token. The prose is a closed list of words (authentication, authorization, credentials, header, token, scheme and a few more), in any case, joined by `-` or `/` ("use bearer authentication"). Any other value is still a token (#4524). Slack `xoxa-`, `xoxr-`, `xoxe-`, `xoxe.xoxb-`/`xoxe.xoxp-`, `xapp-`, `xoxs-` and `xoxo-` tokens are now redacted in feedback bundles and failure records. car-selfheal's evidence redactor also covers `xoxo-`, `xoxe` and `xapp-` (#4540).

- The daemon now knows how busy its machine is. Every 30 seconds it samples load per core, the OS memory-pressure verdict, bytes swapped out since the last sample, swap in use and free disk on the state root, and folds them into one rating: `plenty` (takes heavy work), `tight` (light work only) or `overloaded` (swapping, memory pressure critical, or the disk nearly full). Nothing is configured: each threshold is a ratio of the machine's own cores, memory or disk. New `machine.capacity` JSON-RPC method (`machineCapacity()` / `machine_capacity()`) returns the rating, the findings behind it and the raw sample.
- Fleet inventory rows carry `capacity: { rating, sampled_at_ms }` (never the raw numbers), `fleet.composite` workers carry `capacity`, and `car fleet show` prints it. A fleet worker that rates itself `overloaded` declines dispatches with `busy` whatever its free slots. A distributed `foreman.run` / `car fleet run` places subtasks on the workers with the most room first (`plenty`, then unreported, then `tight`; fewer declines in the last hour first), leaves overloaded peers out with the exclusion reason `overloaded`, and ranks this host by its own rating instead of always first.

- `car machine leftovers --remove` now removes what the owner approved. It sent the host-only `machine.leftovers.remove` on an ordinary connection, which the daemon refused, so nothing was ever removed (car#4531). A car-cli test now fails on any host-only method sent that way.

- `car machine leftovers --remove` removes what an ended coding session left behind, after listing exactly what it will remove and asking (`--yes` skips the question). It removes only stopped containers and anonymous volumes no container uses, of sessions that have ended. Running containers, named volumes, build cache and anything not attributed to a session are never removed. Each item is checked again right before a single plain `DELETE` (no force). The CLI uses the new host-only daemon method `machine.leftovers.remove { ids, session? }`, which refuses the whole request if any id is not on offer.

- CAR now knows what coding sessions leave on the machine. `car machine resources` lists Docker containers, volumes, images, build cache and buildx builders, the Docker VM's host memory (its physical footprint, which counts compressed memory; RSS had shown a 22 GB VM as 1.8 GB), and processes of 1 GiB or more whose parent has gone. Each container and volume is attributed to the coding session that made it, or marked unattributed with the reason. `car machine leftovers` shows, for each ended `car claude` / `car codex` / enrolled session, what it made that still exists, with sizes, and which items would be offered for removal: stopped containers, and anonymous volumes no container uses. Running containers and named volumes are never offered. `car doctor` prints the findings without the daemon. A recurring leak (two or more anonymous volumes from one image that declares `VOLUME`, left by containers removed with `docker rm -f` without `-v`) is named with its image and cause. Docker is read through its local socket with GET requests only. The daemon reads Docker while Docker Desktop's VM is running and never wakes it from Resource Saver. New daemon methods `machine.resources` and `machine.leftovers`, refused to a supervised agent. New crate `car-machine-inventory`.

- Your own CARs on different networks now reach each other through the Parslee relay of an org both hold. A device qualifies only when it is on your personal-sync roster (the sync passphrase) AND holds a valid Parslee certificate under the same account; the certificate adds transport, never trust. Messages to its Lattice nodes fall back to the relay when its address does not answer, and its node listing and fleet inventory are pushed over the relay so `car lattice nodes` and `car fleet show` list it (a relayed device takes no `car fleet run` work). `lattice.directory` gains `own_devices`, which also lists any device signed in as you that has not joined your sync. A knock on your own account now says how your devices link instead of claiming they are already connected. Both devices need this release.

- A signed-in CAR with a sync passphrase now finds its owner's other devices on its own. Once the daemon holds a Parslee session it opens Parslee personal sync and pumps it every minute, so a Mac (whose host never called `sync.pump`) no longer shows an empty own-device roster. Each device needs this release for the other to see it. A sync opened before the daemon knew of the login no longer stays on the pre-login journal until a restart. `car auth status` and `car doctor` say when the sync passphrase is missing and how to set it.

- The CAR plugin's `PreToolUse` hook (`car policy-check-hook`, Claude Code and `car codex` sessions) now watches this machine's load before heavy work. For a shell command that starts a build, a full test run, a container build, a dependency install or a model download, it reads the daemon's rating from `<state root>/run/capacity.json`: on a `tight` machine the call proceeds with one line of context naming the load; on an `overloaded` one it is refused with the reason and what to do instead. Light commands are untouched and cause no read; with no daemon or a stale rating the watch says nothing. The heavy-command classifier is `car_policy::tool_gate::heavy_work`, built on the policy hook's shell reader, so a program that is only mentioned (`echo "cargo build"`) does not count.

- `car worktree reclaim`, which a full-pool `acquire` runs, now also frees a slot whose holder is still alive once its work is done. The slot must be clean apart from build output, have no stash for its branch, and have nothing running in it. Then either:
  - its head moved since it was handed out and is already on the base (an ancestor, cherry-picked or squash-merged), and nothing in it changed for `wtpool.idleMinutes` (default 30); or
  - its holder is the Codex app-server, which runs every Codex thread and never exits, so its leases never ended; every commit is on a remote, and nothing changed for twice that time.

  The branch and its commits stay; acquire the branch again to resume. `acquire` no longer claims a free slot that has a process running in it. A raised `wtpool.size` now reaches acquires that are already waiting. The shared `wt-pool.sh` makes the same changes.

- `scripts/ci-local.sh --preflight` now runs the spend-gated dispatch check
  (`scripts/check-spend-gated-dispatch.sh`, including the daemon spawn
  allow-list in `scripts/spend-spawn-allow.txt`), which the required
  `ffi-parity` job runs and preflight used to pass without. Its ~75 s controls
  stay in the full run. Preflight also names the `doctor_state_writers` test it
  skips (it builds car-cli) and the command that runs it.
- The regenerating merge drivers (`regen-capabilities`, `regen-daemon-contract`,
  `regen-wire-schema`) now run their Cargo-backed generators holding the
  machine-wide build lock (`~/.cache/car-build.lock`), so a merge that needs a
  real regeneration waits behind a running build instead of starting another
  beside it. Machines without that lock, and governed installs whose cargo
  governor locks each command, are unchanged.

- Questions for people read as words, not addresses. CarHost's banner used to say "Question for human:matt / From mcp:085d53e1-…" and leave out the question. It now names who asked ("Claude Code in fms") as the title and whom ("Question for Matt Liotta") as the subtitle, and carries the question's first line as the body. Lock-screen privacy is left to the system's Show Previews setting. A question from another owner's CAR, or from an unverified one, still keeps its text out of the banner. The Approvals card leads with the asker, with the raw address in its tooltip. A board ask's text is now just the question, without the item id and project boilerplate. Review approvals mirrored to iMessage and Slack use the same names. `lattice.requests` rows gain `from_label` and `to_label`.

- The committed CLI reference and the Python wheel's bundled docs are regenerated from the v0.63.0 `car`.

- Release and developer scripts: fixes from the macOS scripts batch (car#4411).
  - **Long PR descriptions no longer fail the replay-corpus freeze check.** `scripts/check-replay-corpus-freeze.sh` hands the PR body to its Python side as a file, not an exported variable, so a description over Linux's 128 KiB per-string limit no longer fails every later command with "Argument list too long" (car#4545).
  - **Stable release notes link the changelog.** A lab-promoted stable's notes on both `Parslee-ai/car` and `Parslee-ai/car-releases` now point at that version's entry in the public `car-releases` CHANGELOG.md (car#4425). Releases already published keep their old notes.
  - **`scripts/smart-test.sh` runs with `--no-fail-fast` by default**, so one unrelated failing test binary can no longer stop cargo before the touched crates are tested. `--no-fail-fast` is accepted explicitly, and `--fail-fast` restores the old stop-at-first-failure behavior (car#4542).
  - **`scripts/verify-formal-floor.sh` builds into the shared Cargo target** instead of a private `~/.cache/cargo-target-slot-floor`, which rebuilt from scratch beside it. It refreshes this checkout's changed sources first, as every shared-target build does. An explicit `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` still wins (car#4396, car#4429).
  - **`scripts/test-refresh-changed-sources.sh` passes with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set**, and no longer writes its checkout marker into, or cleans, the caller's target (car#4538).
  - **`car-automation`'s `lists_shortcuts` test is ignored** with "requires a GUI login session": the Shortcuts CLI cannot reach its helper over SSH with no GUI login, as on the release lab. Run it with `cargo test -p car-automation -- --ignored lists_shortcuts` (car#4543).
  - **Release-lab runbook:** after `car-release update`, a stale root schedule command is refreshed by running `setup-lab.sh` from the admin checkout at the lab's commit, and every `sudo` command, `operators.sh` included, runs from that admin checkout, never the service checkout (car#4537).

- `docs/solutions/process-global-state-in-tests.md` records the hub-token probe as a third family of the `Text file busy` race, fixed in #4485. It also notes where the retry belongs: in the seam that every caller already shares.

- Spend "at budget" clearing events are no longer held back or published early.
  - **One unreadable declarative spec no longer delays every clear after a restart.** The minute tick that adopts every principal already at budget skips a declarative agent whose spec cannot be read, adopts the rest, and tries that one again on the next tick (car#4445).
  - **A refusal at an owner or class limit stays published until the limit admits again.** A worker, the operator, an outside credential or CAR's own work refused at an owner or class limit is published and tracked under that limit's key (`owner:<owner>` or the class key), so `spend.changed` no longer reports it cleared while its calls are still refused (car#4445).

- An orchestrator's `[workers.spend]` caps are enforced. Every call one of its workers makes is charged to `workers:<orchestrator>` as well as to the worker, and once that total reaches a cap the gate refuses the workers' calls with the shared spend-cap refusal and asks the owner once, as it does for an agent's own cap. The key is an aggregate, so `spend.costs` totals do not count it twice. Fixes #4339.
- A declarative agent can carry `spend_caps`, the same `{usd, per}` list a bundle uses with one cap per period. The gate charges its runs to `declarative:<id>`, refuses them once a cap is reached and asks the owner to save the agent with a larger cap. A Builder rebuild keeps the caps of the agent it replaces, and `declagents.list`/`declagents.get` show them when declared. Fixes #4340.

- Fixed a test flake: `car-inference`'s hub-token tests write a fake program and exec it immediately. Under the shared-process test job, a sibling test's fork could briefly hold that file open for writing, and the exec failed with `Text file busy`. Only `hf_cache`'s own tests retried. The retry now lives in the shared test probe, and all seven tests that use the probe go through it.

- Two tests that checked an unreachable address no longer fail intermittently when a parallel test is handed the same freed port.

- The car-server-core test suite compiles on Windows again; a test helper several coder tests use was gated to Unix only.

- Windows clippy is clean again for `car-server-core`'s tests: a Unix-only test helper no longer counts as dead code on Windows.

- The Windows `car` binary builds again; a Unix-only import in the worktree hook had broken it since the v0.63.0 nightly, and the merge queue now clippy-checks `car-cli` for Windows.

- Fixed: on Windows, every trajectory append failed with "Access is denied", so `car-memgine`'s trajectory store recorded nothing there and the engine's derived per-tool success rates stayed empty. `File::lock` is `LockFileEx` on Windows, which needs read or write access, and the store opened its day file append-only; it now opens it with read access too. Three Windows-only test failures that assumed a Unix shell (a `#!/bin/sh` uv launcher fixture, the plugin hook's `/bin/sh` fallback, and an unquoted Windows path in a `cd` command) are gated or quoted to match.

See the [release notes][v0.64.0].

## [v0.63.0] — 2026-11-13

### Changes

- An A2UI surface's agent ownership is now checked and changed in one step. Before, two supervised agents creating the same surface at the same moment could both pass the ownership check, leaving one recorded as owner of the other's content, and a host replacing a surface could land between an agent's check and its change, so the agent edited or deleted the host's new surface. Now the second creator is refused, and a host replacement either waits for the agent's change or makes it refused.

- The Node agent loop's chat turns (`runChatTurn`) now run their tools on a real daemon: every proposal carries an id, where a chat turn's had none and the daemon refused it. A `runAgent` or chat run that declares its own `write_file` or `edit_file` tool now registers and runs it; before, the loop registered CAR's built-in file tools first and the daemon refused to let the declared ones replace them.

- A daemon bound to a wildcard address (`--host 0.0.0.0` or `::`) now gives supervised agents `CAR_DAEMON_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` (or `ws://[::1]:<port>`) instead of the wildcard, which is not an address an agent can dial. Any other bind address, the port, and an agent spec's own `CAR_DAEMON_URL` are unchanged.

- Add `host.request_approval` presentation controls: `present: false` keeps an answerable approval row off the phone floor, and `only_if_floor_clear: true` atomically records and returns `floor_busy` without creating or parking a row when a question is current. Both fields are advertised through `capabilities.list`; omitted fields keep existing behavior.

- Held approvals now carry `presented:false` through host replies, lists, snapshots and row events. iOS, Android and macOS keep them answerable in Approvals without notification, sound, banner, new-request activity or attention counts; ordinary and older rows retain their presentation behavior.

- A chat approval row a replaced route kept back, when both its gate outcome and the route's close failed to write, now closes with the gate's outcome when the next route is stopped or replaced again, instead of waiting for a restart to close it `unknown`. Fixes #4303.
- The Claude Code plugin's policy hook now also sees `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `NotebookRead` and `WebSearch`. After a session reads a file that names key material (`~/.ssh/…`, `.aws/credentials`, a `.pem`, by the fragments CAR's risk classifier uses), a later `WebFetch`, `WebSearch` or command the egress inspector flags in that session asks the person first, naming what was read. Each call is still checked on its own as before. Fixes #3367.
- Chat's work panel lists, under Context, the tools the conversation's agent can call: the assistant's current model-visible set, or a saved agent's allowlist. An agent that reports no tools, such as an external CLI, shows none rather than a guess, and no skills or connectors are listed because none is bound to a conversation. Fixes #1761.
- A trajectory record is appended under the file lock, so concurrent writers can no longer split one record across two writes. Fixes #1830.
- `materialize_checkpoint_messages` takes the whole stored checkpoint and the number of earlier messages, and publishes only the turn's own messages, so a later turn can no longer republish the conversation under new identities. Fixes #1870.

- The owner's conversation floor survives long use and storage trouble. A floor that has recorded more than 1,024 finished questions or answers now drops the oldest ones instead of refusing every new question; a question reservation, a new topic or an assistant binding whose save fails is undone instead of being kept in memory (a failed reservation no longer suppresses every later send, and a failed binding no longer leaves the assistant-only gate on); an approval whose question cannot enter the floor is recorded in the floor's refusal log and tried again on the next tick; and a resolve whose floor save fails leaves the pending approval to survive a restart.
- With an assistant selected, `host.request_approval` from an unbound session now requires the host token, so an agent that drops its binding can no longer put an approval on the owner's phone. An `approval_resolved` frame carrying a word the gate never emits is dropped while the turn's acknowledgement is still unread, so Chat and approval history agree.
- `ledger.class.put` and the inline `class` on `ledger.put` keep a stored class's fields the request leaves out (report format, approval rules, skill ids, pass-rate bars) instead of resetting them; a field sent as null is still cleared. `spend.assign_class` enters the decision ledger, and the goal loop adds up each iteration's priced model calls so `max_cost_usd` halts a run.
- `lattice.inbox` acknowledgements may be `{id, from}`, and a bare id that two senders share is refused with their names instead of marking both read. A peer turn past its time limit is answered at once even if its cancel stalls, a flood of peer messages makes at most four busy-answer tasks, and a session that already authenticated as one principal can no longer rebind to another with `session.auth`.
- `car approvals set-tool --as-host` sets an approval unattended on a daemon started in a CAR home of its own, and `car approvals set-tool --standing` lets a person authorize one tool override to be re-applied unattended (`agent_permissions.apply_standing`); a changed schema, a different agent, tool or mode, or a later change by a person ends or refuses the standing authorization.
- A forge write from chat always asks the person, with no trust, full-access or saved answer standing in for the question, and the loop strips a model-supplied approval marker. The read-only git shortcut refuses `--ext-diff` and `--textconv`; listing or printing an archive with `unzip` takes the read-only shortcut; and folder agents read Word, Excel and PowerPoint files with a read-only tool instead of asking.
- Chat and saved agents: saved agents take chat image attachments with the run's first model request, asking chat to change an agent built elsewhere proposes an edit of it, the standing-agent task list ends at the draft, an empty final turn after tool narration ends as an error, an inline `agents.chat` goal no longer records its result against the goal it replaced, and chat's git push and sudo refusals say what to do instead of naming a coder session.
- Smaller fixes: an agent restart refuses a brief whose class policy was edited since it was compiled, removing or re-enrolling a voiceprint drops the cached speaker pipeline, `http_request` flags a body its charset cannot decode as binary, and a failed terminal approval receipt carries the typed `action_failed` cause. Parslee Core no longer states a CAR release its own lookup does not support.

- `capabilities.list` now shows a host session every method it can call, including the agent-role ones it passes as host (`agents.chat`, `agents.start`, `infer`, `runs.list` and the rest). A bound agent's list and an unbound session's list are unchanged: an unbound session is shown `operator` and `operator_only` methods only, whether or not a host token is installed.

- CarHost's Lattice screen is now People. It lists each person once across all of your orgs, with their orgs as tags and a filter when you're in more than one. Each row says only what's true between you: connected, waiting on a reply, not connected (with Connect…), not reachable, or not on CAR yet. Account ids and fingerprints moved under Verify identity on each row. Everything the Lattice screen had, such as connections, invite codes, nearby CARs and attestation notes, is under Connections on the same screen. Saved Tools pins and links to the old screen open People.

- Credential refusal rows stay bounded: each outside credential's refusal file is trimmed to its newest 500 rows once it passes 256 KiB, so a client that keeps sending refused frames cannot grow it without limit (Fixes #3436).
- A signed-in dashboard session reports `caller_role: "dashboard"` in `capabilities.list` (it said `operator`); a `runs.subscribe` stream picks up a key stored after it started within a few seconds, without resubscribing; and a dashboard session reads `host.approvals`, `memory.query` and `a2ui.surfaces` replies with stored keys scrubbed, as it already read run history (Fixes #3675, Fixes #3676).
- A host approval a person resolves now records who resolved it and how the decision arrived (`resolver: { principal, transport }` on the row, stamped by the daemon), and is appended to a private `host-approval-resolutions.jsonl` that outlives the 24-hour in-memory row and a restart; `permission.approve` and `permission.reject` record `conn:<id>@host` instead of a bare connection id (Fixes #3398).
- `car audit export` writes one JSON record of what each agent did and what was approved, by whom and when: the per-client event journals, the `permission.approve` and `permission.reject` decisions, the host approvals with their resolvers, and the policy denials, with run content redacted. It names the earliest record it could read (finished session journals are deleted after 30 days) and each journal's hash-chain status, and works with the daemon down. The same document comes from the new host-only `audit.export` RPC, which refuses an agent-bound session and a daemon with no host token (Fixes #3399).

- The published CLI reference now documents `car board-hook` and `car codex`, which every release since they were added has shipped without.

- Groundwork for pair conversations between colleagues (#4405): CAR has a client for Parslee's conversation store, signed with the device certificate like the relay. Nothing uses it yet, so nothing changes for people or agents in this release.

- Collaboration sealing now follows the spec's answers of 2026-11-12:
  - An agent registration lives as long as the issuer's `exp` allows, inside the delegation window, rather than being refused after 24 hours.
  - For sealed content, a revocation list is fresh exactly while `iat` ≤ now < `exp`. A list dated after the reader's clock no longer counts as fresh.
  - `ReaderContext` takes the org's account directory (`directory`: account to `AccountKind::Person` or `AccountKind::Agent { owner }`), and step 7 decides person or agent from it alone. The following writers now read as unverified: a listed agent with no registration (`registration_missing`), a listed agent whose registration names another owner (`registration_owner`), a listed person carrying a registration (`registration_kind`), and a writer the directory does not list (`not_in_directory`); an unlisted writer is never taken to be a person.
  - New golden vectors cover these cases, and show that a revoked issuer key or credential refuses content the same way a revoked device does.

- Groundwork for sealed collaborations (#4405): CAR implements the content envelope, per-device key copies, key_id and the inner signature from the collaboration sealing spec (docs/proposals/collaboration-sealing.md), with known-answer vectors in car-a2a/tests/fixtures/car-collab/golden.json. Nothing uses it yet, so nothing changes for people or agents in this release.

- `car doctor` now reports how much disk the coder state under the CAR home uses, kept worktrees included, as a size and never a cleanup verdict. If part of it cannot be read, the total is shown as a floor and names what could not be read.

- `gate_flow` now blocks a flow report that is unsafe but names no violation, which is how an evaluator/optimizer boundary with an invalid role assignment reports "nothing was checked"; it used to allow it. A tool listed twice under the same boundary role is now accepted instead of refused as if it held two roles.

- `car run-task` compacts its history from the same measured inputs as the assistant: the tool definitions each request carries and the provider-reported input size of the last call, so a long headless run no longer overruns the model window before compaction starts. Governance benchmark grading now finds a forbidden file whose name has capitals, refuses shell and `edit_file` writes to the credential file as well as `write_file`, and fails the destructive-cleanup task when its artifacts are deleted.

- A restarted daemon now renews its Parslee device certificates without anyone signing in again, so colleagues keep reaching this CAR over the Lattice. At each `car auth login` (CLI and `auth.complete`) CAR registers a fresh per-machine **device key** for that login: an Ed25519 key in `<state root>/login-keys/<account id>.key` (0600, never the OS secret store), registered with the bearer the sign-in just obtained at `POST api/v1/me/device-keys`. The key it replaces is revoked. An unarmed daemon trades a signed assertion from that key for a narrow renewal token through the `jwt-bearer` grant. It uses that token only to renew a certificate Parslee already issued to this device, and never for sync or anything else. If the grant refuses the key (`invalid_grant`), the login waits for the next sign-in rather than retrying. That covers an expired key (30 days idle, 180 days old), a revoked one, or clock skew. A revoke that fails at sign-in or sign-out is recorded, ids only, and retried at that login's next sign-in. Renewal works only for a device and key that Parslee certified in that org within the last 30 days. The first certificate in each org still comes from an interactive sign-in. When renewal is refused for that reason, the org waits for the next sign-in instead of retrying, and `peers.cert_status` gives the reason. It never reads the Keychain to do so, so the demand-driven credential rule still holds. A login with no key behaves as before, and armed passes are unchanged. `car auth logout`, `auth.logout` and `auth.remove_account` revoke the login's key (best effort, under the existing sign-out budget) and delete its file whatever Parslee answers. A failed registration is reported and never fails the sign-in. Until the Parslee authority supports device keys, registration answers 404 and is skipped quietly.

- `car lattice knock --member` without `--device` or `--fingerprint` now reads the org directory fresh and offers the connection to every unexpired device of that colleague. The first device to accept wins, and the other offers are withdrawn on both sides. Before, the knock went to the device with the newest certificate from a cached directory, which could be a machine that was switched off. A message refused across owners now names the cause, such as a personal node that an org session cannot reach, after the usual `peer is outside this work context` prefix. With no device certificate yet, `car lattice directory` says so and gives the command that issues one, instead of pointing at org enroll codes.

- The isolation probe's baseline expects the host-token doors shut on macOS as on Linux, since unwalled Mac agents now start inside the host-token profile, so `hostile_probe_agent_baseline` passes on macOS again. Fixes #4362.
- `scripts/lib/refresh-changed-sources.sh` cleans every real target triple in the shared target, one-hyphen ones such as `wasm32-wasip1` included, so another checkout's cross-target artifacts are never reused. Fixes #4349.

- Mail listings no longer pair one message's Message-ID, subject or sender with another message's row when a message is moved or deleted while the listing runs. Mail.app's property lists are read again until the row ids hold still, and rows are matched by id; a mailbox that keeps changing returns its rows without those fields rather than with another message's.

- New `car lattice org` key-holder commands, so an org's trust root has more
  than one holder and needs no seed file or hand-run tool: `create --org <org>`
  starts an org's org scope with your login-derived granter key (an Owner or
  Admin; refused when the org already has org scope on this CAR),
  `granter-key --org <org>` prints your login-derived granter key for another
  key holder, `add-granter` / `remove-granter --org <org> <key>` let a current
  key holder change the set (never to empty) and print the new enrollment code,
  and `grant --org <org> [--confirm <account>:<fingerprint>...] [--epoch N]
  [--rekey]` hands the org key to the members you confirm by the org-key
  fingerprint they read you, every member whose CAR you attested, and
  yourself; a fingerprint that does not match refuses the grant. The first four need no
  running daemon; `grant` is the new host-only daemon method
  `lattice.org.grant`. None of them prints the passphrase or a seed.
  `docs/ORG_SCOPE_TURN_ON_RUNBOOK.md` now walks through these commands.
- `car lattice org status` and `enroll-code` now open sync and the
  configured orgs first when org scope is configured (`lattice.org.status`
  `open: true`), so a member who just joined sees the org and their
  `org_key_fingerprint` instead of "not enabled". Host apps' polls do not
  send it and open nothing.

- A second device of the same owner no longer needs an enrollment code to get
  org scope. A device that holds org scope announces its granter sets on the
  owner's personal oplog, which is end-to-end encrypted under the sync
  passphrase. On `sync.pump`, each of the owner's other devices adopts an org
  it has no scope for, provided every announcing device agrees and the
  signed-in login belongs to that org. Adoption never replaces a configured or
  adopted entry. When devices disagree, nothing is adopted, and
  `lattice.org.status` lists the fingerprints under
  `from_own_devices.conflicts`. An adopted org opens at the next daemon start
  (`restart_required`). It is kept in `<journal dir>/sync/org-scope-adopted.json`
  and merged into `PARSLEE_SYNC_ORG_SCOPE` for orgs that value does not name.
  A member's first device still joins with `car lattice org join`. Device
  certificates play no part in this.

- Org-scope sync now opens each configured org as the signed-in login that
  belongs to it, not only the login present when the daemon started. An org
  held by a second login (`car auth login --add`) opens under that login's own
  relay bearer, passphrase-derived org keys and login-derived granter key, and
  `lattice.org.*` with `org` acts as that login. An org that no held login
  belongs to (or that several other logins belong to) now stays closed on its
  own, reported in `lattice.org.status` and `sync.pump` `org_error`, where it
  used to stop org scope for every org and fall back to the local journal.
  Signing a login out closes the orgs it serves until a login serves them
  again. Org scope announced on a second login's personal oplog is adopted by
  that login's other devices.

- `runAgent` / `run_agent` now refuse a resume whose `priorMessages` / `prior_messages` exceed 15 MiB, with an error naming the limit, before sending anything. Before, a resume past the daemon's 16 MiB WebSocket frame dropped the connection and the run ended without an outcome.

- A Claude Code or Codex session started plainly with the CAR plugin is now a
  full collaboration session, not only one started with `car claude` /
  `car codex`. `car peer-inbox-hook` and `car board-hook` find the session they
  run in by walking up to the nearest enrolled assistant process (both routes
  record its pid in `<CAR_HOME>/run/<id>.pid`), so the inbox nudge reads that
  session's pending count — which its collaboration server now keeps in
  `run/<id>.pending` — and the board briefing leaves out the session's own
  edits. `car session-release` removes the pending file too.
- Every coding-assistant session now joins its project on the Lattice by
  itself once attached, so another owner's `agents:<project>` share includes it
  without the model calling `lattice_join`. The project is the name of the
  session's repository's main checkout, so a session in a linked worktree or a
  subdirectory joins the same project as one at the root; outside a repository
  it is the directory's name. `car codex` names its project by the same rule
  (before, the directory's own name, so a session in a worktree-pool slot
  joined `slot-N`). Supervised CAR agents join nothing by themselves.

- `car policy-check-hook` has an opt-in strict mode for unattended agents: with `CAR_POLICY_HOOK_STRICT=1` a call it cannot check, or one in a directory no `.car/policies/` covers, is denied with the reason. `CAR_POLICY_HOOK_ROOT=<dir>` pins where rules are read from. The default stays open and now notes on stderr when no CAR policy applies.

- A hard link to a protected file is now caught however deep inside a protected folder the file sits; the check used to stop four folders down.

- The CAR docs bundled in the Python wheel (ASSISTANT.md and MCP.md) now name the version they describe, 0.62.0, instead of 0.61.2.

- `registerAgentBasics(root)` / `register_agent_basics(root=...)` / `agents.register_basics { root }` can now keep the daemon's built-in `write_file` and `edit_file` inside an absolute folder: a write that resolves outside it, through `..` or a symlink, is refused naming the root, and writes inside it work. With no root the tools behave as before, and the binding docs now say what that is: they run as the daemon user on the daemon host, follow symlinks, and are admitted at the session's default tier with no prompt.

- On macOS, `scripts/cargo-shared-target.sh` now marks the Cargo target directory `.metadata_never_index` before each build, so Spotlight stops indexing build churn (it had held `mds` above 100% CPU and slowed Mail search).

- A Claude or Codex session's pending-message count no longer goes back to an older org-inbox count when a background poll answers after a drain that started later. Moving a scheduled task onto the run recorder during reconcile now changes the stored task record under its lock, so a run that fired meanwhile keeps its record.

- `submitProposal` / `submit_proposal` now take the same per-runtime lock as `executeProposal` / `execute_proposal`, so mixing the two on one runtime no longer lets one call's tool requests reach the other's handler. On Node, a `submitProposal` after an `executeProposal` also reinstalls its tool bridge, which the earlier call had removed.

- `car-runtime` fetches its native artifacts once when several processes use it for the first time together, such as a worker pool or a test runner. Each download goes to a file of its own and is renamed into place only when complete and executable, so no process fails over another's download or loads a half-written `car-server`. The other processes wait for the one install, and a lock left by an exited process is taken over. Fixes #4296.
- The integration-test guard that keeps a test's `ServerState` off the developer's real CAR state reads test files as Rust tokens. A renamed import (`use ... ServerState as State`), a `type` alias, a line break after `ServerState::`, a call inside a macro and the `<ServerState>::` form are all caught, and a constructor named in a comment or a string is not. Fixes #4309.
- Fixtures that model a chat a host started now say `host_started: true`, as production records it, and the proxied-chat fixture is checked against the arrival check `agents.invoke_external` applies. Fixes #2457.
- car-server-core's integration test suites leave nothing in `$TMPDIR`. A journal a daemon task writes after its test ends, the run store's index beside it, the suites' own CAR homes and what a daemon's child processes write to a temporary directory now live under a scratch root removed when the test binary exits. Fixes #3062.

- The worktree hook's sh fallback now refuses hook input whose closing bracket does not match its opener (an object closed by `]`), as the Rust hook does, instead of reading it as valid.

- In a repo that turns the worktree pool on, an agent's own `git worktree add` (through Claude Code's Bash tool) is now logged to the pool's `direct-add.log` by default. With `direct_add = "refuse"` in `.car/worktree-pool.toml` it is refused with a pointer to `car worktree acquire`. `CAR_WORKTREE_DIRECT_ADD=off` turns the check off. Repos with the pool off are unchanged.

See the [release notes][v0.63.0].

## [v0.62.0] — 2026-11-11

### Changes

- `car doctor` now checks the CAR plugin as Claude Code and Codex install it. It reports a `car` marketplace that is not pinned to the running release, one on a local folder that no longer exists, and a plugin that is missing or disabled. `car update` and `car doctor --repair` re-pin a marketplace that already follows `Parslee-ai/car`, or points at a vanished folder, to the release now installed, then install and enable the plugin. A marketplace on your own checkout or fork is reported with the exact commands and is never replaced. Before this, upgrading CAR left both assistants on whatever plugin they were first installed from, so sessions could miss the work board entirely.

- Two `car install` runs whose agent ids differ only in letter case, started together, can no longer both pass the case check and write the same binary on a case-insensitive Mac disk: the check, the folder and the write now happen under one lock on the agents folder, so one installs and the other is refused. A spend ledger removed and made again at the same path in one process now syncs its new directory entry on its first append. Fixes #3680.
- The assistant's local Calendar, Mail and Notes tools now follow their macOS permission while it runs. Grant Mail access, and the next chat turn can use the Mail tools and shows the Mail starter chips, with no restart. Revoke it, and the tools and chips leave without a restart. The chips refresh each time Chat comes forward, checking every app at once and answering within 0.7 seconds, and what that check finds is what the next turn uses, so a revoke made just before returning to Chat drops the chips and the next turn's tools at once. An app that takes longer than 0.7 seconds to answer keeps its earlier chips in that refresh; its new answer reaches the next turn and the next time Chat comes forward. Otherwise a turn reuses one check for up to 15 seconds, so a revoke made inside that window reaches turns once a newer check answers or the window ends. Each check is the same non-prompting status read as before, so a turn never raises a consent prompt and a wedged app slows at most one turn in 15 seconds. The note naming tools left out because an app did not answer now changes with them, turn by turn. Fixes #1711.
- A strict assistant model pinned by its display name (in any letter case) or its untagged `:latest` alias now runs in process like the same model pinned by its id, so a remote provider's credential error keeps its recovery steps instead of arriving as plain text through the daemon. A supervised agent's remote calls still go through the daemon. Fixes #1859.
- Quitting `car code`'s board no longer closes the discussion it was in. It detaches, so a reply CarHost or another terminal has running in the same conversation goes on, and that client can keep sending. The daemon still closes a discussion once nothing is attached and it has been idle for an hour, and `x` still closes one on purpose. The protocol docs now say plainly that every operator client may read, send into and close any operator discussion. Fixes #2153.
- `car code` no longer looks hung while it waits. Every 30 seconds it prints to stderr which phase it is in and how long that phase and the whole wait have run (`still waiting: enumerating for 2m10s (this wait 5m02s)`). After 45 seconds with nothing at all from the daemon, the line says the CAR service has not answered and that it is still waiting. While watching a session it also reads the session's recorded state once a minute, so a session that ended without its event reaching the CLI is reported within a minute instead of at the next request. The wait itself is unchanged: only the daemon's silence and no-progress rules end it. Fixes #2469.
- `car codex` keeps the developer instructions you pass with `-c developer_instructions=...` (also as `--config`, and after `exec`). They outrank your config.toml and your profile's `<name>.config.toml`, as in Codex itself, and CAR's brief is appended to them instead of replacing them. A value that is TOML but not a string is refused, as Codex refuses it. A named profile (`-p <name>`) no longer stops `car codex` at the hook-trust check, because that check no longer hands `--profile` to `codex app-server`, which refuses it. A profile whose file declares `hooks` is refused with a message, because CAR's trust check cannot list those hooks. Fixes #4102.
- A Claude or Codex session supervised by CAR no longer loses track of a colleague's message that arrives while its org inbox is being polled. The waiting-message count the Stop hook reads is now written with the live queue as it stands at that moment, so a count read before the message arrived can no longer overwrite the newer one. A pending file that cannot be written is reported on stderr and in `collaboration_status` (`pending_file_error`) instead of being ignored. Fixes #3484.
- A CAR client that starts the daemon for a `CAR_DAEMON_URL` on an IPv4 loopback other than `127.0.0.1` (such as `ws://127.0.0.2:9100`) now starts it on that address. It used to start it on `127.0.0.1` and then fail to reach it. `car-host` launches it the same way. `localhost` and `::1` are unchanged. On macOS only `127.0.0.1` is configured on `lo0` by default, so the daemon can bind another loopback address only after an alias is added (`sudo ifconfig lo0 alias 127.0.0.2`); without one it fails to start with "Can't assign requested address". The CarHost app's own bundled daemon still binds `127.0.0.1`. Fixes #2846.
- Documentation now matches what CAR does: a second daemon sharing one `CAR_HOME` exits before it adopts state or listens (it does not run as a non-primary); the auth-token path list includes the `CAR_HOME` location; no HTTP route serves the daemon or host token; the `CAR_DAEMON_URL` helper's reach is stated (commands with `--url` use that flag, `car ui` uses `--port`); the CLI's usage examples, the agent authoring guide's CLI section (there is a `car registry` and a CLI reference; `car daemon` runs car-server as a child and waits), the meeting bot's smoke test (no sample recording ships), CarHost's README and app comment (no App Intents types are declared), its Settings captions (the log level is saved but not applied yet; Reveal always opens `~/.car/`) and the `health.*` namespace (the person's health data, not daemon liveness). Fixes #3939.
- `car doctor` with several problems that `--repair` does not fix (a drifted client library and a misnamed provider key, say) now lists each one's own remedy instead of closing with "Re-run with `--repair`", which would fix neither. Fixes #3925.
- `car doctor` and `car speech doctor` no longer print the model registry's load warnings (such as "ignoring signed overlay that names different weights for a compiled builtin") ahead of their report: they read like problems doctor found, and nothing in the report referred to them. Other warnings still show, and `RUST_LOG` still overrides. Fixes #3881.
- A connection whose repeat `server.handshake` is refused is no longer still authorized by its earlier successful one: the refusal clears its negotiated protocol and capabilities, so protected methods are refused until a handshake succeeds again. `car doctor` no longer closes every refused agent handshake with "update its car-runtime package"; it points to the per-agent advice above, which says whether the client, the daemon or the request is the side to fix. Fixes #3652.
- Signing out of Parslee (`car auth logout`, or `auth.logout` through the daemon) now asks each signed-in login's issuer (with or without a current organization membership) to revoke this device's certificate before its bearer is discarded, and removing one login (`auth.remove_account`) revokes that login's only. The revokes run at once and are given 8 seconds together, so a sign-out never waits longer whatever the number of logins. A revoke that cannot go through, offline, refused or unanswered, is shown as a warning (`warnings` in the reply, a line on stderr for the CLI, and under the account in the CarHost app) and the sign-out still happens; such a certificate expires within 12 hours. Fixes #4155.
- On the Mac, an agent the wall does not confine can no longer present the host key. Every such agent except CAR's own assistant now starts under a Seatbelt profile that denies reading or writing the host-token files (the Application Support copy and the state root's `run/host-token`) and any file beside them whose name starts with theirs, and the folders above them cannot be renamed. The daemon writes the token through a fresh, exclusively created temporary file, so a link planted beside it never receives the token. Such an agent also cannot start a program outside the profile: opening an app or document through LaunchServices (`open`), submitting a launchd job and sending Apple Events to another app are refused, as they already are under the full wall. The daemon also no longer hands such an agent `CAR_HOST_TOKEN`. So `env -u CAR_AGENT_ID -u CAR_AGENT_TOKEN car ... --as-host`, the interactive host prompt and a plain `cat` all fail from inside one, as on Linux. Nothing else changes about how these agents run: the auth token, their own files, the programs they start themselves and the network work as before, except a setuid program such as `/bin/ps`, which macOS does not run inside a Seatbelt profile at all (Neo reads processes through psutil, which works). An agent that applies its own macOS sandbox cannot nest it inside this profile. Fixes #3706.
- A scheduled command task whose start cannot be recorded (a full disk, a read-only task folder) no longer runs: the recorder fails and says why, so every run that happened has a start record. The daemon's own interval timer records a start the same way before it runs a command. Every writer of a task record (a run, a refused firing, a timer run, a dream pass, `scheduler.run`, an agent schedule's install) now writes under the record's lock against a fresh read, so two writers that overlap each keep their run count and their execution in its history, instead of the later save erasing the earlier. `car doctor` no longer reads healthy when the task store cannot be read: whether the schedules run is then unknown, and it counts as a problem. Fixes #3496.
- The CI guard that keeps `car doctor` from calling CAR's own state "not written by this version" now also catches entries CarHost (the Mac app) creates in `CAR_HOME`, names built with `format!` (checked by their literal prefix and suffix; one with no literal prefix fails), and names whose file-or-directory kind the scan cannot read, which must now be declared instead of passing against either of doctor's lists. Fixes #3882.
- `car models update-policy <policy>` reads the policy in force back after saving yours. When a project `.car/update-prefs.json` where the CAR service runs overrides it, the command now fails and names the policy actually in force, instead of printing your choice as though maintenance followed it. Fixes #2737.
- `car worktree` claims are safer on the Mac. A lease now records which `car worktree acquire` wrote it (`claim=<pid>@<start>`, after the fields v2 reads), so two acquires from one session are told apart, and a slot taken from an acquire while it was being prepared is no longer handed out to it.
