A `ready=0` lease whose acquire has stopped is given back and claimed again by that holder's next acquire, and `release` frees it without `--force`; one whose acquire may still be running is still waited for. `reclaim`, `acquire` and `clean` no longer trust an `lsof` scan that failed (exited non-zero) or listed nothing: whether someone works in a slot is then unknown, and the slot is left as it is. As before, the scan sees your own processes (setuid ones such as `login` aside), not other users'. Fixes #3732 for macOS (the Linux `/proc` scan is #4054).
- `car worktree release` says what it compared. "Not leased" now names the lease it looked for and the pool it looked in (and, with no leases folder, suggests the slot may belong to another repository's pool), and says a lease also ends when a reclaim frees it after its holder process ends. "Leased by X, not you" now names the identity it compared you as. Fixes #4086.
- The plugin's sh fallback for the worktree hook (used when `car` is missing or too old) bounds its fetch even when `git` on PATH is a wrapper script: the timeout now ends the fetch's whole process tree, transport included, instead of finding no `git` process and waiting for the network. A hook killed in the middle of that cleanup no longer leaves the fetch's processes stopped. Fixes #3742.
- `car worktree status` no longer hides slots after the pool size is lowered. A slot above the new size that still has a folder or a lease is listed and marked `(above size N)`, with its holder, so a leased slot-5 in a pool cut to 2 is still seen. `car worktree clean --apply` also archives a worktree whose folder name git refuses in a tag (for example one with `~` or `:`): the archive name keeps only characters every git ref accepts. Fixes #3736 and #3838.
- `car worktree status` no longer calls a slot free when git no longer knows its folder as a worktree. It reports the slot as unusable, as `car worktree acquire` treats it, and says how to recover: remove the folder if nothing in it is needed, and acquire recreates the slot. Fixes #3733.

- The `car-runtime` npm package no longer depends on npm running its install script. npm 11 warns that the script is "not yet covered by allowScripts", and `--ignore-scripts` skips it. In both cases the first `require('car-runtime')` or `car-server` now fetches the matching `.node` module and `car-server` binary itself, with progress on stderr, and honours `CAR_RUNTIME_DOWNLOAD_BASE` and `CAR_RUNTIME_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1`. To keep the download at install time, approve it once per project with `npm install-scripts approve car-runtime`.

- Chat approval history now shows what the agent's gate actually decided. A Command Deck click, or an iMessage or Slack reply, no longer marks a chat approval approved before the gate records it, so a decision the gate could not record reads as denied in both places (car#1930). iMessage and Slack replies to a chat approval now reach the waiting turn instead of only the history. If the turn ends after a decision was sent but before the agent confirmed it, the row reads "outcome unknown". Agents declare this with `approval_frames: true` in their `agent.chat` acknowledgement; `car do --serve` does.
- A finished browser sign-in now always retries a device certificate that failed for lack of a credential, `lattice.knock` says why a certificate is missing and what fixes it, an organization directory with every held org unavailable lists them instead of failing, and a revoked or conflicting device key is told to re-key rather than refresh, in `car auth status` too (car#3477).
- `browser_await_signin` with no `success_url_contains` starts only on a page whose path is a login step (`/login`, `/oauth2/authorize`, `/saml2`); a login word in the query, fragment, host or inside a longer word no longer qualifies a page whose later navigation would read as signed in. A sign-in that starts on an SSO host's root, such as `sso.example.com/`, now needs `success_url_contains` (car#2694).
- Chat can run `gh repo list`, and a refused forge write in Chat or `car do` tells you to run it yourself instead of naming a coder merge step (car#2369).

- CI: when a hosted Linux runner cannot resolve the Azure Ubuntu mirror (`azure.archive.ubuntu.com`), the system-dependency install adds public DNS resolvers and, if the name still does not resolve, uses the first Ubuntu mirror whose host does (archive.ubuntu.com, then mirrors on other domains), instead of failing every job at `apt-get update` as during the 2026-11-11 DNS outage. With no mirror reachable it fails naming DNS.

- `car code`'s independent audit reads the auditor's last answer whatever its wrapping. A clean draft in a fenced block no longer wins over a later bare correction that reports a defect, and a bare draft no longer wins over a later fenced revision. Fixes #2682.
- Self-healing stops working an organization's repositories as soon as its `[[org]]` entry is removed. The detector's hand-off drops them at once, and removing every entry clears the discovered list and its status. One owner's listing now reads up to 100,000 repositories instead of 4,000. Fixes #3804.
- A foreman worker that commits its work between two progress samples is no longer stopped as making no progress: the supervision fingerprint now includes the HEAD commit. When the watchdog stops a headless `car code` build loop, its terminal record keeps the iterations the loop had started instead of 0. Fixes #2002.
- The self-heal detector hands a detection to the repair loop only through an issue that loop will pick up. An open issue that carries the detection's marker but not the loop's label is no longer adopted, which left the detection with no owner; a labelled issue is filed for it instead. Fixes #3799.
- Self-healing records an item as handed to a person only once the hand-off landed. A label edit, comment or approval card that failed (an expired GitHub login) is tried again on the item's next failure, instead of leaving it never escalated. An approved escalation card whose run cannot start (its repository left `heal.toml`, a setup error) is kept for the next tick instead of being dismissed with only a log line. Fixes #3802.
- `heal.status` no longer reports edited `[unattended]` models as the ones the running cadence uses. The cadence keeps the models it started with until the daemon restarts; `running_unattended` names them, and `car heal status` prints them when `heal.toml` now resolves to others. Fixes #3830.
- `selfheal.dismiss` no longer waits behind a hanging notification command. A self-heal tick delivers gave-up notifications outside the lock that dismissals take, so a dismissal returns at once and delivery finishes on its own. Fixes #3876.
- A self-heal notification command whose program path contains the value of a `*SECRET*` or `*KEY*` environment variable is no longer refused as leaking a secret. The program is the executable the operator configured; its arguments are still refused when they carry a stored secret. Fixes #3872.
- The self-heal detection ledger (`selfheal/detections.jsonl`) no longer holds values from CAR's secret store. Its redactor hid only values whose variable name looks secret (`*KEY*`, `*TOKEN*`), so a stored value named, say, `SLACK_WEBHOOK` reached a persisted row; every value this daemon has read from the store, through the resolver or directly (a supervised agent's secret), is now redacted whatever its name or length, wherever it appears, and every value a rotated secret has had is kept. Fixes #3870.
- `car code`'s verifier can no longer grade an outcome PASS on a contract check that failed. A cited `run_check` probe must have met its check's own assertions (exit status, `output_contains`, no timeout), as the builder's gate judges it; a plain shell probe may still expect a non-zero exit. Part of #2084 (rest: car#4232, car#4284).
- `car code`'s verifier runs, for an outcome, only the contract check that outcome was frozen with. Another approved check, however green, is refused before it runs, so its passing probe can no longer certify an outcome it does not test. An outcome whose own check is not approved cannot be backed by another. Part of #2142 (rest: car#4284).
- A `car code` contract whose every check the runtime denies no longer counts as a pass. A supplied contract left with nothing to run now fails at start with `no check is left to run`, naming the held checks, as a derived one already ended asking for an executable check; an empty contract was read as green, delivering work no check looked at. Fixes #3868.
- A `car code` check counts as asserting its claimed output only when its command is, as a whole, an assertion. Every command in it must be simple, with no `;`, `&`, `||`, `#`, newline, subshell, heredoc, `$(` or backtick outside quotes. Its first word must be `grep`, `rg`, `diff` or `cmp`, `test` or `[` with a `$(…)` inside a double-quoted argument (`test "$(cmd)" = ok`; single-quoted text is literal), or an inline program that compares a value in an `assert` (`python3 -c`, with only `-I`, `-B`, `-E`, `-s` or `-S` before `-c`, `node -e`, `ruby -e`, `perl -e`, or such a command through `sh -c`); or it is a pipeline whose last stage is `grep`, `rg`, `diff` or `cmp` (`python3 greet.py | grep -F Hello`). Text the command prints, a comparison only in the assertion's message, and one only in a single- or double-quoted string of the program do not count, and an inline program with a `#` is not counted. A check such as `cd dir && grep …` is no longer counted as asserting output: write it as one command or a pipeline, or use `output_contains`. Fixes #3810.
- A `car code` check no longer runs on a half-seeded cache. When a cloned cache root fails and its partial copy cannot be removed, the check is refused as an infrastructure failure instead of running with the partial root in place. Fixes #2262.
- When `car code`'s verifier grades an outcome UNPROVEN with a prerequisite missing the field its kind takes (`{"kind":"Tool"}` with no `binary`), the refusal now names that field and the exact shape to send, instead of a bare decode error. The tool schema stays flat, which every provider accepts. Fixes #2141.
- When a Build an Agent folder agent's working folder is deleted after its build, verification and a scenario rerun (`declagents.run_scenarios`) no longer recreate it empty and fail the agent's scenarios against missing inputs. The re-run ends as an infrastructure failure naming the missing folder. Fixes #2800.
- Two `coder.projects.create` calls for the same project at once no longer race on its `project.json`. Creation takes a per-project lock, so the second call opens the project the first one made instead of overwriting it, and both answer with the kind on disk. Fixes #3611.
- A daemon that restarts under a crashed daemon's process id no longer keeps and reuses that run's stale multiplayer builder home. Contract-run labels carry a per-process nonce, and boot cleanup keeps a home with its own pid only when the nonce is its own; an unreadable cache entry is now logged instead of skipped. Fixes #3558.
- A `car code` check that needs approved credentials no longer runs on a Docker or VM substrate and then fails on a missing variable. It is refused before it runs, naming the credentials and saying they stay on this Mac. Fixes #2044.
- A `car code` session pinned to a key-based provider's model (an API key or bearer token) with no key set no longer pauses waiting for a Parslee sign-in that cannot fix it. It ends as a missing key, naming the variable to set. Fixes #3924.
- On macOS, a `car code` check is refused before it runs when a credential file its sandbox hides by name has a second hard link, which would still read the real contents, as the assistant shell already refuses. Fixes #2857.
- A finished `car code` session whose worktree could not be removed when it ended no longer keeps that worktree forever. Past the two-hour age floor, the daemon's sweep tries the removal again, once per pass. A workspace kept on purpose (`keep_workspace_on_failure`, keep-on-cancel, a discussion, or one a restart interrupted) is never touched. Fixes #2332.
- Talking a task through in `car code` (`discuss.start`), the `route_split` planner, the self-heal review panel and MCP assistant runs no longer download a local model nobody asked for. Each call routes only to a model that is ready, or ends naming the `car models pull` command, as saved-agent runs and coder sessions already do. Fixes #3883.
- An outcome check is refused as broken quoting only when a quote in its command never closes. Adjacent quoting is valid shell and now runs: `printf a''b`, `'a'b'c'`, and an empty `''` glued to text, which was refused before; a quote character inside a `#` comment or a heredoc's body is text, and only a heredoc that never reaches its delimiter line is refused. A check whose test prints a Python "No module named" line for a module the command does not name stays a red test instead of a check that cannot run. Fixes #3807.
- A `car code` check that waited less than a second for the protected Cargo home's lock now has that wait taken out of its time limit, rounded up, and a timeout after any such wait is booked as starved rather than a red verdict on the work. A scenario folder over the copy budget now says it holds more than 1000 files, folders and links, since links count too. Fixes #3693.
- A `car code` check pass whose evidence folder cannot be created runs no check and passes none; each check reads as an infrastructure failure that names the folder. Two checks whose names sanitize to the same folder name (`a/b`, `a:b`) now get separate evidence folders. A sanitized name keeps the full hash of the original, and a name with a capital letter is hashed too, so distinct names never share a folder, even on a case-insensitive disk, and a name that was already a safe folder name is unchanged. A baseline that ran in a removed pristine copy records no folder, so its rerun line no longer starts in one that is gone. A noisy check's output is bounded in memory at the evidence cap instead of growing until the check ends. A redirect whose path holds a variable anywhere, such as `> out/$X`, is refused like one that starts with it. Fixes #2003.
- On macOS, a `car code` check, whether the builder's or the verifier's, can no longer write anywhere in the shared `/tmp`, `/var/tmp` or per-user temp folder, where it could overwrite another program's predictable temp file. It can still write the names that tools ignoring TMPDIR create there: bash here-document spools and `mktemp` files and folders, plus Swift Build's temp folders. A check that writes a fixed name such as `/tmp/foo` now fails, and its output names the path and says to write under `$TMPDIR` instead. Fixes #2121.
- The daemon's stall watchdog can no longer cancel a `car code` session as stalled when progress arrives between its last liveness check and the cancel: progress is stamped either before that check, where it is seen, or after the cancel. A native turn that hits the session deadline while the worktree already passes the contract now ends green with a note, instead of also reporting the timeout as an error and a budget exhaustion. An in-flight native turn ends at the session's real deadline, not up to a second past it. Fixes #1641.
- A `car code` session whose model keeps proposing a tool call that is refused before it runs (an approval denied, a policy denial) now stops as idle after three such iterations, as one proposing nothing does. Only a call that ran counts as activity. A baseline check whose own program is missing (`pnpm: command not found` for `pnpm test`) is reported as unable to run at any exit status a wrapper gives it, while a helper missing inside a script it runs stays an ordinary red check. Fixes #2035.
- The daemon now boots when the self-heal ledger (`<CAR_HOME>/selfheal/detections.jsonl`) ends in a partly written row, which a crash in the middle of an append leaves, or holds a row of a kind a newer build wrote. Each such row is skipped with a warning. A partly written last row is copied to `detections.jsonl.torn-<time>` and cut from the ledger, and a whole last row missing its newline gets one, so the next record does not join it and the next boot still loads. A malformed row elsewhere in the file still stops the boot, as corruption. Fixes #3850.
- A refused `[selfheal] notification_command` is now shown by `car selfheal status` and `car info` (and `selfheal.status`'s new `notification_refusal_reason`), not only in the daemon log. A TOML syntax error elsewhere in `<CAR_HOME>/config.toml` is reported as the file's, with its line, instead of being blamed on the setting. An empty argument (`args = [""]`) is refused. A key under `[selfheal]` nothing reads, such as `notifcation_command`, is named in the new `config_warnings` instead of silently meaning "not set". Fixes #3871.

- The `car ui` dashboard now shows the decision ledger. A feed lists one day's entries newest first, each with what was done, why, its class, the rung that decided it, an evidence link, its undo (or "cannot be undone") and its grade state; a Good given by seven days of silence is shown apart from a clicked Good. Good, Wrong and Undo are one click each, with an optional note, and the entry updates from the ledger's own answer. An autonomy view shows each class's rung, clean streak, clicked-grade count, pass rate against its bar and the change that last moved it, and marks a class that dropped a rung in the last 24 hours. A standup panel shows the four numbers (handled without you, needed you, out of the loop by class, agents working now) counted the way the assistant's morning standup counts them.
- A decision class may carry `standup_reports` (`stored`, `learned` or `source_health`), set through `ledger.class.put` or `ledger.put`'s `class` and returned by `ledger.classes.list`. It marks a class whose entries the owner's standup reports as records, not decisions; absent means a decision class, and older class records keep working. The dashboard's standup numbers count decision entries only: an entry in a class carrying `standup_reports` is a record and is left out of handled, needed and the out-of-the-loop share, read from this field alone, so the numbers come from CAR's own records and match the assistant's standup. Each entry counts by the first of nine rules it matches, read from the entry and its class record alone: a record, an attempt mark (an id ending `:live` or `:failed`), the owner's approval record (an id containing `:approved:`) and a deadline default's record (an id ending `:deadline_default`) count nowhere; a class-setup entry, a refusal and an entry whose `dispatch_state` is `failed` are handled; an entry decided at `ask_first` or `draft`, or tagged `[keenan-rung: ...]`, is needed; anything else is handled. So a decision the owner approved counts once, as needed, and once as handled if its dispatch failed.
- A note typed on a ledger entry now survives the dashboard's 30-second re-read, with its cursor, and is sent with the grade.
- The signed-in dashboard may call `ledger.list`, `ledger.classes.list`, `ledger.rung_changes.list` and `ledger.grade`; its grades must say `source: "dashboard"`. `ledger.rung_changes.list` now also returns `grade_record: {entry_id, kind, source, at}` on a change a grade caused.

- `car auth login` now registers your flagship assistant as your agent in Parslee, in every organization you belong to, and publishes a card listing the tools it can offer, so each organization can see every member's flagship and what it does even while that machine is offline. Each machine gets its own key for the agent, kept as a file under `~/.car/agent-keys`. `car agent publish` repeats it on demand, for example after joining an organization or updating CAR. Until the Parslee backend supports agent accounts, both say so and change nothing. Design and wire contract: `docs/proposals/agent-accounts.md`.

- A damaged `declagents.json` no longer makes a host's fleet inventory read as full with no built agents. The inventory now says `fidelity: "partial"`, with `error` naming the file, so peers and `car fleet` treat the empty list as unknown rather than none (car#2666).

- The git, gh and glab commands CAR starts, and the programs it starts for a workspace (a coding agent, a supervised agent, a foreman verify command, a subprocess tool or MCP server, a substrate command line, a benchmark grade command, builder shells and unprotected contract checks), no longer follow an inherited GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, index or object-store redirect into another repository: the work board and fleet, the registry publish command, the worktree pool, the coder's merge and self-heal `gh` calls, the code-task default-branch lookup, and the test fixtures. A builder shell started by a daemon that has `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` exported (a bare-repo dotfiles setup, say) no longer sees them; set them in the command itself, where they still apply. The daemon, the MCP server and every `car` subcommand except `car claude` and `car codex` also drop the redirects from their own environment at startup, so no child can inherit one; the two session launchers keep a `GIT_DIR` you exported for your own session. A source check in car-fleet (`every_git_command_clears_inherited_repository_redirects`) fails on a literal git, gh or glab spawn that does not clear them, and a second (`every_program_helper_clears_inherited_repository_redirects`) fails when one of the helpers above stops clearing; neither can see a spawn that is neither (car#4115, car#2130). A task the scheduler's recorder runs (`run_recorded`, also reached through the FFI scheduler) and the replay freeze hook's Python launcher drop those variables themselves, so they hold when a library or test calls them without a binary's startup having run.

- Model catalog and wire schema: catalog rows without a drafter, run count or spread now validate against the published schema; a suggested model upgrade keeps every ability the installed model has; the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B vLLM-MLX row fits a 64 GB Mac under the everyday policy, and `car models recommend` names the policy ceiling a model is over and each one's estimated peak.
- Model loading and routing: a null or empty chat template is repaired, and a failed template download stops the load with its cause; a routed stream never goes to a Codex CLI model; a structured-output stream to the Codex subscription is refused before any credential lookup; a current model is never redirected to a deprecated MLX twin; Private Cloud Compute availability follows Apple Account sign-in and sign-out without a restart; a uv launcher whose Python was removed is noticed.
- Spend and cost: a stream reset after its request was sent, a 2xx whose body does not parse, and a refusal are charged what was billed, including a refusal from the Parslee gateway, the ChatGPT Codex backend or an Anthropic stream; `InferenceError::ContentRefused` gains a public `usage: Option<TokenUsage>` field, so code outside CAR that builds that variant must set it. OpenRouter calls and their late cost lookups reach the right URL for every base shape (`…/api`, `…/api/v1`, the full chat URL), and a lookup stays with its own call; the default ElevenLabs voice is priced at $0.04 per 1,000 characters; `events.cost_by_agent` keeps unknown costs unknown, shows subscription calls apart and lists unattributed calls on their own line. The dashboard and CarHost show the estimated cost of each agent and of the operator (calls from a connection bound to no agent), in total and per run: CAR's estimate from list prices and reported tokens, not the bill. The spend ledger records each call's run.
- Sub-agent cost: `multi.run_agent` callbacks carry a `callback_id` that clients pass on their `infer` calls, so overlapping sub-agent runs are each credited only their own calls. When a client does not tag its calls and two callbacks overlap, the runs' self-reports are kept and listed apart (`ambiguous_reports`, `ambiguous_reported_cost_usd` on `events.cost_by_agent`), never added to the measured total, so two calls count as two. The daemon keeps them beside each payer's spend ledger, so the dashboard and CarHost show them as their own line.
- Local workers: MLX's buffer cache is bounded and cleared after each request, and a worker reports at least what MLX holds for its process, so admission's charge covers it (with several models resident, each is charged that figure: an over-charge, never an under-charge); an external grade that cannot be saved is taken back; a part-list message keeps its text on the managed text-only lane; the self-harness scores the candidate prompt on tasks without tools.

- The Release workflow now refuses a `promote_tag` recovery dispatch started by Link's GitHub App (`parslee-car-link[bot]`), as actor or rerunner, before any job publishes. `build.yml` names that login once, in a workflow-level env, so the existing guard in `lab-mode` is live without the `CAR_LINK_GITHUB_ACTOR` repository variable. Dispatches by a person or the release lab App run as before.

- A Claude Code or Codex session started plainly (`claude`, `codex`) can now use the CAR work board, peer messaging and Lattice tools through the CAR plugin, without `car claude` or `car codex`. When the plugin's collaboration server starts with no supervised credentials, it runs `car session-enroll`. That command binds the work context `car auth resolve` names for the session's directory, so a repository's declared org applies, and enrolls the same per-session agent `car claude` does. The server removes the agent when it exits. The session-start briefing in such a session now reads the same board, not the personal one.

- The board reconciler now closes a "main is red" incident it opened on a board it no longer watches for that project. This happens when a repository is bound to an organization after it was watched as personal work, or when the project is no longer watched. Before, nothing could ever close such an incident: only the code host may write it, and no later pass looked at the old board again. A project whose current board cannot be resolved in a pass is left alone, so a transient error never closes a live incident.

- The board reconciler no longer closes or abandons an item that names a pull request its branch does not have in the watched repository. Such an item tracks work somewhere else, for example a change spanning several repositories that share a branch name. Before, one repository's PR merging marked the whole item done, and one repository's branch being deleted marked it abandoned. An item with no recorded PR, or one naming a PR its branch does have, follows the code host as before.

- `car install` now shows what the agent's CAR token may call on the daemon before it asks, and says what that means on each platform: on Linux the scope is a wall, and on a Mac it limits the token only. `agents.install` returns the same `method_allowlist`, and `shared_secrets` names each declared key another installed agent also declares, because both are handed the same stored value (car#3397, car#3561).
- An agent at its own spend cap now asks the owner once per period. The request names the cap, the reset time and how to raise the cap (car#3407).
- The hourly memory consolidation now runs on the daemon's real memory: the shared graph and every agent's and namespace's graph. It saves what it changes, so consolidation survives a restart (car#3495).
- A process that outlived a daemon restart and asks for a secret before it is adopted is told to wait, and its broker asks again for up to 30 seconds instead of failing. A survivor that is never adopted has its own log record name every value handed to the agent (car#3670, car#3677).
- Reliability fixes:
  - A damaged spend file is rebuilt from the call ledgers (car#3384).
  - A worker waiting to retry a failed start gets that retry after a daemon restart (car#3447).
  - A walled Mac session keeps its restrictions after its agent is removed (car#3696).
  - Removing a data-only agent never leaves files that the next install with that id inherits (car#3791).
  - A notification sender cannot leave background processes running (car#3877).
  - Bead ownership is kept per device, and an interrupted handoff is finished by the next rebuild (car#4101).
  - A worker's secret-read record or failed-start cleanup can no longer be lost without notice (car#3417).

- The lab promotion test now checks that a failure outside any step posts exactly one `failed` issue and Teams notice, with no later reaper post, and names the step it followed (`plan`). The release-lab guide says such a failure is reported as the last finished step (#3021).
- Release docs and the promotion preflight now say why a nightly whose pip or npm publish failed can still be promoted: the stable publishes PyPI and npm itself from the nightly's wheels and commit. A fixture pins that behavior. The release-failure notes and catch-up notices now say a failed or blocked pip or npm lane is `Not published` and does not gate a promotion; only a Linux or Windows lane is `Not promotable` (#3827).
- The agent-binding trust-boundary proposal now notes that #3705 superseded its no-host-token finding: with no host token nobody is the host, so `agent_permissions.*` refuses every client (#1390).
- The tombstone guard no longer reads approved outcomes files in `docs/outcomes/`. Like `docs/plans/`, `docs/solutions/` and `docs/proposals/`, they are dated records, so an outcome approved before a removal no longer has to be rewritten to pass (#3600).
- `car-release status` hardening (#2996): it waits only for its own prefetch workers, keeps the prefetch directory under the lab's `run/` (a cancelled status removes it and stops its workers; one killed outright leaves it for the next status to remove after an hour), and prints a prefetched result only when both its `Catch-up:` and `promotable:` lines are there, falling back to the inline check otherwise. A failed vault read in the token mint is retried once, the retries together, so the vault reads take at most two timeout windows (the GitHub token request after them keeps its own limit). The status log-tail fallback is scrubbed again on output. The status and preflight timing tests use millisecond clocks with limits between the overlapped and serial times, and a fixture pins that a different-version stable whose `Promoted-From:` names the nightly but sits on another commit is not read as that nightly's promotion.
- The release lab no longer says "A later nightly succeeded" for a nightly that published the Mac side alone. Its own notice, sent while the Linux, Windows, pip and npm lanes are still catching up, says `Mac published` and which lanes are not published or still catching up; "succeeded" needs all four attached. The CI catch-up failure notices say, from two nightlies in a row, how many went without every platform, counted from the earlier nightly releases' catch-up markers, and at three their comment and Teams notice escalate. One fully published nightly resets the count (#3772).
- The daemon reachability sweep no longer skips the `session.bindSandbox` agent cell when Docker goes away mid-run. Only the cells the committed `docker_unavailable` category names (daemon and host authority) are skipped, so an agent-side failure is still recorded (#1978).

- The car-releases docs sync refuses to publish a staged binary file or a file over 5,000,000 bytes rather than publishing it unscanned. It scans a file whose path has non-ASCII or glob characters as that file alone, and keeps scanning past an added line that begins `++`. Fixes #4333.
- The Mac release verification lists `verified sha256 <digest> <asset>` for every Mac asset both release repositories served identically, so a lab run records which bytes it checked. Fixes #4242.
- A release-lab nightly's late "succeeded" comment skips a reused failure issue whose newer failure came after the run started, even past the first 100 comments gh lists. A comment that fails during a partial GitHub outage is retried for that issue alone. Fixes #4285.
- `car-lane.sh` restart and stop boot out a lane's legacy gui-domain copy when the same label is also loaded in the user domain, and status warns while both are loaded. Fixes #4267.
- `scripts/lib/refresh-changed-sources.sh` cleans every workspace package from the shared cargo target unless this checkout built there last. That covers another checkout's refresh, another checkout's build straight through car-sharedbuild (its `.last-builder`), a target with no record, and dep-info naming another checkout's sources by absolute path. Only real target triples are cleaned per target, so a dashed directory a test left there does not fail the clean. After a clean it also names this checkout in car-sharedbuild's record, so another checkout's next wrapper build sees the switch and cleans. A failed clean stops the build rather than letting it reuse another checkout's units. The record is written only after a clean succeeds, the check also runs under car-sharedbuild, and `ci-local.sh --preflight` leaves the target alone. Part of #4326.
- A benchmark run whose time limits came from a cached calibration records `calibration_reused`, and the consolidator counts its speed-scaled timeouts as incomplete tasks, left out of the score, rather than scored zeros. Fixes #4325.
- `lab-health` warns when the lab's nightly runner (`lab-nightly.sh` and `nightly-changes.sh` in the service checkout, uncommitted edits included) differs from main's (`origin/main`, or `main` in the lab's mirror worktree), naming `car-release update main`. Part of #4329.
- Release verification of a release that is no longer the latest reads car-releases at that release's own docs-sync commit, not the mirror's current tip. It compares CLI.md's generation date with that of the mirror commit that last changed CLI.md, so re-verifying a superseded release no longer fails its docs-mirror checks. Fixes #2876.

- `scripts/ci-local.sh` no longer stops silently when another worktree's recent commit added a Rust file this checkout lacks and it sorts last: `scripts/lib/refresh-changed-sources.sh` now always exits 0 and still touches every changed source that exists. Fixes #4230.
- `scripts/ci-local.sh` takes the `no-changelog` exemption, before the pull request and its label exist, from a declared `CAR_NO_CHANGELOG_REASON="<why>"`, and logs the reason. Without it, a change with no fragment still fails locally as it does in CI. Fixes #4162.
- The isolation-probe integration test no longer panics on an empty report: the probe publishes its report whole (written aside, then renamed), and the test keeps polling until the report parses, within its 150-second deadline. Fixes #3948.
- An integration test process removes its isolated CAR state root (`<temp>/car-it-state-<pid>-*`) when it exits, instead of leaving one in the temp directory per run. Fixes #4259.
- The benchmark consolidator counts each machine once in a catalog speed: a machine's own runs are medianed first, so ten runs from one machine no longer outweigh one from another. Fixes #3753.
- The documentation guards' same-sentence anchor stops at a sentence end followed by a closing quote or bracket (`?"`, `!'`, `.)`), so a hedge in a quoted sentence no longer excuses a claim in the next one. Fixes #1974.
- A release-lab nightly the lab refuses now posts a Teams notice that says it was refused and quotes the reason, instead of failing to render; a render failure is logged with its error. The morning nightly alarm says the lab refused the nightly, naming the failing check, instead of "the lab did not report". Fixes #3319, #3320.
- A release-lab run found dead is retried by every later recovery until both its issue and its Teams notice are delivered, even when its first announcer died before writing anything, instead of being marked announced before delivery. Fixes #3002.
- `car-release runs [--after <run-id>]` lists every release-lab run record newest first, a page at a time, and `car-release status <run-id>` answers for one run of any age; Link's role may run both. Fixes #4169.
- Adding a release-lab key refuses a public key that any `authorized_keys` entry already holds, including entries the helper did not write, so the Link role cannot share a key with a broader entry. Fixes #3878.
- Scoped testing selects the N-API and PyO3 suites when a shared fixture under `car-rs/test-fixtures/` changes, instead of reporting nothing to run. Part of #4179 (rest: car#4326).
- The verify-car skill's doctor fails a daemon still running an earlier build of the same version: it checks the build id the daemon stamped at startup against `car-server`'s build on disk, and for a local build with no build id, whether `car-server` was rebuilt after the daemon started. Fixes #3941.
- The issue-burndown runbook's shared-build guard keeps the build lock with the build itself, so a killed guard cannot let a second build in; a lock-helper error stops it instead of reading as contention; and a stale queue ticket is recognised by its process start time, not by a name match. The heartbeat cron is re-created whenever it is missing, not only when no cron is left. Fixes #3603, #3608, #3613.
- The README lists what `car purge` leaves behind (CarHost's support folder, Keychain items, a project's `.car/`), and `SECURITY.md` names the account-linked data the runtime sends to Parslee and when. Fixes #4154.
- The car-releases docs sync refuses to publish a `CLI.md` generated on another version: without the release's own `car`, the committed copy publishes only when it names this version, or with `--backfill`. Fixes #3840.
- The release script scans the release's own CHANGELOG section, and the car-releases docs sync the text lines it adds, for credentials, and refuses on a finding, naming the file, line and rule but never the value. Part of #3091 (rest: car#4333).
- The Windows test build compiles again: two worktree-pool tests that need a Unix process holder are Unix-only. Fixes #4104.
- A nightly whose release body CI writes now carries the "What changed since the previous nightly" section. Part of #3347 (rest: car#4329).

- `cargo test -p car-server-core` no longer reads or changes your own CAR state. Its integration tests used to start the daemon's real startup, which marked your stranded coder sessions failed and pruned old coder snapshots in `~/.car/coder`; they now run against a temporary state root, and a guard test fails any new test that builds its state without it.

- On Windows, the self-heal ledger's repair of a torn last row now actually cuts it. It shortened the file through a handle opened for append only, which Windows refuses, so the cut failed with only a warning and the next record was appended onto the torn row, where it was skipped on every later boot. The Windows build also compiles again: two helpers used only on Unix (`car-mcp`'s assistant detection and the supervisor's host-token rule with its test) are now built only where they are used.

- `car worktree acquire` (and so Claude Code's worktrees with the pool on) works in a repo with no `origin` remote: it does not fetch, and a new branch starts from the main checkout's current branch. It used to fail with "'origin' does not appear to be a git repository", or with `--offline` "invalid reference: origin/main". Fixes #3860.
- In a git submodule, or a repository made with `--separate-git-dir`, the worktree hook (Rust and the plugin's sh fallback) now roots Claude Code's worktrees at the checkout instead of at the git dir under `.git/modules/`, whether it runs from the checkout or from a worktree made under it, so a worktree it made is removed again by WorktreeRemove and SubagentStop. `car worktree` puts the pool beside the submodule's checkout too, not under the superproject's `.git`. The sh fallback also refuses hook input whose top-level key holds an escape, or that has anything after its JSON object, or that holds byte 0x01, so no input reads one way to it and another to Claude Code. Fixes #3738 (the Windows Git Bash fixture is #4046).
- For a repository made with `--separate-git-dir` and no `core.worktree`, `car worktree` writes the main checkout's path to `car-main-checkout` inside the git dir, so a session in a linked tree can find the checkout again; the hooks also look beside the registered trees, and a recorded path is used only when git confirms it is that checkout. Fixes #3738.

See the [release notes][v0.62.0].

## [v0.61.2] — 2026-11-10

### Changes

- Owner, writer and CAR names on another CAR's work-board items are now quoted in the session briefing, the per-prompt note and overlap notices, like titles already were. They are that CAR's claims, so a connected account could otherwise place unquoted text in a session's instructions (#4252).
- A relay connection whose board becomes readable again with an unchanged batch now ends its outage, so the next failure warns again instead of only logging at debug level (#4256).
- The board reconciler records rotation progress per board, so watches on different boards no longer erase each other's progress and starve older items (#4260).

- `car-winenv` gains `readmit_os_env`, which restores the variables Windows itself needs (`SystemRoot`, `windir`, `TEMP`, …) after `Command::env_clear()`. The `subscription_usage` integration test cleared its daemon's environment without them, so on Windows the daemon could not open a socket and the test failed every `windows-integrations` run. A new check, `scripts/check-env-clear-windows.py` (run in the `terminology` job and `ci-local.sh`), refuses a Windows-compiled test fixture that clears the environment without restoring them.

- `car-server`'s `car-winenv` dev-dependency is path-only, so a release bump that rewrites workspace versions no longer leaves an unresolvable `^0.60.0` requirement on `main`.

See the [release notes][v0.61.2].

## [v0.60.0] — 2026-10-31

### Changes

- `car doctor` recognizes the `commons` and `topology` folders that the shared contribution graph and coordination-topology records write under the state root, instead of offering them up as leftover debris. Self-healing's `[[org]] roots` expand `~` on Windows too, where the home directory comes from `USERPROFILE` rather than `HOME`.

- Walled agents on a Mac can run Apple's developer tools (`git`, `python3`, `clang` in `/usr/bin`) when Xcode is installed but nobody ran `xcode-select -s`. The wall granted the Command Line Tools in that case, while `xcrun` ran Xcode's tools, so every one of them was refused. It now resolves the active developer directory the way `xcode-select -p` does.

See the [release notes][v0.60.0].

## [v0.59.0] — tagged, never published; shipped in [v0.60.0]

v0.59.0 was tagged but never released. Every change below first reached users in v0.60.0.

### Changes

- The `a2a.start` listener no longer answers requests from web pages open in the operator's browser. Its JSON-RPC and stream routes now answer `403` to a request carrying a non-loopback `Origin`, on every bind, and, on a loopback bind, also to a request whose `Host` is not a loopback name, which is how a DNS-rebinding page reaches `127.0.0.1`. Before, any page could POST to the listener and reach its runtime's tools. Requests with no `Origin` (every CLI and SDK caller) are served as before. A loopback listener also serves the host of an explicitly supplied `public_url`, so a tunnel or reverse proxy that forwards the public host name keeps working. A listener started with `allow_non_loopback_bind` does not check `Host`, and the Agent Card routes stay public. For embedders: every `car_a2a::http` router, including the peer-authenticated one, refuses a foreign `Origin`. Only the new `build_router_bound_to(dispatcher, bound, public_url)` and `build_router_with_auth_bound_to(dispatcher, auth, bound, public_url)` also check `Host` when `bound` is a loopback address; `build_router`, `build_router_with_auth`, `serve` and `serve_with_auth` check `Origin` only. On those, a DNS-rebinding page can still make same-origin GET requests, which carry no `Origin`, so on a loopback bind it can read the `/a2a/stream/:task_id` task stream (read-only; writes are POSTs, which always carry `Origin`). A loopback embedder that isn't behind a tunnel should use `build_router_bound_to` or `build_router_with_auth_bound_to`, which also blocks a DNS-rebinding page from reading `/a2a/stream`. `a2a.start` already does. The `Origin` rule and the loopback set are now one implementation in `car_a2a::loopback`, shared with the MCP endpoint and the dashboard's sign-in routes; the MCP endpoint's own `Host` check is unchanged and also accepts any IP literal. As a result, the dashboard's sign-in routes also refuse an `Origin` header that is not valid UTF-8.

- A supervised agent now controls only A2UI surfaces it actually created: when a surface is deleted, recreated on the same id (by the host, an A2A peer or an agent) or expires, the agent that owned it loses that ownership, so it can no longer update or delete a surface the host later put on that id. A test also pins that `workflow.run` and `multi.*` build their runtimes without the operator's connector tools, so a walled agent cannot reach one through them.

- Every connection the `car` CLI opens with an agent's credential (its raw handshake and every `DaemonClient` it creates) is now an additional session: `session.auth { agent_id, token, attach: false }` has the agent's scope and method allowlist but no longer takes over the agent's live connection, so a `car` command run from an agent's shell no longer detaches the agent or ends its chats when it exits. The one exception is the supervised serve process itself (`car do --serve`, with or without `--governed-host`), which is the agent and still attaches. The SDK default is unchanged: a supervised process attaches. A second Rust process inside an agent that should not take over its connection calls `set_additional_agent_sessions(true)` from `car-daemon-client`; a Node or Python helper has no such option and must send `attach: false` in its own `session.auth`.

- `agents.stop` on an adopted agent whose pid cannot be verified as its process (an unreadable start token) now fails with "stop of agent <id> declined" instead of reporting `stopped`. The agent stays running and supervised and keeps its pid file. The token read failure is transient, so retrying the stop is the remedy; Windows records no start token and never declines. If the SIGKILL after the grace period was withheld, the error says the SIGTERM may already have been sent, and the exit it causes leaves the agent `stopped` instead of restarting it. `agents.restart` and `agents.remove` return the same error rather than restarting or dropping the spec of a live process, and shutdown's `stop_all` lists it as still running. A stopped agent's pid file is now cleared only once its process is gone, and a SIGKILL whose exit is not observed leaves the agent's `pid` in place so `stop_all` reports it rather than calling it gone. The `start_all` warning for an agent already running outside supervision now says what `agents.start` actually does (car#3081).

- CarHost's Build an agent screen (Command Deck, New Agent) now keeps the build it starts. After CarHost quits or restarts mid-build, the screen says it is checking on that build instead of showing a blank start screen, and finds it once CAR is connected; leaving the screen before then keeps the build. A build that ended comes back as its answers on the review: one CAR's quit or restart ended says "CAR quit or restarted while this was building, so nothing was added.", and one that ended some other way says how, as the in-chat build card already did. Choose Create build plan (Save & rebuild for an edit) to build it again. A build still running is followed, and a start whose reply hadn't come back is looked for once its start window has passed: followed if it is running, named if it ended, and if CAR still can't say, the screen says so with Try again. The message stays, across relaunches too, until you build again or let those answers go (discard them, choose another starting point, or open another agent to edit). If CAR is connected but can't reach the build, the screen says so and offers Try again. Answers you haven't built yet are still not kept after quitting.

- CarHost Chat: a saved agent that was saved with a model runs on that model; a chat with it shows that model in its model menu, which can't change it, and names the model that answered on its replies. Chats still send their own model choice, which applies to agents saved without one. A saved agent can't take attached files yet: its chat keeps any dropped or pasted file in the message box, says "<agent> can't take attached files yet. Remove them to send." and holds Send until they are removed, and Regenerate, Edit & Resend and Send again of a message with files say the same and change nothing. An Edit & Resend that is refused before it starts puts back every message it replaced. Clicking a "CAR … needs you" approval banner opens the chat at the waiting approval card, also when the click launches CAR, or Approvals when the chat no longer shows it.

- The `car` CLI's raw daemon connections and `car-host` now present the agent credential (`CAR_AGENT_ID` + `CAR_AGENT_TOKEN`, with `attach: false`) inside a supervised agent even when `CAR_AUTH_TOKEN` is also set, matching the SDK daemon client. Before, the env token won and the command ran as a generic daemon session outside the agent's identity and method allowlist; `car-host` also read the daemon token file from inside an agent, which it no longer does. A process with only one agent variable uses `CAR_AUTH_TOKEN` when set and is otherwise refused with an error naming the agent credential. Visible effect for an unscoped agent on the Mac, whose supervisor passes `CAR_AUTH_TOKEN`: its raw CLI commands now run as that agent, so `runs.list` shows only its own runs, and `car code` approve, cancel or subscribe on runs it did not start (including runs left unowned from before this upgrade) are refused. The CAR app can still act on those runs.
- Inside a supervised agent (`CAR_AGENT_ID` or `CAR_AGENT_TOKEN` set) the `car` CLI never presents CAR's local host credential (car#3072). `car start`, `car stop`, `car restart`, `car runs cancel`, `car board` and other dual-role calls go out under the agent's own identity, and the daemon decides what that identity may do. `car install`, `car uninstall`, `car ui` and other host-only commands are refused with "this command needs the operator (host); a supervised agent can't run it". The CLI's operator secret broker is not installed in an agent, so an agent's CLI reads secrets from the store directly, and on macOS that can show keychain prompts. The `car agent new` and `car agent run --scheduled` refusals now also apply to a process with only `CAR_AGENT_TOKEN` set. The operator's CLI is unchanged.

- Building an agent whose folder CAR can't use (often one in Downloads, Documents or Desktop, which macOS guards) no longer hangs for 15 minutes and then says only "The build stopped". When macOS refuses CAR the folder, the build fails at once and says how to fix it: allow CarHost in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Files and Folders, or pick a folder outside Downloads, Documents and Desktop. When making, saving in or copying the folder gets no answer for 45 seconds, the build fails and says that it waited and got no answer, that macOS may have asked whether CarHost can use the folder (allow it in Files and Folders), and that otherwise the disk should be checked or another folder picked. This holds for every copy of the folder the build makes for its test runs, not only the first: a folder that fails part way stops the build, instead of being counted as the agent failing a test and designed again. A build that fails this way has stopped, and it no longer goes on to "Designing the agent" once the folder becomes usable. A folder whose own permissions keep CAR from reading it now says to change those permissions, instead of telling you to move files out of it. The build's final check reports a folder that fails part way as a folder problem, not as the agent failing its scenarios. `declagents.run_scenarios` ("Run scenarios") returns an error naming the folder and the fix when CAR can't use the agent's folder for a scenario, and does not return the results of cases that already ran in that call (car#3176).

- Agent ids are unique ignoring letter case. `agents.upsert`, `agents.install` (WebSocket, NAPI, PyO3) and `car agents install` refuse a new id that differs from an existing agent's only in case, such as `Bob` beside `bob`, with an error naming the existing agent. On a case-insensitive file system such as APFS the two would otherwise share one folder, token, binary, logs and saved memory. Re-installing the same id works as before, and existing registrations are not changed.

- A supervised agent's secret values no longer stay in its log files after the process that received them is gone, and old values no longer reappear in `agents.tail_log` after a secret is rotated or removed, or after the agent or the daemon restarts. Each start of an agent (a run) now writes files of its own, `<id>.<run>.stdout.raw` and `<id>.<run>.stderr.raw`, created new and owner-only, beside a `<id>.<run>.run.json` record of salted fingerprints (never values) of everything the run is handed. While the run is alive, `agents.tail_log` redacts every value the daemon handed the agent in memory. When the process is gone (stop, restart, remove, a crash or exit, or daemon shutdown), the daemon reads each raw file from its first byte, writes it with every handed value replaced by `[redacted]` to a fsynced temporary, renames that to `<id>.<run>.<stream>.log`, a name that does not exist yet, and only then unlinks the raw file. Nothing is truncated or renamed over an existing file, so this works the same on a local disk and on an SMB/Azure Files state root, and a value split across writes is still found; where the file system has neither a no-replace rename nor hard links (an SMB mount on macOS) a run's end fails closed, keeping the raw file served redacted and reporting the failure. A process that outlives the agent and still holds a raw file open writes into the unlinked file: those late writes through its open descriptor are dropped, and never reach a file the tail, a feedback bundle or a later run reads. The copy stops at the length the raw file had when the run's end began, and the twin's rename refuses an existing name; a `.log` that is a symbolic link or has a second name is never trusted or served. A daemon that died without a shutdown leaves its runs for the next one, which recovers them at startup: it redacts a run again when the agent's declared secrets, resolved now, cover every value the run's record names, and otherwise withholds the raw files under `<id>.<run>.<stream>.withheld`, which are never served, never put in a feedback bundle, never deleted automatically, and are named in a `[car: …]` line at the end of the tail. A process adopted from an earlier daemon names its run in its pid record; its output is served redacted only when the values resolved at adoption cover that run, and is withheld when it ends otherwise. The tail reads every kept run in order, oldest first; the daemon keeps the last 20 finished runs per agent (set another number with `CAR_AGENT_LOG_RUNS_KEPT`), a run is kept or deleted whole, and the newest run of the running daemon is always kept. `agents.list` `log_path`/`stderr_log_path` and the tail's `stdout_path`/`stderr_path` now name the newest finished run's redacted log, never a running run's raw file, a log from before the upgrade, or a symbolic link. While a run is alive, the tail redacts each file's window whole, so a value spanning lines is hidden, reads ahead of a window that starts mid-file so a value it cuts is hidden, and hides the start of a value still being written at the end of the file; feedback bundles do the same. A run whose redacted log cannot be written keeps its raw file, served redacted, reports the failure in the agent's `status_reason` or as the new `log_scrub_error` field of the `agents.remove` result, and is retried by the next stop, removal or shutdown. **One-time effect of the upgrade:** an agent's logs from before it (`<id>.stdout.log`/`<id>.stderr.log`, and the copies an earlier scrub set aside) are withheld on its first recovery, whatever the earlier scrub marker says: they are not shown in the dashboard, `agents.tail_log` or feedback bundles, and they stay on disk as `<id>.0000000000000-00000000-0.<stream>.withheld` for the operator. An earlier scrub could miss a value split across writes, a `secret.get` reply, or a secret since rotated or no longer declared, and nothing now can tell those logs apart, so none is published. `secret.get` from a supervised agent now hands a value over only after recording it durably against a run of the agent this daemon holds, and otherwise fails with `log_record_error`: when the daemon holds no run of the agent (a process that outlived an earlier daemon and is not adopted), when a run has no record or its record cannot be read right now, or when the value cannot be written into it. So no run record understates what a raw file holds. A process adopted from before the upgrade is given a record at adoption, so it keeps receiving values, and its logs stay withheld. Two daemons sharing an SMB/Azure Files state root remain unsupported (car#3634). Feedback bundles read only finished runs' redacted logs and the raw file of a run whose values are known: the daemon includes a run it supervises with its values redacted, and `car feedback`, which runs without the daemon, only a run that was handed no values, so `car feedback` no longer includes the live log of an agent that was handed a secret until that run ends. Because each run's files are created new, symlinking `<id>.stdout.log` to `/dev/null` no longer discards an agent's output. A value printed in a form no text match finds (encoded or transformed), or split by the agent into pieces too short to match alone, is still not redacted (car#3150, car#3180, car#3589, car#3620, car#3637).

- Supervised-agent logs are now owner-only (the `logs/` directory 0700, each `<id>.stdout.log` and `<id>.stderr.log` 0600, tightened on daemon start for logs left by older releases), and `agents.tail_log` redacts known secret shapes (API keys, `ghp_` tokens, AWS key ids, `Bearer` tokens, `NAME_KEY=value` assignments) before returning lines. The files on disk still hold exactly what the agent printed, because the agent writes them directly and keeps running if the daemon dies; Parslee-ai/car#3090 stays open for that. The redactor also masks 40+ character hex or token-like runs (which includes git SHAs and digests) and rewrites `/Users/<name>` to `~` in the returned lines. A symlinked log or `logs/` directory is used as before and never chmod'ed.

- A supervised agent can no longer start an outside coding CLI (Claude Code, Codex, and others) through `foreman.run`, or through `coder.start` with an `external` or `foreman` engine, unless it is answering a chat the host started with it. It names that chat with the new `chat_session_id` parameter (NAPI `CoderStartOptions.chatSessionId` and `foremanRun(..., chatSessionId?)`, PyO3 `chat_session_id=`), the same rule `agents.invoke_external` already applies. An agent can confirm such a coder run (`coder.confirm_contract`, which starts the outside CLI) only while that chat turn is still running. `heal.run`, whose default engine is Foreman, follows the same rule and takes the same parameter. Without it, an agent's `coder.start` with `auto` runs on the native engine, which stays available to agents. An agent can never run the Foreman engine on a contract it supplied (`coder.start` with `foreman` and `contract` is refused and points at the native engine, where a supplied contract keeps running in the check sandbox; confirming a Foreman run with an edited contract is refused the same way), and an agent's `verify_command` and `union_verify_command` on `foreman.run` are always refused, because the daemon would run them without the approval the agent's own shell commands need. Hosts, CarHost and other callers that are not bound to an agent are unchanged. (car#2445)

- Daemon: removing an agent (`agents.remove`, `car uninstall`, the CarHost Agents settings, the SDKs' `agents_remove`) no longer reports success when its `manifest.toml` under `~/.car/agents/` cannot be deleted. That is every manifest there declaring the agent's id, since the next boot loads a manifest by the id it declares whatever its folder is called; a manifest there that cannot be read also fails the removal, because boot repairs its permissions and may load it as this agent. Before, the agent was dropped from the daemon's memory while the file stayed, so the next boot loaded it back. Now the file is deleted before the agent is dropped: when that fails the call returns an error naming the file, and the agent stays installed until a later removal can delete it (the removal has already stopped it, and does not start it again). The same holds for a worker whose `spec.toml` cannot be deleted. On an install that still has the legacy `agents.json`, its entry is rewritten before the manifest is deleted, and a failed rewrite also leaves the agent installed. Removing an agent also no longer deletes the folders of agents tracked on disk only (`pure_data` and `health_url`-only installs), which every removal of another agent used to delete.

- Daemon: removing an agent (`agents.remove`, `car uninstall`, the CarHost Agents settings, the SDKs' `agents_remove`) no longer returns an error after the agent is already gone. Before, a removal deleted the agent's files and then rewrote every other agent's `manifest.toml` from memory; a failure writing one of those turned the completed removal into an error, and a retry then reported nothing removed. A removal now rewrites no other agent's `manifest.toml` (so a hand edit in another agent's manifest also survives it), and removing a supervised agent reports `removed: true` once the files the next boot would load it from are deleted. The same holds for a worker whose other files, such as its handed-over values, cannot all be deleted after its `spec.toml` is gone: the removal succeeds and is recorded, the daemon logs the failure, and the files it could not delete stay on disk.

- An agent's run no longer counts as finished when a change it tried failed. If `write_file`, `edit_file`, `shell`, or any tool marked as one that changes something (the spreadsheet and Word tools, and generating a Parslee document to the connected drive, among them) returns an error, and no later call of the same tool succeeds, the run ends with "The agent stopped without finishing", naming the step that failed and the tool's error, even when the agent's last answer says "Done." CarHost shows the run as failed, routing learns it as a failure, and a test case with that error fails instead of passing on its answer text. Before, only the spreadsheet and Word tools in an agent that keeps a folder worked this way. A later successful change to the same file clears the failure whichever tool makes it, so an agent that follows a refusal pointing it to another tool (a spreadsheet written with `write_file` instead of `append_spreadsheet_row`) still finishes. A failed read or search, a web request that only reads (`http_request` with GET, HEAD or OPTIONS), and a command that ran and exited non-zero still leave the run to the agent's answer. An agent with a goal check is not stopped by such a failure: its next try is told what failed, and the run fails only if the last try still has it. A failed test case now reports the run's error rather than "expected output containing …", which read wrongly when the answer did contain the text.

- An agent's run is now told the local date, time and time zone when it starts, so a run asked to write a timestamp or "today's" date no longer makes one up. A scheduled run is also told the time it was scheduled for, in the schedule's own time zone when it uses one other than the Mac's, and a missed time run by hand is told which time it is for. The test runs while an agent is being built get the date and time too.

- Build an Agent: an agent now runs on the model it was built with. Picking a model to build with saves it as the agent's model, so its test cases, Run now, chats with it and routed runs all use it. Rebuilding on Automatic, or on the same model, keeps the saved model and its reasoning effort; picking a different one replaces it.
- If an agent's model isn't available when it runs, CAR never quietly uses another one. With no other model connected, Parslee's default route (`parslee/advisor`) answers instead, strictly, with no on-device fallback. Whenever Parslee served a turn of the run, the result carries `stood_in: { for_model, on_model, notice }` beside an unchanged `output`, even if the run then failed for another reason; the agent page shows "Ran on Parslee because <model> isn't available.", and `car agent run` prints it on stderr. When Parslee never answered, there is only the error. With other models connected (a Codex CLI counts when its sign-in is confirmed), or when Parslee itself isn't available, the run stops with "This agent runs on <model>, which isn't available. Reconnect it, or edit the agent to pick another model." That holds only when every credential state is known. When CAR can't tell whether a model is connected (a secret-store error, or a Codex CLI whose sign-in is unknown, which is always the case on Windows), it never reads that as "unavailable": it tries the agent's model first, before Parslee's availability is considered, and a failure ends with the same suggestion.
- Edit agent opens on the saved model, and its Inference card reads "Runs on <model>, the model it was built with".
- Edit agent: leaving without changes just leaves, with no dialog. When something changed, the dialog asks "Discard your changes?" and says "Your saved agent stays exactly as it is.", with "Discard changes" and "Keep editing". The bottom-bar exit reads "Leave without saving", and an edit's later exits (Start fresh, Back to Agents) use the same words.

- A supervised agent on macOS and Windows can no longer answer, through `host.resolve_approval`, an approval meant for the person. Before this, an agent could open a second connection and approve its own parked high-risk call, or another agent's. A session bound to an agent now gets an error for two kinds of row, and the row is left as it is: any row the high-risk-method gate raised (`ws.method:<method>`), whoever's call it parks, and a system-level approval the agent raised itself (`host.request_approval` with `system_level: true`). Each refusal is recorded as a new `approval.resolve_refused` host event (its `reason` is `gate_row` or `own_system_row`) and as a warning in the daemon log. This matches Linux, where a walled agent cannot call the method at all. CarHost and the other host apps, the daemon-token operator, `car-host approve` and the iMessage and Slack approval transports resolve these rows as before. A session-owned approval (`system_level: false`) is the agent's own record, not a human gate, so its owning connection can still resolve it. That is how an agent records a decision the person made in the agent's own UI, and how it completes a decision CarHost forwards to it through `approval.resolve_requested`. `host.dismiss_approval` is also closed to the same gap: an agent re-authenticating on its connection could, for a moment, dismiss another agent's resolved approval and receive the whole row; it is now held to its own rows throughout, and the method's capability role reads `agent`.

- A session bound to a supervised agent can no longer install, replace or remove an OS schedule (#3440). `scheduler.os_install` and `scheduler.os_uninstall` now refuse it on every platform, macOS and Windows included ("… is not available to a supervised agent: agents get no runtime scheduling; …"), following CAR in the Cloud outcomes D1: an agent's schedule is the `cadence` its author declared for it (declarative agents), it changes only with a new version, and only a person pauses or removes it. `tasks.schedule` and `tasks.unschedule` refuse it the same way, including on a daemon with no host token installed, where their host-role gate let every session through. `scheduler.os_install` and `scheduler.os_uninstall` now carry role `operator_only` (`tasks.schedule` and `tasks.unschedule` stay `host`); host and operator sessions and the CLI keep all four, and `scheduler.os_reconcile` is unchanged. The two methods leave the set an agent token's `method_allowlist` may name: a new scope naming either is refused, and an existing agent whose saved scope names one keeps working, with that entry dropped and a warning naming it.
- `scheduler.run` and `scheduler.run_loop` from a session bound to a supervised agent still run, but no longer read or write the shared task store (#3440, D1). Before, the posted task was saved there, so an agent could plant an interval command task the daemon's command scheduler then ran every interval, or overwrite another task's id with a manual trigger so `scheduler.os_reconcile` removed that task's OS schedule. An agent's runs are no longer deduped across calls; host and operator sessions and the CLI are unchanged.

- Agents CAR runs no longer inherit the daemon's environment. A supervised agent starts with a short allowlist of ordinary process variables (PATH, HOME, USER, the locale and temp-dir variables, SHELL, TERM, CAR_HOME and, on Windows, the system variables a program needs to start), the `CAR_*` variables the supervisor sets, and its literal `env`; provider keys the daemon holds do not reach it. An agent that needs a key lists its name in the manifest, `secrets = ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]` (`agents.upsert` takes `secrets: string[]`), and the daemon fetches it from the secret store at every start, with a policy check and a value-free audit row per read. A missing secret, a policy denial or a locked store blocks the start with a reason naming the secret or store in `agents.list` (`status_reason`); upsert rejects an invalid, reserved or empty name and a name that is also a literal `env` key. A supervised agent's `secret.get` now refuses names it did not declare with `not_declared`, and `secretGet` / `secret_get` in a supervised Node or Python agent go through the daemon and never read the keychain themselves. On a Linux machine with no Secret Service, the store is one owner-only file per key under `~/.car/secrets/`, and a declared secret resolves from there. An agent that declares nothing is flagged in the daemon log and by a `secrets_notice` in `agents.list`, `car inspect` prints its declared names, and `car doctor` lists agents that started in the last 30 days without a declaration. `agents.tail_log` shows a delivered secret value as `[redacted]`. An agent adopted after an unclean daemon death keeps its old environment until it next restarts. CAR's threat model is protecting people from the agents they create on their own computers: an agent gets whatever CAR deliberately gives it, which is its declared secrets. Agents run as the same OS user as the person and CAR does not wall them off from that user's files, so a declaration is not a boundary against an agent that reads the secret store, `~/.car/secrets` or the daemon token file directly. The pass-through list also keeps `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, the proxy variables and the CA-bundle variables; `secret.list`, `secret.status`, `secret.put` and `secret.delete` are refused to a supervised agent's session; `car install` prints the secret names a manifest will receive.

- A process running as a supervised agent (`CAR_AGENT_ID` or `CAR_AGENT_TOKEN` set) no longer silently falls back to the daemon-wide token. The daemon client (NAPI, PyO3, `agent_loop`) and the `car` CLI's raw handshake present the agent credential, use `CAR_AUTH_TOKEN` only when the supervisor put it in the environment (unscoped agents on the Mac are unchanged), and never read the token file; a process with only one of the two agent variables now gets an error naming the agent credential. Processes that are not agents behave as before.

- Build an Agent: an agent now runs on the schedule chosen for it, even while CAR is closed. The answer to "When should this work be requested?" is saved as the agent's schedule when it is built (every N minutes, hourly, daily, weekdays, weekends, or named days at a time; "only when I ask" stays manual), and the daemon installs a durable OS schedule that runs `car agent run --scheduled <id>`. On macOS that is a launchd job. On Linux it is a crontab line (an interval there must be every N minutes dividing the hour evenly, every N hours dividing the day evenly, or every day; any other interval is refused there); on Windows a Task Scheduler task for an interval of whole minutes up to 31 days or a single time on one day or every day, with no log file. An interval (every N minutes or hours) on Windows runs on Task Scheduler's own timer: it is not checked for lateness, never records a missed time, and may shift by an hour after a daylight-saving change. A daily or single-day schedule keeps its clock time there and follows the 15-minute rule. Other schedules (on Windows, any fixed-zone schedule, intervals included), and any schedule under a non-default `CAR_HOME` or a `CAR_DECLAGENTS_PATH` registry on Linux or Windows, are saved and reported as not installed, with the reason, which `declagents.runs` keeps showing. When the platform's scheduler cannot take a schedule (judged by the same check that installs it), CAR removes the agent's earlier job (if that removal fails, the schedule's note says so, and a launch still refuses to run it), `declagents.runs` shows no next run or missed times for it, and neither a scheduled launch nor Run now on one of its times runs it. A schedule runs on the Mac's own clock, or on a named zone's wall clock (`ET`, `America/New_York`, or the builder's zone) wherever the Mac is. An answer CAR cannot read saves no schedule and the approval says so; the build still succeeds.
- Schedules can be paused and changed without touching the agent: `declagents.pause` stops only the schedule (Run now and chat keep working), and `declagents.set_schedule` replaces it and saves it as the builder answer, so rebuilding the agent keeps it. Both are host-management only. Removing or disabling an agent takes its schedule down; approving a build keeps a pause made while it ran; the daemon repairs schedules at boot, including one that still points at a `car` an update replaced. Each CAR state folder keeps its own schedules and never replaces or removes another folder's; a job carries only the `CAR_HOME` and `CAR_DECLAGENTS_PATH` its daemon was started with, so the default folder's jobs run as the default folder. Cadences are validated when an agent is saved (a schedule repeats at most once a minute, and cron numbers are plain digits), and the cadence is no longer part of an agent's fingerprint. For an agent not made with Build an Agent, approving an edit keeps a schedule set with `declagents.set_schedule` while the edit was built, unless the edit itself changed the schedule; for a Build an Agent agent, that change also changes its builder answer, so an edit started before it is refused as out of date and must be rebuilt.
- Every scheduled run leaves a record (`agent-runs/<agent>/<run>.json` beside the agent registry, `~/.car` by default; on macOS and Linux the files are readable only by your user account, on Windows they take the folder's permissions, and the host reads them through `declagents.runs`, which is host-management only) with its output, error, serving model and scheduled and actual times. A schedule with clock times (a cron, or an interval that fits the clock such as every 15 minutes or every 2 hours) runs a time only within 15 minutes of it: after the Mac wakes from sleep, the most recent time runs if it is under 15 minutes old, and earlier times, or a time the Mac was shut down at, appear as missed in `declagents.runs` (a launch 15 minutes or more late also records its time as missed), with no catch-up run. An interval that does not fit the clock, such as every 7 minutes, cannot tell a late launch from an on-time one, so after sleep it runs once on wake, and it reports no missed times. A time from before the schedule started or resumed is never run or missed, and within one CAR state folder two launches of one time run it once; a registry shared by several state folders (through `CAR_DECLAGENTS_PATH`) is not supported for scheduling. If the daemon stops between taking a time and writing its record, that time shows as missed, or as failed once a later launch of it finds it taken; it never runs twice. `declagents.runs` (host-management only) returns the records plus each scheduled agent's next run, last run and missed times (the latest 20); records come as short previews, the newest 50 per agent by default, paged with `limit` and `before`, and `run_id` returns one in full. Run now on a missed time (`declagents.invoke { trigger: "manual", scheduled_for }`) records the run against that time, so it is no longer missed and shows as run by hand. When the daemon cannot be reached, or stops mid-run, the scheduled run records the failure itself. A Mail agent whose Mail Automation permission is not granted fails its scheduled run with a plain message instead of running without Mail.
- `schedule.suggest` now treats a `timezone` param as a fixed zone (`timezone_mode: "fixed"`), reports a name that is not an IANA zone as `reason`, accepts more phrases (`every day`, `weekends`, several named days, `am`/`pm` times, `only when I ask`, a trailing zone), and returns a plain-words `summary`.

- A supervised agent on macOS and Windows no longer reads every agent's approvals and host events. `host.approvals`, `host.events` and `host.subscribe` (its snapshot and its live `host.event` stream) now show a session bound to an agent only the records attributed to that agent, the way `host.agents` already showed it only its own row; before, an agent got every other agent's approval rows, including their call arguments in `details.params_preview`, and every agent's host events. The approval the high-risk-method gate raises for an agent's own call is now attributed to that agent, so it stays in that agent's `host.approvals`; an agent approving its own gated call is now recorded as a self-resolution (an `approval.self_resolved` host event and a warning in the daemon log), as it already was for `host.request_approval` rows. Host apps (CarHost, the iOS, Android and Windows hosts), the daemon-token operator and the CLI still see everything. Watcher agents stay possible: the new host-management-only `agent_permissions.set_observer { agent_id, enabled }` grants one agent the full view of those three methods: its `host.subscribe` snapshot then lists every agent, while `host.agents` stays own-row. Set it in CarHost under Settings → Agent Permissions ("Can see other agents' approvals and events"; the card's Reset also withdraws it), with `car approvals set-observer <agent> on|off`, or through the generated wrappers `agentPermissionsSetObserver` / `agent_permissions_set_observer`.
