Its system messages lead the instructions, tool calls and results are included, and an external tool result is fenced as data, as it is for a remote model. On macOS 27, images inside `messages` now reach the model on non-streaming requests without tools or a JSON schema; before, they were refused. That does not cover `car do`, which always sends tools, so its image turns still route to a vision model. A history too long for the model's context window is not truncated. An overflow is now a context-window refusal (`UnsupportedMode`, with the token counts in the log) instead of a model failure, so it no longer counts against the model's circuit breaker or health record. An unpinned non-streamed request moves to the next model, a stream ends with the refusal, and a request pinned with `strict_model` gets the refusal where it used to be answered without its history. A pinned `car do` turn on this model still cannot be answered: its tool catalog alone exceeds the 8,192-token window on macOS 27 (measured on turn 1: 10,262 tokens before this change, 11,625 with the system prompt it now receives). The history fix applies to requests that fit. The overflow is recognized in each form the framework reports it: on macOS 27, the typed error and the untyped error a tool-bearing session raises (both measured); on macOS 26, `GenerationError.exceededContextWindowSize`. The mlx-vlm route (`mlx-vlm/qwen3-vl-2b:bf16`) now also receives the rendered conversation and its images. A request without `messages` reaches it unchanged.

- A fresh install no longer writes the deprecated `agents.json`, so the next boot no longer warns "loading agents from legacy agents.json". Agents are registered only in the current `agents/<id>/manifest.toml` layout. An install that already has an `agents.json` keeps it up to date and keeps the warning; because writing is keyed on the file existing, downgrading to an older CAR (which recreates `agents.json`) and upgrading again returns that install to legacy mode. `car doctor`, `car info` and feedback bundles read agents from both layouts, so they still list agents on a fresh install.
- If saving an agent fails on a fresh install, the daemon no longer keeps the agent in memory (or keeps an edit) that is not on disk, and removing an agent still deletes its folder under `~/.car/agents/` even when another agent's file cannot be rewritten.
- CarHost Settings -> Agents now points at `~/.car/agents/` (Reveal in Finder) instead of `~/.car/agents.json`, and no longer creates a stub `agents.json`.

- The concierge no longer recommends GLM-4.7-Flash's 4-bit build. On simple prompts it repeats itself until it runs out of tokens ("+ 5 - 5 + 5 - 5 …"), at every sampling temperature and on both vllm-mlx 0.4.1 and 0.6.0, and it scored 0.081 on CAR's judged suite. An installed copy still works and stays listed, marked deprecated. The 8-bit build (`vllm-mlx/glm-4.7-flash:8bit`) answered the same prompts correctly and is cataloged in its place. It needs about 37 GB, more than the default local-model allocation on a 64 GB Mac (40%), so on that machine it is offered only under the `local_focused` profile.

- `agents.chat` goal turns continue the session's conversation. A goal turn on a session that already had turns used to start from a fresh transcript after waiting for the earlier turn and then store it over that turn's exchange, so the next turn lost the earlier history and could reuse its call ids. It now loads the session's thread the way an ordinary turn does (the stored thread, else the durable checkpoint, else a fresh one). The goal's completion check sits with the conversation's system prompt for that goal turn only: a later goal turn replaces it, and an ordinary turn after a goal turn no longer carries it (car#2794).

- `openai/gpt-6.1-sol:latest` carries a car-judged score (1.0, one run, measured 2026-10-26 with `thinking: auto`) and a measured answer rate, like the other native frontier rows. It was the last OpenAI frontier row ranked without one.

- `vllm-mlx/gpt-oss-20b:mxfp4`'s car-judged score now rests on two clean runs, 0.501 (spread 0.029), the second taken under the tool-less task prompt. Its two tool-less tasks that used to stop for a phantom python tool now reason to the output limit instead; both still score 0 there.

- The catalog no longer claims tool calling for `vllm-mlx/gpt-oss-20b:mxfp4`, so the router stops sending tool-using agent turns to it. On vllm-mlx 0.6.0 gpt-oss cannot emit a tool call at all: with CAR's `--tool-call-parser auto`, the streamed reply carries the model's intent to call ("We need to call the get_weather function…") as reasoning and no `tool_calls`, and the non-streamed one returns the arguments as plain text (`{"city":"Paris"}`) with no function name. `--tool-call-parser harmony` with `openai-harmony` installed does the same. The row keeps generate, code, reasoning and summarize.

- `params.reasoning_effort` now reaches gpt-oss on vllm-mlx, as its chat template's `reasoning_effort` ("Reasoning: low" in the harmony system message). It was dropped there like on every local model, which left gpt-oss with no thinking control at all: its template ignores `enable_thinking`. The effect is large: on a hard probability task with a 4000-token limit, the default (medium) and `high` reasoned to the limit and returned no answer, while `low` finished in 2835 tokens with one. Only the explicit field is sent; a level derived from `budget_tokens` is not, so an automatic thinking budget cannot push gpt-oss to `high`. `xhigh` is sent as `high`.

- gpt-oss served through vllm-mlx no longer returns its reasoning as its answer. vllm-mlx 0.6.0's non-streaming path flattens gpt-oss's harmony channels before its reasoning parser runs, so a turn cut off at `max_tokens` inside the analysis channel came back with that analysis as the answer ("We need to count spanning trees…"), and a finished turn lost its reasoning entirely. Its streaming path keeps the two apart, so CAR now sends gpt-oss's non-streaming requests as a stream and folds the result back: the reasoning is thinking, the answer is only the final channel, and a turn that never reached an answer is empty and handled as one (CAR's thinking recovery). Every other family keeps the plain request.
- A gpt-oss turn cut off at `max_tokens` is no longer retried with thinking off, and CAR never sends gpt-oss `enable_thinking=false`. Its harmony template has no thinking switch, so the retry decoded the same reasoning a second time, and on vllm-mlx the switch only turned the server's reasoning parser off, which returned the analysis channel as a "recovered" answer.
- `vllm-mlx/gpt-oss-20b:mxfp4`'s car-judged score is re-measured with the fix: 0.516 (1 run). The three earlier runs (0.531–0.693) are withdrawn because their judges graded leaked analysis-channel text as the answer. Turns that hit the output limit inside the analysis channel now score as what they produced, nothing. Two hard tasks also come back empty because the suite's system prompt tells the model to use tools it does not have, and gpt-oss starts writing code for its built-in python tool; that is a harness issue, not counted here as fixed.

- The `car-judged` benchmark the router ranks models by is now a 17-task suite with harder math, tracing and debugging problems, because the old one saturated: half the catalog scored 1.0 and the router could not tell a frontier model from a mid-tier one. The scored models in the built-in catalog were re-measured against it on one machine with one judge; Gemma 4 31B and GLM-4.7-Flash 8-bit could not be re-measured in time, so their old scores are removed rather than left on the old scale. Cloud models now spread from 0.49 to 1.0 and the best local model scores about 0.66. A model whose run did not complete (more than one timed-out or errored task) has its old score withdrawn instead of kept. The four 6,000-token tasks allow 600 seconds instead of 300, so a model that thinks by default can finish them; no other model came near the old limit. The `tau-bench-airline` scores, measured once in June for nine models and never refreshed, are removed, and `openai/o4-mini` is marked deprecated because OpenAI's API now answers 404 for it. Because real scores now sit lower, the size estimate `car models recommend` uses for an unmeasured local model is scaled to the best measured local score, so "most capable" no longer picks an unmeasured 31B over every measured model.

- `car-self-harness` now splits its tasks three ways, following *Harness Learning* (arXiv 2609.35738). The current harness's failures on the **feedback** set become the evidence the proposer sees. Candidates are compared on a separate **scoring** set the proposer never saw: a candidate is kept only if it improves there without getting worse on the feedback set. A third **eval** set is measured every round and for the final harness and decides nothing. Before, the loop mined and ranked on the same tasks, so an edit that fixed exactly the failures it was shown looked like an improvement. `--held-in-fraction` is replaced by `--feedback-fraction` (default 0.4) and `--scoring-fraction` (default 0.3), and the report's `held_in_task_ids`/`held_out_task_ids` by `split` and `final_eval`.
- `car-self-harness` records every proposal that never became a candidate, with the reason (`model_error`, `parse_failed`, `apply_failed`, `noop`, `duplicate`), in each round's `dropped` list, and flags a candidate that passes no scoring task as `zero_score`. The summary prints failed edits and zero-score candidates per round and the run's share of unusable proposals. Before, dropped proposals disappeared without a count.
- `car-self-harness` re-runs the round's best candidate and the current harness on the scoring set before merging, and merges only if the candidate still passes more tasks; the report records the re-run as `confirmation`. Each candidate's evaluation names the scoring tasks it gained and lost and the feedback tasks it lost. A candidate that did not improve the scoring set is rejected without running the feedback set. The run refuses to start when the task set is too small to give the feedback, scoring and eval sets a task each.
- `car-self-harness` proposals are SEARCH/REPLACE edits against the current system prompt instead of a rewritten prompt. Each SEARCH text must occur exactly once; an empty one appends. A reply that does not parse or whose SEARCH text does not match is sent back with the error, up to three attempts, and otherwise recorded as `parse_failed` or `apply_failed`. Each candidate keeps its `replacements` beside the prompt they produce.
- When two `car-self-harness` candidates improve the scoring set by the same amount, the one whose runs errored or timed out less is nominated.
- The `car-self-harness` proposer now sees, for each failed example, the task text, the agent's final answer, its turn and tool-call counts, and the grader's explanation for each unmet criterion. It also sees the run's earlier candidates and whether each was merged, did not improve results, or did not hold up on a re-run (never scoring-set numbers). Bench `TaskScore` gains an optional `trace` excerpt (task, answer, turns, tool calls).
- `car-self-harness --independent N` runs a baseline arm instead of the loop: N independent edits of the seed prompt from one execution report, each measured on the scoring and eval sets and never merged. It reports the seed's eval score, the mean candidate's, the share above the seed, the candidate the loop's own selection (gate, nomination, confirmation re-run) would keep, and the oracle best on eval (labelled as such). It refuses to run when the seed's feedback report has nothing actionable to propose from. With `--out`, the report is tagged `"arm": "sequential"` or `"arm": "independent"`.
- `car-self-harness` records every proposer call (exact prompt, raw reply, how far it got, the candidate it became) with a reward following Harness Learning's Eq. 6 and 8, and `--dataset <path>` writes them as JSONL rows for training a proposer elsewhere. A no-op reply is scored as the current harness and a duplicate as the candidate it copies, and each row carries its own scoring pass rate and the current harness's, so a quality filter applies to a row alone. `--proposer-model <id>` runs the proposer on a different model from the one under test; `SelfHarnessConfig.model`, which was documented as a proposer override and read by nothing, is replaced by `proposer_model`.
- Skill evolution now says why an attempt produced nothing. `MemgineEngine::evolve_skills_attempt` returns the skills with an `EvolveOutcome` (`proposed`/`ingested` counts, `parse_failed`, `model_error`, `nothing_to_evolve_from`), and `parse_skills` has a `try_parse_skills` sibling that keeps a reply that is not a skill array apart from an empty answer. The `evolution.run` Skills step and the daemon cadence's Skills step append the counts to their summary, and count a domain as evolved only when a skill was admitted to trial.
- Fixed: the dream pass (`consolidate`) and the daemon's evolution cadence never evolved a skill. Both call skill evolution with no failure traces, meaning "evolve from the existing skills", and evolution returned early on an empty trace list without asking the model. With no traces it now builds the prompt from the domain's recorded outcomes and each skill's success and failure counts, which is what elected the domain in the first place, and it makes no model call when the domain has no recorded outcomes, or none since its last attempt, so a reply that admits nothing is not paid for again on every dream pass or cadence tick. The dream pass now counts a domain as evolved only when a skill was admitted.
- Fixed: `car-harness-opt`'s random restarts all climbed from the seed config. The perturbed start point for each later restart was computed and thrown away. Each later restart now climbs from a perturbed seed that actually differs from it, scored and recorded as that restart's step 0, and that evaluation comes out of the restart's share of the budget, so a search spends at most `budget` evaluations, the seed's included.

- The self-healing repair loop can cover every project in every organization you belong to. A new `[[org]]` section in `heal.toml` names a GitHub organization or user, or `*` for your `gh` login and every organization it belongs to. Each sweep keeps that owner's unarchived repositories your login can push to and that you have checked out under `roots`. Checkouts are matched by `origin` remote, never by directory name; a main checkout is preferred over a linked worktree; symlinks, hidden directories and `~/Library` are not searched; and nothing is cloned. Each kept repository's labelled issues are worked like a `[[target]]`'s. A sweep now works at most three items across all targets, and the next sweep starts just past the last target it reached. `heal.status` reports the configured `orgs` and what the last sweep `discovered`. `heal.run` with `item` accepts a discovered repository, matched case-insensitively. The self-heal detector's hand-off sees discovered repositories too.

- The self-healing repair loop hands work it cannot do unattended to a person instead of retrying it on local models. The cadence skips any item carrying `human_label` (`needs-human` by default). When local models fail an item twice, or it hits a failure no retry changes, the loop does four things. It labels the item. It assigns the `escalate_to` GitHub logins from `heal.toml`, so GitHub notifies those teammates in whatever organization the repository belongs to. It comments the reason. And it raises a CarHost approval card. Approving the card runs that item with the attended configuration (frontier models) on the next tick, charged to the operator. `car heal run --item owner/repo#N`, `heal.run` with `item`, `healRun(chatSessionId, item)` and `heal_run(item=...)` run one item that way at any time, setting aside its backoff, exhaustion and label. An item is handed over once (recorded in the claim ledger) with one comment. The approval card is a high-risk gate row, so a supervised agent cannot approve the frontier run it starts, and it is dismissed only after the run it approved has happened. A change that passed review but could not be delivered is escalated without offering a frontier run. `heal.run` refuses a malformed `item` instead of sweeping every target.

- Self-healing escalations reach people over Lattice. A new `notify` list in `heal.toml` names Lattice addresses (`<node>@<car>`): your other devices, or nodes a consented connection shares, so a teammate's CAR hears when an item needs a person. The daemon sends as `car-self-heal`, now a reserved id no agent may take. It sends in the work context of the item's repository: your context for the organization its checkout declares in `.car/config.toml`, or personal. An organization's notice therefore reaches only that organization's nodes. Each notice passes every stage an agent's `agents.message` does: the channel guard, the context rule, policy, the audit, and the hold on a first message to another owner's CAR. `agents.message` and the daemon now share one pipeline, which takes the sender's context as stated rather than reading it from the sender's name.

- The self-healing repair loop's unattended sweeps (the cadence) now run on local models only, so it never spends money with no one watching. The engine is `native`, because an outside coding CLI bills its own provider outside CAR's meter. The coder and every review seat are pinned to installed local models, and the sweep runs under a new local-only spend scope (`SpendScope::local_only`), which refuses any remote dispatch at admission with `remote_in_local_only_scope`. Name the models under a new `[unattended]` section of `heal.toml`, or leave it out and CAR picks them from installed local models: only downloaded text models with at least 32,768 tokens of context are considered; the largest that writes code and calls tools codes, and the largest model of each other vendor reviews, up to three seats. A local seat's independence is counted by lineage (who trained it), so Qwen variants are one seat. Under the local-only scope, routing considers on-device models only and the verification auditor picks a local model from another vendor, so a run never reaches a remote model it would then be refused. The refusal also holds where no spend gate is installed. The self-heal detector's own auto-fix now runs `car code-task --local-only`, a new flag that restricts that process to local models, and the detector hands work to the repair loop only while its unattended cadence is running. `heal.status` reports the result as `unattended` (`{coder_model, review_models, source, refusal}`). The top-level `review_models`, `coder_model` and `engine` now apply only to a sweep a person starts with `heal.run`, which may use frontier models. Targets alone enable the loop; before this, the cadence ran on the attended configuration, by default an outside coding CLI and a frontier panel, with its spend uncapped. Named models meet the same bar as picked ones (a coder that writes code and calls tools, text seats with room for a diff), a reviewer from the coder's own vendor is seated last, and a remote verifier or non-`auto` auditor named in `~/.car/coder.toml` refuses the cadence up front instead of failing every item at verification.

- Unattended self-healing picks local models that can actually run and finish. It skips models served by vLLM-MLX while that runtime is missing or outdated, and models larger than the Local Models RAM allocation, and refuses a named one of either with the reason. It ranks candidates by CAR's measured quality before size, and requires a coder that generates at least 50 tokens per second when its speed is measured. Outcome enumeration runs one model at a time under a local-only scope, so local models are not loaded side by side.
- A contract check whose nested single quotes split its argument (`python3 -c 'print('x')'`) is refused when the contract is validated, not reported as a failing check. A `python -m <module>` check whose interpreter lacks the module is reported at baseline as unable to run, naming the interpreter, instead of as a bug the coder must fix.

- Redaction: long hex values and keys cut into short segments no longer pass as plain identifiers and survive into coder ledgers, evidence artifacts or feedback bundles. A run of 40 or more characters stays readable only when it looks like an identifier. These are now redacted: a run spelled entirely in hex digits however it is grouped, a run where segments carrying a digit outnumber letter-only ones (`k3jx9qm_p2v8wzr_…`), and a run with an 8+ character segment that is all hex digits (including letter-only hex such as `deadbeefcafefacebead`) or mixes letters and digits. Descriptive names such as `conversation_task_list_isolation_and_restart` and `test_utf8_base64_decode_handles_padding_ok_x` stay readable.

- The Claude Code plugin's policy hook (`car policy-check-hook`) and the `car-mcp` `policy_check` tool now run CAR's built-in egress guard on Claude Code's `Bash` and `WebFetch` calls. Before, the guard only looked at tools literally named `shell`, `http` or `webfetch`, so it never ran in a plugin session. **This turns on new denies in every plugin session, with no rule written:** a `Bash` command or `WebFetch` URL that runs `nc` or `netcat` is denied — as the command, as an argument (quoted or not) of any program not on the guard's naming list, such as `sudo nc`, `watch nc`, `docker run alpine nc -z db 5432` or `kubectl exec pod -- nc -z host 80`, or in script text a shell runs, including what `echo` or `printf` pipe into a shell (`echo 'nc …' | sh`) and `bash <(echo 'nc …')`. So is any text containing `/dev/tcp/`, which matches as a plain substring, so a `grep` or a doc line naming it counts too; and so is one of `| bash`, `| sh`, `curl -X POST`, `wget --post` or `base64 -d` combined with a host off the guard's allowlist; the allowlist includes the installer hosts `sh.rustup.rs`, `bun.sh`, `astral.sh`, `ollama.com` and `claude.ai`, so their `curl … | sh` installers warn rather than deny, while the same pipe from a host off the allowlist is denied, and an upload pattern (`curl -X POST`, `wget --post`) to one of them warns rather than denies, the same as one to `github.com`; that rule, like `/dev/tcp/`, reads the raw text, quoted strings and here-documents included, so a command that only writes those strings is denied too. Each deny names the guard and the pattern (`egress: egress inspector blocked: suspicious pattern 'nc'`). `nc` passes as an argument of a program on the naming list — programs that only name, look up, install, print, or inspect and manage files and processes (`man`, `which`, `brew`, `cargo`, `make`, `grep`, `rg`, `echo`, `git`, `ls`, `cat`, `cp`, `rm`, `pkill`, `killall` and the rest the README lists) — except their runner forms (`npm exec`, `pnpm dlx`, `yarn exec`, `git bisect run`, `rg --pre`, `vim -c`, `make --eval`, `cargo --config`; `npx` is never exempt); inside a quoted string holding a space for another program; and in a here-document no shell reads, such as a commit message written with `$(cat <<'EOF' … EOF)` (an unquoted one's `$(…)` and backticks are still followed). The guard is a heuristic: other transports, an upload to an unlisted host without one of those patterns, and `nc` inside a multi-word quoted argument of a non-shell program (`ssh -o ProxyCommand='nc %h %p'`, `tmux new 'nc …'`), another interpreter (`python3 -c`), a script read from a file (`bash script.sh`, `cat f | sh`, `echo … > f; sh f`), a command built at run time (`$N`, `bash -c "$(echo nc …)"`, brace expansion), a locale string (`$"nc"`), an option or assignment value (`-o ProxyCommand=nc`, `LESSOPEN='|nc …' less`), a pager or editor running it some other way (`less +'!nc'`, `nano --speller=…`), the arguments `cargo run --` passes to the user's own program, or a Makefile target that runs it are not denied, and an unlisted host on its own only warns. Every URL in the text must be allowlisted; loopback (`localhost`, `*.localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`) counts as allowlisted, but `nc`, `netcat` and `/dev/tcp/` are denied even toward loopback. Operator rules still match the host's own tool names exactly (`deny_tool = ["WebFetch"]` matches what it matched before). The response gains `inspected_as`, the CAR tool a call was inspected as. CAR's own `http_request`, `browser`, `browse_navigate`, `browser_await_signin`, `web_fetch`, `run_command` and `pty_start` are inspected too, and a tool with no mapping that carries a `command` or `url` string is inspected but its guardrail findings only warn.
- `car_policy::EgressInspector` (library behaviour): `nc` and `netcat` now match where they run, reading the line with shell quoting, comments, substitutions and here-documents, instead of as the substring `nc `. A command that merely contains the letters (`rsync`, `async fn`, `cargo test -p car-sync`) or names the program (`git commit -m "fix nc"`, `man nc`, `pkill nc`, `brew install netcat`) is no longer denied; an `nc` argument of any program off the naming list (quoted or not, unless the quoted text holds whitespace), script text a shell runs, input a shell would reject as unterminated that names it, and nesting deeper than 8 are denied. `| bash` and `| sh` match only when the command after the pipe runs that shell (also through `sudo` or `xargs`), so `| sha256sum` is no longer read as `| sh`. The host allowlist matches on a domain-label boundary for every URL in the text, so a lookalike such as `evilgithub.com` is no longer treated as `github.com` and an allowlisted URL no longer excuses an unlisted one beside it; an `@` after `?` or `#` is not userinfo, and a host counts as allowlisted only if it does under both readings of a `\` before `@` (curl reads `https://github.com\@evil.com/` as `evil.com`). Loopback hosts count as allowlisted. `EgressInspector::default()` adds `sh.rustup.rs`, `bun.sh`, `astral.sh`, `ollama.com` and `claude.ai` (and their subdomains) to its allowlist, for every caller of the default, so a pipe-to-shell installer from those hosts warns instead of being denied. A deny reason now names `'nc'` rather than `'nc '`. Its contract is otherwise unchanged: it still inspects only `shell`, `http` and `webfetch`.

- Host approvals no longer accumulate rows nobody can clear, and a resolve that did not land now says so (Parslee-ai/car-releases#89). `host.resolve_approval` on a row that is no longer pending (another decision won, or the daemon closed it as `agent_gone` when the agent's session dropped) is refused with `-32003` and `error.data.reason: "already_resolved"`, carrying the resolution that stands and the row. Before, it returned success with the unchanged row, so a client that checked only for an error believed its deny had landed. The first resolution still stands either way. A resolve of a row whose owning session is not subscribed is now `-32003` with `error.data.reason: "owner_not_connected"`; the message text is unchanged. The new `host.dismiss_approval { approval_id }` removes a resolved row: an agent may remove its own agent's rows, and a host app or the operator any; a pending row is refused (`approval_pending`), and so is a Lattice review mirror whose decision has not reached the Lattice ledger yet (`lattice_mirror`). `host.approvals` now drops resolved rows older than 24 hours when it is read, not only when an approval is created, so an idle queue is pruned too; pending rows still age out only when an approval is created. `host.request_approval` adds two fields to its result: `subscribed`, whether the requesting session is subscribed to host events, and `answerable`, whether a host's decision can take effect. A session-owned row from an unsubscribed session is `answerable: false`, since it can never receive a host's answer, and the daemon logs a warning. A `system_level` row from an unsubscribed session can be decided, but the requester will not receive `approval.resolved` and has to poll `host.approvals` for the outcome. CarHost on macOS, the iOS and Android apps, the Windows tray, `car-host` and the bundled web host UI read the new refusal reason (an `already_resolved` refusal whose standing resolution is the one sent counts as landed), and keep comparing the returned row when connected to an older daemon. CarHost shows a row whose agent is not connected as "The agent that asked for this isn't connected, so your answer can't reach it" instead of the raw daemon error.

- **Host authority fails closed (front doors PR 6d, car#3208).** A session is the host only when it proved the host token. Before, a daemon with no host token installed (`--no-auth`, a failed host-token write at startup, or an embedder that never called `ServerState::install_host_token`) let every authenticated session act as the host. Now nobody is the host there, and every host-management method refuses every session with `this operation requires the host-management role` plus the notice and its cause. The same holds for acting on another agent (`agents.start`/`stop`/`restart` and the rest of the own-agent-or-host methods), `workers.spend` without an orchestrator binding, the host-only credential event stream, and an agent's Coder run. A bound agent still acts on itself, and an unbound connection still acts on a person's Coder run.
  - **Who breaks.** A deploy script that runs `car install`/`uninstall`/`start`/`stop`/`restart -y`, or `car agent new --yes`, against a daemon with no host token; a cloud or headless CAR started with `--no-auth`; a Rust embedder that never installs a host token; on Linux, any supervised agent other than CAR's own assistant under `--no-auth`, which is now not started (status `errored`, with a `status_reason` naming `--no-auth`); an unbound client of a no-host-token daemon that read the daemon token from `mobile.runtime`; every scheduled declarative agent on a no-host-token daemon, whose runs are now refused. A refused scheduled run does not stop silently: its time is recorded `failed` with the host-role reason (shown in `declagents.runs`), the daemon logs it, and it emits the host event `agent.scheduled_run_refused`.
  - **Migration.** Run `car doctor`: its `Daemon auth:` line says whether the running daemon has a host token and why not. If the host-token write failed, fix what it names (usually the permissions of `~/.car`) and restart the daemon. Drop `--no-auth`. In a deploy script run by the server's owner, replace `-y` with `--as-host` on `car install`, `uninstall`, `start`, `stop` and `restart`: it presents CAR's local host key without asking, needs the host-token file, and is refused in a process started as a supervised agent. That refusal reads environment variables the agent controls: on Linux the agent's wall keeps the host-token file from it, but on the Mac an unwalled agent can read that file and present the key (car#3706). Plain `-y` never presents the key. An embedder calls `ServerState::install_host_token`.
  - **Not changed yet.** `host.resolve_approval` still admits an operator session holding the daemon token, because the phone apps, CarHost and the SDK resolve approvals with that token today. It moves to the host role in a follow-up (car#3701).

- The host-permission probe tests no longer fail on a loaded machine (#3370). The success and error cases each use their own probe key, so the error case can no longer read the success case's finished answer. The overlapping-caller test waits until the second caller has joined instead of sleeping, and gives the first caller a long enough wait. The stuck-probe test times each call on its own clock and checks the re-probe with a different answer, so it fails when the probe is never cleared. The runtime behaves as before.

- On a machine whose certificate store holds certificates but none that can be read, these paths now fail with an error message instead of panicking: OpenAI Codex device sign-in, `car install <namespace>/<name>` registry downloads, Parslee capability discovery, M365 document generation, the OpenRouter connect flow (which now ends as rejected instead of staying pending), and remote AgentDNS discovery (which is skipped with a warning). `car_connectors::discovery::RemoteRoot::new` now returns a `Result` for this reason. An empty certificate store was never affected.

- `http_request` follows a redirect only on the origin (scheme, host and port) of the URL that was approved. A redirect to another origin is no longer followed: the tool returns that 3xx response with a new `location` field holding its absolute destination, so a POST and its body are never re-sent to a host the approval did not name. To go there the model makes a new `http_request`, which asks for approval naming the new host. Remote MCP connectors (`connectors.add`) follow redirects only on the origin they were added with, and re-send a call, auth headers included, to a 307 or 308 that only upgrades it from `http` to `https` on the same host; any other cross-origin redirect is a connection error naming that origin, instead of re-sending the call and the connector's auth headers there.

- A supervised agent can be a person's **human delegate** on the Lattice without the operator's host credential (car-releases#109). The operator grants it with `delegate_for: ["human:<name>"]` on the agent's spec (`agents.upsert`, host-only; an install keeps the grant already recorded for the id and never takes one from a publisher's manifest; personal agents only). Over its own agent connection the delegate is notified of that person's requests and answers (`lattice.human_request` / `lattice.human_answered` notifications), may read that person's requests with `lattice.requests` (only that person's rows), answer them with `lattice.respond` (recorded as `by: "delegate:<agent id>"`, and the asker is told: every answer from a person's node now carries `answered_by` — `host`, `delegate:<agent id>` or `approval` — on the `agent.peer_message` push, in an MCP inbox, from `lattice.wait`, and across a Lattice connection as `carPeerAnsweredBy`; never for a request it asked or forwarded itself, and never a `review_request`, which is an approval and stays the operator's: `approval_is_host_only`), set that person's status and note with the new `lattice.human.status` (capabilities, display name and project stay as the operator declared them), forward a question it received to that person with `agents.message { to: "human:<name>", on_behalf_of: <id of the delivered message> }` (CAR records the real asker, connection, body and kind from its own delivery record — the delegate's `body` is kept apart as `forward_note`, and it cannot turn a question into a review — charges the 10-pending cap to the asker, stamps `forwarded_by` and `forwarded_from` on the request and the approval row of a forwarded review, and delivers the answer to the asker directly with `in_reply_to` naming the asker's own message, so the asker waits on the id it already has; an answer to another owner's CAR crosses from the delegate's node, which that CAR asked), and read `multiplayer.list` / `multiplayer.get` (git then runs with a minimal environment, no system config, no file or `ext::` transport, and the repository's program-running keys overridden). Consent stays the operator's: `acknowledge_processing`, `agents.message.pending` / `.approve`, `lattice.connect.*`, `lattice.connections`, human registration and approval resolution are refused to a delegate, and an `agents.upsert` that changes `delegate_for` is refused to anything but the host client, even on a daemon without a host token. A worker never carries a grant, whatever its bundle declares. Removing the entry revokes it on the agent's next call, including over a connection already open. `lattice.nodes` lists each of this CAR's people with `delegates`.
- **Breaking (bindings):** `HostClient.latticeRequests` / `HostClient.latticeRespond` (Python `HostClient.lattice_requests` / `HostClient.lattice_respond`) were removed from the npm and PyPI packages. `lattice.requests` and `lattice.respond` moved from the host-only method set to the agent role so a person's delegate can call them, and the generated wrappers follow the role table: they are now `CarRuntime.latticeRequests` / `latticeRespond` (`lattice_requests` / `lattice_respond`), which send the caller's own credential — right for a delegate, refused (`not_a_delegate`) for any other process. A host-side operator process that used the `HostClient` wrapper calls `runtime.daemonCallHostManagement("lattice.requests", paramsJson)` (Python `daemon_call_host_management`) instead; the CLI already does. The wire protocol is unchanged. `multiplayer.list` / `multiplayer.get` are role `agent` (a delegate's read) instead of `operator_only`.
- A refused call on a person's Lattice node now has its own error code, `-32020`, with `error.data.reason`: `processing_notice_pending` (the answer waits for the operator to agree to the cross-owner processing notice; `data.connection` names the connection), `consent_is_host_only`, `approval_is_host_only`, `not_a_delegate`, `not_delegate_for_human`, `self_answer`, `forward_not_found` or `forward_not_a_question`. The message text of the processing-notice refusal is unchanged.
- `agent.peer_message` pushes and `lattice.requests` rows carry provenance an agent can tier trust on without the host-only `lattice.connections`: `connection`, `verified_by` (`fingerprint`, `tofu`, `org:<org>` or `cert:<org>:<account>`), `verified_org`, `verified_account` and `same_org` (whether the certifying org is one this CAR's owner belongs to). The protocol reference now says what an `unacknowledged` delivery means (written, not redelivered, may still be handled; acknowledge first and work after), which lattice fields agents depend on, and how a second attach with the same agent credential supersedes the first connection. No wire-protocol version change: every field is additive.

- The `human_delegate_ws` test suite now raises its compiler recursion limit, as the other suites that drive the WebSocket dispatcher already do, so it builds on Linux and Windows and under the release profile.

- A streamed reply whose caller has disconnected by the time the stream settles is no longer recorded as a success on the API key; it only frees the key's slot. CAR cannot see whether a disconnected caller read the final event, so two edges remain: a caller that read it and disconnected before the stream settled is released rather than counted, and a caller that stays connected without reading and disconnects only afterwards is still counted as a success. A successful HTTP response whose body CAR cannot parse is recorded as a failure on the key, with no tokens, matching the error the caller receives.
- A Codex CLI model is not listed as available while CAR's first `codex login status` check for it is still running, so a signed-out Codex no longer appears usable for the first few seconds after start. A check that fails or times out still leaves an installed Codex available, as before.
- On-device Foundation Models structured output now reports a constraint it cannot enforce as a schema degradation, instead of dropping it silently: numeric bounds (`minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`), string constraints (`pattern`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `format`) and array constraints (`minItems`, `maxItems`, `uniqueItems`).
- A multi-turn conversation sent to an on-device model, and the coder discussion transcript the coder distills into an intent, indent each turn's text, so text inside a turn that looks like a speaker label cannot pass for a turn of its own.

- Two `car-inference` test fixes. On an Apple Silicon Mac, the model-maintenance tests no longer depend on which models the machine has cached: they point the Hugging Face hub at their own temporary cache, and their fixtures carry the tokenizer and weight files a real snapshot has. The test-environment lock's 30-second backstop now fails only when the lock stops changing hands, so a long but moving queue of tests under `cargo test` no longer trips it. Its message now names a stuck holder instead of blaming lock order for a long wait. Test-only: no runtime behavior changes.

- `agents.install` (and `car install`, and the in-process `agents_install` binding) no longer replaces an agent already installed under the manifest's id without a word. It refuses, changing nothing, and names the installed agent and its version: "agent <id> is already installed (version <v>); nothing was changed. To replace it with version <w> on purpose, install it as an upgrade: `car install --upgrade`, or `upgrade: true` on agents.install". The same version is always refused as "agent <id> <v>: this version is already installed", with the way to install it again (`car uninstall <id>` first); versions compare by semver when both parse, so `v1.0.0` is `1.0.0`. A different version, an older one included (a rollback is an explicit upgrade), replaces the installed agent only with the new `car install --upgrade` flag or a top-level `upgrade: true` in the `agents.install` params, and then replaces it as before. An install never switches an id between a supervised agent and a `pure_data` / `health_url`-only bundle; that is refused with "Remove it first". An agent enrolled by `agents.upsert`, or a `pure_data` bundle tracked on disk only, holds its id the same way, and of two installs of a new id at the same moment exactly one is installed. An install id is validated before any path is built from it, so an id like `x/../notes` is refused instead of overwriting another agent's manifest. `agents.remove` of a `pure_data` or `health_url`-only agent now deletes its `~/.car/agents/<id>/` folder and reports `removed: true`; before, it removed nothing. The installed version is now recorded as `AgentSpec.version` (the manifest's `agent.version`), and an `agents.upsert` that names no version keeps it, as it keeps the token. `agents.upsert` still adds or replaces (car#3264).

- CarHost's Model Library and model setup no longer offer "Use in CAR Chat" for an installed model this Mac cannot run (for example downloaded GGUF weights on Apple Silicon, where CAR runs local text only through MLX). The daemon already marks such a row `platform_compatible: false`, and its installed weights never run here: CAR either refuses the row or quietly runs a different model, its MLX twin. Installed models CAR can run keep the action.

- On a cloud CAR, an agent can no longer see or act on other agents (#3257). A session bound to a supervised agent now sees only its own row in `declagents.list`, `declagents.get`, `registry.list` and `host.agents`, and only its own paused workflow runs in `workflow.list_paused` and `workflow.resume` (a refused resume is logged and leaves the run for its owner). `fleet.composite`, `fleet.inventory`, `tasks.list` and `scheduler.os_list` are refused to such a session with a plain reason because they have no "own rows". On Linux it is also refused `tasks.schedule`, `connectors.add_stdio` and `browser.run`, which make the daemon start a program outside the agent's wall. The Mac does not change for those three, and host, operator and CLI sessions are unchanged everywhere. Paused workflow checkpoints and `workflow.list_paused` rows gain an optional `owner` field.

- An agent now sees only its own records. A supervised agent that binds a memory namespace gets its own private graph (`agent:<id>:namespace:<ns>`), so two agents that pick the same namespace name no longer share facts, and `agents.list` returns an agent-bound session only that agent's own row instead of every agent's spec, `env` values and log paths. An agent-bound session's `memory.load` and `memory.persist` touch only the file of its own bound graph, and `agents.health` returns only its own row. The `registry.*` methods and `meeting.list` / `meeting.get` refuse a caller-named `registry_path` / `root` from an agent-bound session. Operator, host and `car` CLI sessions still see every row and bind the bare namespace name as before. Facts an agent stored under a bare namespace name before this change stay there for operator and host sessions; the agent starts empty under its own key. Step 4 of CAR in the Cloud agent isolation (`docs/proposals/cloud-agent-isolation.md`).

- On Linux, a supervised agent can now call only the daemon methods its own role and a short reviewed list allow (#3257). Every other method is refused with `<method> is not available to a supervised agent` and the refusal is logged, including the A2A methods (`SendMessage`, `ListTasks`, ...) and `coder.start`, `foreman.run`, `vision.ocr`, `transcribe`, `synthesize`, `models.register`, `declagents.invoke` and `scheduler.os_uninstall`, which ran outside the agent's folder wall and could read or write other agents' files. `agents.invoke_external`, `agents.chat`, `evolution.run` and `sync.*` (outside a work context) are refused too, host-role methods are refused whether or not a host token exists, a work context no longer exempts a session, and the built-in assistant is recognised by its daemon-registered binary, not its id. The Mac, host, operator and CLI sessions, and the built-in assistant are unchanged. A walled agent also cannot resolve approvals (`host.resolve_approval`), cannot call the operator's connector tools through `proposal.submit`, and can update or delete only the A2UI surfaces it created.

- Release lab: a promotion now opens its stable's bookkeeping pull request on its own. The lab's checkout is a worktree of a mirror clone, which has no `origin/main`, so v0.58.0's bookkeeping died after `DONE` and main kept the previous version and every consumed fragment. The step's `bookkeeping.log` is now published with the run record and printed by `car-release log`.

- Release lab: the lab retries opening the stable bookkeeping pull request itself (five attempts, doubling backoff) instead of leaving a person to run `bookkeeping-pr.sh`.

- Release lab: when enabling auto-merge on the stable bookkeeping pull request fails, the retry now requests auto-merge again instead of reporting success because the pull request exists. An attempt counts as done only when the pull request has merged, has auto-merge enabled, or is in the merge queue; otherwise it fails, and `bookkeeping.log` names the pull request and the `gh pr merge` command that queues it by hand. When the release branch was pushed but opening its pull request failed, the retry opens and queues the pull request from the pushed commit (after checking it is exactly the bookkeeping commit) instead of failing every retry on a rejected push. Only pull requests from the repository's own release branch count (a fork's pull request from a same-named branch is ignored), and a merged one is preferred over an open one, and an open one over a closed one. A pull request closed without merging now fails the attempt unless `main` already records the stable.

- Release lab: nightly catch-up now shows up everywhere once it lands. CI records each `catch-up-<lane>.txt` marker on the `car-releases` mirror as well as the primary, so `verify-release.sh --scope full` no longer fails on `asset count mismatch` after every lane succeeded. `--scope mac` reports each lane as `DONE catch-up attached`, `PEND catch-up pending`, or `FAIL catch-up failed` instead of always saying pending. A finished nightly's run record now gets its catch-up states written back and republished, both on `car-release status` and every ten minutes from the notices drain.

- Release lab: the catch-up sync now reads every nightly in its window. It used to look at only the ten newest runs of any kind, so after a busy stretch of updates and promotions a recent nightly's run record could stay `pending` until it aged out. When `car-release status` and the notices drain sync the same nightly at once, neither overwrites the newer catch-up states the other wrote: a sync whose read is overtaken leaves the record to the other one, and a publish that fails keeps the newer states; both say so on stderr. A failed run-record publish no longer replaces a log link another publish has just written with the `car-release log` fallback. When GitHub does not answer, the sync stops after the first failed read instead of waiting out a timeout for every nightly.

- Release lab: every nightly or promotion that does not finish DONE now reports itself once, with one Teams post and one GitHub issue. This covers a failed step, a failure while planning (before a commit or build id exists, which used to break the notice renderer and stay silent), an interrupted run, and a run found dead by the next command (the 2026-10-17 02:30Z scheduled nightly, which nobody announced). A step name missing from the name table now gets the generic label "an unnamed step" instead of crashing the notifier. Failing registry clones and run-record clones or pushes now log the real error line.

- Release lab: a missing `actions: write` grant on the lab GitHub App now shows as a `WARN ... needs-person` row in `lab-health` instead of a failure, so it no longer blocks `car-release update` or the nightly. Only the `promote_tag` recovery dispatch needs it, and `lab-promote` still stops with a message naming `actions: write` when it is missing.

- Release lab: full `lab-health.sh` now runs a suite listed twice in `scripts/ci/release-lab-tests.d` (or in `CAR_LAB_HEALTH_TESTS`) twice, as the CI runner does. It used to skip the repeat silently, so a suite whose second run fails could pass health and then fail CI.

- Release lab: retrying a nightly that failed after its tag was pushed now finishes it, when retried on the UTC day of its version or the next day. After that the planner decides again, so a version that cannot be resumed never blocks later nightlies. Before this change the retry asked the planner again, the planner answered `already-cut` because today's tag existed, and the nightly stayed half-published until someone deleted the tag by hand. The retry now resumes the recorded plan from its step ledger. It checks that origin's tag still names the recorded commit and Build-Id, puts back the archived macOS files instead of rebuilding them, skips the publishing steps that already finished, and runs the Mac-side verifier again. If the tag has moved to another commit, the retry ends `REFUSED tag-mismatch` and names both commits.
- Release lab: `car-release status` now shows when the Linux and Windows catch-up builds are attached to a nightly. Its `Catch-up:` line reads each lane from the release's assets (`attached`, `failed` or `pending`), separately from the `Mac side:` line. Before this change the line read `pending` forever.

- Release lab: when a promotion's promote-publish job fails, `lab-promote` now dispatches the `promote_tag` recovery itself (and fails naming `actions: write` if the lab App lacks that permission); `lab-health` gains a "GitHub Actions write" row.

- Release lab: `lab-promote` no longer hides a failed GitHub read. During `wait-ci`, a read that fails (the markers, the tag run, the `promote-publish` check, the dispatch listing, a job) was taken as "no answer yet": a failed tag-run read meant no recovery was dispatched, and the operator saw only the marker timeout an hour later. Each failure is now printed as `wait-ci: <read> failed (exit <N>: <last two lines of its error>)`, cleaned and redacted like admission's `remote-failed`. An answer waiting cannot change fails the step naming the read (GitHub's missing-grant 403 at once; HTTP 401 or a run read's 404 when the same read repeats it on the next poll); a 5xx, a rate limit, a network failure or a release read's 404 keeps polling to the deadline, whose timeout names it. A recovery dispatch refused with any 403 other than GitHub's missing-grant answer is no longer blamed on `actions: write`, and one that failed on a server error or a lost connection says it may still have gone through; a failed npm or PyPI read is reported as unreadable rather than as a stale latest; a failed read of whether the stable release exists, or of its assets, stops the upload naming the read. `lab-health` reports a GitHub read as `read refused` only when GitHub's answer says so, and any other failure as `read failed` with its status and message; a failed run listing no longer passes the "GitHub Actions jobs" row as "no run exists" (car#2940).

- Release-lab promotions now run the changelog assembly script from the lab's own checkout instead of the promoted nightly's frozen copy, so a fix to promotion tooling reaches a promotion of an older nightly.

- Release lab promotions now refuse an unpromotable nightly before anything starts. `car-release promote` checks the nightly before taking the run lock or creating a run record, prints one named reason (`REFUSED too-old`, `not-lab-built`, `catch-up-missing`, `run-failed`, `run-unfinished`, and the rest) followed by `nothing was started for <nightly>`, and exits 1; before, the refusal came from inside a started run and the command exited 0 with `no plan was recorded`. During a promotion `car-release status` now names the nightly being promoted, and every finished promotion shows `Promoted from:` and `Verifier: pass|fail|pending`. CI now records `npm-latest-moved.txt` and `pypi-latest-moved.txt` on the `car-releases` stable release as well as the primary, and the lab waits for both before verifying, so the primary and mirror stable releases list the same assets and the stable verifier's equal-count check can pass.

- A release lab promotion is reported `already done` only for the nightly it actually promoted. Before, `car-release promote <nightly>` exited 0 with `already done: <stable> published and verified` whenever any nightly of the same version had finished promoting, so a request for a different nightly reported success without checking or promoting it. That request now goes to admission, which refuses it with `REFUSED already-published: <stable> exists, promoted from <nightly>`, prints `nothing was started for <nightly>`, and exits 1 (car#2830).
- A release lab promotion no longer skips steps that a promotion of a different nightly of the same version completed. Before, a promotion that failed after `relabel` and before `tag` let a later promotion of another nightly of that version skip `preflight`, `fetch` and `relabel`, although that work lived in the first nightly's cache. A promotion now reuses a step only from an earlier run of the same source nightly (car#2830).
- `car-release promote` no longer waits forever when GitHub or the vault stops answering during admission. Each `git ls-remote origin` tag read is limited to 30 seconds and the whole admission to 120 seconds; past either limit the request prints `REFUSED remote-timeout: …` or `REFUSED admission-timeout: …`, `nothing was started for <nightly>`, and exits 1, and the timed-out checks' processes are stopped (car#2830).

- `car-release promote` now names a remote read that fails at once instead of blaming the nightly. A `git ls-remote origin` or GitHub read that fails with a DNS, authentication, transport or server error is refused as `REFUSED remote-failed: <read> failed (exit <N>: <last two error lines>)`, followed by `nothing was started for <nightly>` and exit 1. The error has control characters removed and secrets redacted before it reaches `car-release status` or a notice. Before, a failed nightly tag read was reported as `not-lab-built`, a failed release read as `catch-up-missing`, and a failed stable read as "stable absent", which could admit a promotion the already-published check should have stopped. Only an HTTP 404 from GitHub now counts as absent, and only after admission has confirmed that the token can read the repository, since GitHub answers 404 for a repository it hides too (car#3183).

- Release lab: the schedule command no longer runs code the `car-release` service account can change as root. `setup-lab.sh` now installs a root-owned copy at `/usr/local/car-lab/sbin/car-lab-schedule.sh`, and the runbook runs `sudo /bin/bash /usr/local/car-lab/sbin/car-lab-schedule.sh on|off|show` instead of the copy in the service checkout. As root, `schedule.sh` refuses before doing anything unless its own file and every directory above it, on the invoked and the resolved path, are owned by root with no group or world write bit and no ACL entry granting write, and the refusal names the path. Root also takes every command from the system directories, never the caller's PATH, and reads and writes `schedule.json` and publishes it only as `car-release`. Health warns, without failing, when the copy is missing or stale. Rerun `bash scripts/lab/setup-lab.sh` as the rental administrator to install the copy; until then the old checkout command refuses with the path to use.

- Release lab: a scheduled nightly now runs where a manual one does, in `car-release`'s Background launchd context. The first scheduled tick ran as a `car-release` job in the system domain, where `nohup` cannot adopt a session; its detached runner never started and the run was recorded `INTERRUPTED planning`. The nightly LaunchDaemon now starts as root only to enter that context with `launchctl asuser` and `sudo -u car-release`, sets `AbandonProcessGroup` so the run outlives the scheduler's exit, and has launchd open no file as root. `setup-lab.sh` is now the plist's only writer: `schedule.sh on` used to rewrite it with different bytes, which made every later `car-release update` fail its setup check. The scheduler also refuses to start a run outside that context. `car-release update` cannot deliver this change: an administrator must run `setup-lab.sh` from a setup checkout at this commit, then `schedule.sh off` and `schedule.sh on`.

- Release lab: log excerpts and notices now redact Azure client secrets (the `~`-bearing secret format) and `*_CLIENT_SECRET=` / `*SECRET*=` assignments before they reach a Teams post or GitHub issue, and the notice gate refuses text that still holds one.

- Release lab: setup now installs `cmake`, which the Mac build needs to compile whisper.cpp (the first lab nightly failed at mac-build because it was missing). Setup prints its version, the lab health command reports it, and a release refuses before any build step, naming `cmake` and the `brew install cmake` fix, if it is absent.

- Release lab: when `car-release status` cannot read a nightly's release from GitHub (an outage, a timeout, a refused token), its `Catch-up:` line now ends with `(recorded states; GitHub could not be read)` and stderr says `car-release: could not read <tag> catch-up from GitHub (<gh error>)`. It used to show the states stored in the run record as if they were current, so lanes whose files had landed read as pending. That message and the catch-up sync's own now redact any secret in gh's error before printing it.
- CI promotion: `promote-publish`'s wait for `promotion-assets-complete.txt` no longer treats a release it could not read (a refused mirror token, an outage) as one without the marker. The poll line shows `could not read (<gh error>)`, redacted, and the final error says the release could not be read instead of that the marker is still missing.

- Release lab: `car-release status` no longer takes over a minute. It checked every stable tag ever published (86 GitHub calls, about 33 s) for each nightly, rounded each vault read up to a whole second, and ran them one after another; it now reads only the tag that can belong to the nightly, polls in tenths of a second, and does the vault reads and each nightly's GitHub reads at the same time. A failed `car-release update` now shows the lines of the step that failed instead of an empty "Step log" block. `scripts/lab/check-release-actors.sh` no longer passes a window in which a person uploaded release assets to a mirror release whose `created_at` is its commit date.

- A stable promotion no longer fails because the release lab verified the Windows installer before CI had rebuilt it. The lab's `wait-ci` step now also waits for `build.yml`'s `promote-windows-installer` job and runs `verify` only after it passes. The job that counts is the newest run of it for the stable: a `promote_tag` recovery dispatch counts, and `build.yml` now names such a run `promote vX.Y.Z` so a dispatch for another stable never does. A failed job, or a tag whose `build.yml` lacks the job, fails `wait-ci` at once naming the run and the recovery; a job still running at the deadline fails it with a timeout naming the job. Each GitHub read in the wait is bounded by `CAR_LAB_PROMOTE_GH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 60) and an error counts as still pending (car#2932).

- The car.parslee.ai landing page headline now reads "The runtime a business runs its agents on. On machines it owns."

- car.parslee.ai install section: the full `scoop bucket add` command now wraps inside its box instead of being cut off, and the macOS and Windows download buttons line up on one row on desktop.

- The car.parslee.ai landing page now offers the Mac installer (`CAR-darwin-arm64.pkg`, for Apple Silicon Macs) as a direct download beside the Windows one, and the run-history access note in the WebSocket reference no longer cites an internal tracking id.

- An answer to an organization's message from one of this owner's other devices is now admitted only from that organization and only to the device that sent it. Before, a session in another organization could reuse the message's id to reach an address no listing showed it. `lattice.wait` likewise returns a reply pushed to an attached agent, or a person's answer found by address, only in the collaboration context it was asked from (the same organization under any member account, or the same personal account), so an agent id enrolled again in another context does not read the old one's replies (#2807).

- `lattice.wait` finds a reply pushed to an organization's agent again when the asker waits under another member account of the same organization. Since #2908 it compared the whole work context, account included, so an admitted reply could go unfound and the wait timed out with no error. A reply pushed into another organization or a personal context still stays invisible. Rejoining the Lattice under another member account of the same organization also no longer releases the claims that address holds in the organization's claim table (#2909).

- `mail.messages` with `all_mailboxes: true` now names what it did not read when it reads nothing. A locked Envelope Index used to come back `available: false` with `unresolved` empty; it now lists every mailbox of the selected accounts (`timed_out: true`), still without reading any message through Apple Events. Naming them takes one Apple Events walk of the mailbox names, bounded by 2 s (or `timeout_ms` if lower); if it does not finish, each requested account is listed with `mailbox: null`. When Mail reports it cannot list the accounts' mailboxes, each requested account is listed with `mailbox: null` too. With no `account_ids` in either of those whole-account cases there is no account to name, so `unresolved` stays empty.
- `assistant.identity.set` refuses an `apps` list of more than 32 distinct names, and a `role` or app name longer than 120 characters, the way it already refused too many spellings. Both go into every built-in system prompt, and the list had no limit. `car_identity::AssistantIdentity::with_role` and `with_apps` now return `Result`.
- `car_bench::ensemble_eval::analyze` refuses records it used to call interpretable: an arm whose players had no time (80 minutes against 0 passed the budget check), more than one depth player, two roster entries with one identity, and a finding timed after its player's session ended. Each is a new blocking `Integrity` variant.
- `car_harness_opt::search` no longer exceeds its evaluation budget when `budget` is not larger than `restarts`: a later restart's start is scored only out of a non-zero share. The seed is always scored, so a `budget` of 0 spends one evaluation, as documented on `SearchConfig::budget`.
- Skill evolution from recorded outcomes retries after a failed model call. A rate limit or network error used to count as an attempt, so the domain was not tried again until another outcome arrived.
- The `mcp_smoke` example fails when the unpoliced call returns no result, instead of printing `RESULT: direction 2 OK`.

- `car install`, `car uninstall`, `car start`, `car stop`, `car restart`, `car approvals default|set-tool|reset-tool`, and `car do`'s registration with CarHost (the older-daemon fallback and `car do --serve --governed-host`) now present CAR's local host key only after the person at the terminal answers yes (`... with CAR's permission? [y/N]`, asked on stderr), the rule `car agent new` follows. With the new `-y`/`--yes` flag or with no terminal (stdin and stderr), they never present the key, so a daemon with a host token refuses them and says why; a daemon with no host token still admits them. With `CAR_AGENT_ID` or `CAR_AGENT_TOKEN` set they never present it either. An agent with a shell tool can no longer install, start, stop or remove agents, or change approval policy, through CAR's own CLI by borrowing the host key. The Windows tray dashboard's agent Start / Stop / Restart buttons and its setup wizard's approval preset now go out on the tray's own host-authenticated connection instead of running `car start|stop|restart` and `car approvals default`. When `car do` cannot register Parslee Core through an older daemon (refused, declined, unreachable) it now says so on stderr and continues. The create-car-agent skill tells an agent to ask the user to start, stop or install an agent (CarHost, or their own terminal) rather than run those commands itself. CarHost, CAR's boot-time registration of Parslee Core, `car claude`, `car models`, `car approvals get|evaluate-tool` and the SDKs are unchanged. (#2444)

- On Linux, CAR now locks every agent it starts into its own folder with Landlock, a feature of the Linux kernel that CAR applies itself when it starts the agent: nothing to install, no extra users, no Docker or host setting, with or without root, in the stock container or on a server running `car-server` directly. An agent can read and write only `<CAR_HOME>/agents/<id>/data/` (its working folder, `HOME` and `TMPDIR`), read its own code and `manifest.toml`, and run the system's ordinary programs; CAR's token files, key store, state folder and every other agent's folder are refused by the kernel, and so is everything the agent starts. This needs Linux 6.2 or newer with Landlock enabled (Ubuntu 24.04 and current cloud images qualify; Debian 12 and the original Ubuntu 22.04 kernel do not), so that an agent cannot empty other files by truncating them. Where the kernel cannot fully enforce the wall, the agent does not start: it shows `errored` with the reason "This server's Linux kernel can't confine agents to their own folders", and is not retried. The daemon logs the kernel's Landlock ABI at start, and which extras are active: on Linux 6.12 or newer an agent also cannot signal processes outside its wall or connect to abstract Unix sockets, and on Linux 7.1 or newer it cannot connect to pathname Unix sockets outside its folder (on older kernels a same-user program on a Unix socket, such as tmux or `systemd --user`, could act for an agent; our Docker image has none; keeping such programs off the server is the server owner's job: run CAR as its own system user with nothing else under it, or use the Docker image). Agents also get `/dev/shm` read-write, because Python `multiprocessing` (and likely Chromium) cannot work without it; other agents' named shared-memory objects are visible there. A `cwd` outside the agent's own folder is refused, and no path in an agent's manifest (`args`, `cwd`, `command`) grants access to anything outside its folder and the system paths; a `command` outside its folder and `/usr` (including `/usr/local`), `/nix/store` and the other system paths is refused. The agent ids `parslee-core` and `car-assistant` are reserved for CAR's own assistant: `agents.upsert` and bundle install refuse them. The Mac is unchanged. The built-in assistant's shell on Linux now also hides CAR's state folder (except the folder it was asked to work in), and runs under Landlock alone where the `unshare` sandbox cannot start (the stock container), where it used to be refused, and on Linux 7.1 or newer that fallback also refuses connecting to a Unix socket by path outside its allowed folders (a path session bus included). Still open on Linux, and closed by a separate step: an agent can reach CAR's own dashboard and MCP ports on `127.0.0.1`. See `docs/proposals/cloud-agent-isolation.md` (step 3).

- Security (Linux): files and folders the secret sandbox hides from a command, such as `$CAR_HOME/env` with the operator's provider keys and the daemon's socket and token folders, now stay hidden whatever other folders the sandbox locks down. Before, on Linux, a hidden file or folder inside a folder the sandbox also made read-only, such as `$CAR_HOME` itself, could be read by the sandboxed command. The sandbox now hides files and folders after it has set up every other folder, and starts the command from its working folder as seen after that setup. macOS was not affected. The Linux CI `test` job and the release `test` job now enable unprivileged user namespaces with `scripts/ci-enable-linux-sandbox.sh` and run the secret sandbox's tests with the sandbox on, so those tests run on Linux rather than skip.

- Linux: a sandboxed CarCoder check whose working folder sits inside the CAR state folder, such as a session worktree under `$CAR_HOME/coder/worktrees`, can now write to that worktree and to its own evidence and scratch folders. Before, the Linux sandbox made the whole state folder read-only and ignored these per-check exceptions, which macOS already honored, so such a check could not write its own files. The rest of the state folder stays read-only, folders CAR keeps immutable stay read-only even inside a worktree, and hidden files stay hidden.

- CarCoder on Linux: a path the sandbox policy named, such as a state root or a protected directory, can be deleted between building the policy and the sandbox reaching it, and so can the whole directory that holds it. A mount step whose target is provably gone no longer fails setup (exit 125, "mount point does not exist", which reached users as "Cargo PATH probe returned no closing delimiter"). "Provably gone" means the nearest existing ancestor is a directory that lists cleanly and lacks the next component on the way down. This covers the phase-1 mounts, the phase-2 blocks and the explicit read-only remounts of the policy's read-only paths. The check runs `command ls` with `QUOTING_STYLE=literal LC_ALL=C`, so `ls` output formatting variables and shell functions cannot change the verdict, and a path with a `.` or `..` component is never gone. A path that merely cannot be checked (an I/O error on a network home, an unreadable or non-directory ancestor), a mount that fails with its target present, and the read-only remount of host mounts found in mountinfo (which still fails closed) all still fail setup (#3017).

- Linux: CarCoder's sandboxed commands no longer fail with "car: secret sandbox setup failed" (exit 125) while a Docker container is running on the same machine. Before a command runs, the sandbox makes every mount it can reach read-only. A running container's filesystem sits under Docker's root-only directory, where the sandbox cannot reach it, so making it read-only was refused. The sandbox now skips a mount only when the folder above it cannot be entered; the command inside cannot enter that folder either. Any other mount it cannot find or cannot make read-only still stops the command.
- Linux: the sandbox now reads mount paths with escaped characters correctly. A mount whose name has a space followed by a digit (such as a drive called "Backup 2024" or "Disk 7") or ends with a newline was read under the wrong name. The command then stopped with a setup failure even though the drive was reachable. Such mounts are now found and made read-only like any other.

- Linux: CarCoder's independent verifier now runs isolated on Linux in CAR's default layout, so a headless `car code` run on Linux can deliver. Before, when the verifier's frozen copy and evidence folder sat inside the CAR state folder, which is where CAR puts them, Linux reported verifier isolation as unavailable: `run_check` refused to run and headless delivery was blocked. The Linux sandbox now hides the state folder from the verifier and gives back only those two folders, as macOS already did. Everything else in the state folder stays hidden. The folders above them can be passed through but not listed, and inside a write-confined sandbox the folders given back are writable only where the sandbox already allowed writes. As on macOS, the verifier's shell on Linux also no longer sees the shared `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` folders, and each `run_check` keeps its private state in a short folder of its own under `/tmp`.

- Unattended self-healing's local models no longer refuse each other. Under a local-only spend scope, where there is no remote route to fall back to, a local model that fits the Local Models RAM allocation on its own is no longer refused because an idle local model from an earlier request still holds memory. CAR releases the smallest idle local model that makes room, or several largest first, and only when releasing them can actually make room. A model starting up or serving a request is never released. Everywhere else, a refusal at the allocation still sends the router to its next route, as before. The self-heal review panel also asks its local reviewers one at a time. Before this, every reviewer was refused beside the coder that had just finished, so a fix the local coder made could never pass review.
- A contract check whose own `assert` compares the claimed value (`python3 -c "from greet import greet; assert greet(7) == 'Hello, 7'"`) now counts as asserting it. Before, it was held as asserting nothing, which could leave a contract with no runnable check.

- Local model memory estimates now match what models actually use, measured through vllm-mlx on an M5 Pro. Before, Qwen3.8-27B was estimated at 51 GiB for a 64k-token context that peaks at 24 GiB, so the Everyday preset refused it past about 9k tokens. GLM-4.7-Flash 8-bit was estimated at 45 GiB for a 64k context that peaks at 53 GiB, so CAR admitted loads the machine could not hold. Four changes:
  - CAR now reads a model's `config.json` from wherever it is actually served, including the Hugging Face cache snapshot that `ensure_local` reuses. Before, those rows fell back to a parameter-count guess.
  - Layers that keep no per-token cache (Qwen3.5+ linear attention) are no longer counted. Their fixed state is counted once.
  - Multi-head latent attention models (GLM-4.7-Flash, DeepSeek-V3) are sized by their compressed cache plus the memory needed to expand it while the prompt is processed.
  - Models served with a drafter count the full-vocabulary logits of a 2048-token prompt chunk, which mlx-vlm computes (2.8 GiB on Qwen3.8).
  
  The two rows' `ram_mb` is now their measured resident size. Every estimate is within 6 GiB above the measured peak and never below it.

- The model catalog carries re-measured local and frontier scores (car-judged suite, M5 Pro 64 GB, 2026-10-26). Judged tasks now run with `thinking: auto`, as production requests do; before, the suite asked reasoning models not to think. Best local quality: gpt-oss-20b 0.971 at 77.6 tok/s, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 0.893 at 92.3 tok/s, Qwen3.8-27B 0.887 at 33.9 tok/s (with its drafter). Every native frontier row except the two Gemini rows now has a car-judged score and a measured answer rate, so `prefer_quality` ranks frontier models against each other on one benchmark instead of on each vendor's own (Sonnet 4.6 and the GPT-5.6 rows score 1.0, Opus 4.8 0.986, which is the suite's ceiling, not a tie in ability).
- The Gemma-4 rows serve Google's QAT 4-bit conversions; they pointed at full-precision repos whose listed sizes were about 4x too small. New rows: Gemma-4-31B, gpt-oss-20b, Devstral-Small-2-24B and Qwen3.5 4B/2B/0.8B. The 2B and 0.8B score 0.18 and 0.05 on the judged suite and suit only trivial tasks.

- A saved agent can now keep everything it reads on this Mac. The Agent Builder's privacy step has a "Keep everything this agent reads on this Mac" switch (off by default, including for every starter), and a chat draft can carry it as a `local_only` yes/no answer that needs the person's own words. It is stored as `builder_draft.local_only` (default `false`, omitted when off, so existing agents keep their JSON, fingerprint and behaviour); the runtime reads that field, never the free-text privacy answer, and an edit started without answers keeps the agent's stored ones. For such an agent, every model call that sees what it reads uses a model on this Mac: writing and repairing its spec during the build (the repair quotes its test cases' output), its test cases, `declagents.run_scenarios`, and every run. An unaddressed call routes with every model not on this Mac strictly excluded, so a cloud model that would score higher is never picked. A build is refused before any model call, with a "configuration" failure that names the keep-on-this-Mac setting and says to install or pick a model on this Mac or turn the setting off, when the model chosen to build it or the agent's saved model isn't on this Mac, or when no model on this Mac can build it; a run stops with an error naming the setting in the same cases, or when its saved model on this Mac isn't available (Parslee never stands in). The build's final check calls no verifier or auditor model, so a Mail agent's real Mail no longer reaches a model elsewhere during the build: the agent is saved as not independently checked ("It keeps everything on this Mac, so no AI model outside it reviewed the build."), never as passed, the session's `verification` receipt carries `kept_on_this_mac: true`, and CarHost shows that reason instead of saying no second AI model was available. "On this Mac" is a model CAR runs on-device (MLX, Candle GGUF, a CAR-managed vLLM-MLX, Apple's on-device model); an Ollama or external vLLM-MLX endpoint does not count, since it may be on another machine.
- `IntentHint` gains `on_device_only` (default `false`; accepted by `models.route`, `routeModel`/`route_model` intent JSON and generation requests). It is a hard constraint: the request is routed only with models CAR runs on this machine, checked against the registry it is routed with when it is sent (so a model added to the catalog later is never picked), a requested model elsewhere is refused, and with none left it fails with "no eligible model remains after required exclusions" before anything is sent. A local-only agent sets it on every model call.

- The model catalog scores five more local models on the 17-task `car-judged` suite: `vllm-mlx/glm-4.7-flash:8bit` 0.402 (its earlier run errored on every task) and `apple/foundation:default` 0.282, both new, plus fresh runs of `mlx/qwen3-30b-a3b:4bit` (0.470 over two runs), `mlx/qwen3-8b:4bit` (0.439) and `mlx/qwen3-4b:4bit` (0.370 over two runs). `vllm-mlx/gemma-4-31b-it:4bit` and `vllm-mlx/devstral-small-2-24b:4bit` stay unscored: 6 and 4 of their 17 tasks hit a 300 s request timeout, fixed separately. `vllm-mlx/gpt-oss-20b:mxfp4` keeps 77.6 tok/s; its recorded calibration (42.2) was taken under load.
