An in-place `agents.upsert` landing after the install (a new spec or a rotated token) still returns the started agent with its current spec (car#3160).

- `agents.start` (and the start half of `agents.restart`) now fails with `agent <id> not found` when a concurrent `agents.remove` drops the agent while the start is in flight, including when an agent with the same id and a new token is added back meanwhile. It used to report success with a made-up `starting` agent that no slot held and no process backed, or, after a re-add, to run the removed agent's command, environment, secrets and token under the new agent's name. When an `agents.upsert` replaces the spec while a start is in flight, the start now fails with `agent <id> changed while it was starting; nothing was started. Start it again to run its current spec` instead of running the old spec. A stale start also no longer stops the process of the agent that replaced it, and the daemon's boot-time `start_all` no longer counts an agent removed or replaced under it as started (car#3136).

- A Stop sent right after a chat turn is accepted now stops it. The daemon keeps an `agents.chat.cancel` for a session with no route yet for 60 seconds and refuses that client's next `agents.chat` / `agents.invoke_external` under the id with `the turn was cancelled before it started`, and once an agent acknowledges a turn whose route a Stop already removed it sends `agent.chat.cancel` again. `car do --serve` registers a turn's stop flag as it reads the `agent.chat` request, and the daemon client now calls a request handler in the order frames arrive (only the future it returns runs on a task), so a cancel written right behind `agent.chat` is no longer handled first and dropped. The Node and Python bindings queue an `agent.chat` turn in that ordered part too, and a cancel for a turn still waiting for the agent's chat handler now drops that turn and reports it cancelled; the agent's own `agent.chat.cancel` handler still hears every cancel. `car do --serve` stops every turn it accepted when the daemon ends its connection, since no cancel can reach them after that (new `DaemonClient::register_connection_lost_handler`). CarHost sends Stop again once the call of a turn it stopped before acknowledgement returns.
- **API change (`car-server-core`):** `AssistantService::handle_turn_with_model` and `handle_goal_turn_with_model` take an `AcceptedTurn` from the new `AssistantService::accept_turn(session_id)` in place of `session_id: &str`; `handle_turn` and `handle_goal_turn` keep their signatures. `AssistantService::serve_chat` serves `agent.chat` the way `car do --serve` does.

- Sandboxed checks on macOS find the operator's Homebrew `python3` again. A credential store holding a symlink into installed software (gcloud's virtualenv in `~/.config` links to Homebrew's interpreter; `~/.docker/cli-plugins` links into Docker.app) made CAR deny the interpreter itself, so bash skipped it on PATH and checks ran Xcode's `python3` without the operator's packages. Store links into Homebrew's Cellar/Caskroom, app bundles under `/Applications`, and the OS's own directories are no longer treated as store data; links to dotfiles and anywhere else still are.

- Streaming generate keeps the credential cause when every model fails: a stream whose Parslee or work-context credential is signed out, unreadable, denied or needs renewal now leads its error with that cause and its sign-in, membership or retry step, as the non-streaming path already did. It no longer reports only the last fallback's error. A stream that runs out of models also gets the same setup and re-authenticate hints as non-streaming generate.
- A request bound to a work context (buffered generate, streaming generate and classify) whose context credential cannot be used now reports that credential as the cause when routing without Parslee then fails too. Before, Parslee was left out of routing and the caller saw only an unrelated "model not found" or fallback error. A request that succeeds on another model is unchanged.

- Dropping a `car_registry::supervisor::Supervisor` now explicitly unlocks its manifest lock. Before, the lock was released only when the descriptor closed. While another thread in the process was forking a child, that child's inherited copy kept the lock held, so a supervisor reopened over the same manifest in the same process could fail with `AlreadyRunning`.

- The supervisor no longer puts the daemon-wide `CAR_AUTH_TOKEN` (or `CAR_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE` / `CAR_HOST_TOKEN`) into the environment of a supervised agent on Linux, or, on any platform, of an agent whose spec has `method_allowlist` or `work_context`. The removal runs last, so neither the daemon's default env nor the spec's own `env` can restore it. `CAR_AGENT_ID` and `CAR_AGENT_TOKEN` are unchanged, and unscoped agents on the Mac still receive `CAR_AUTH_TOKEN`. On Linux, an agent that used `car keys list` or the daemon token must use its declared keys and its agent session. `method_allowlist` scopes the agent credential; on the Mac it does not confine a same-user process (Parslee-ai/car#3008).

- Supplying a contract no longer approves its network checks (#2025). A check in a `coder.start` contract, a `car code` or `car code-task` `--contract-file`, or the FFI `contract_json` that must reach the network now carries its own `"network_approved": true`, which approves that exact check name and command, the same flag `coder.confirm_contract` already reads. Without it the check runs with network denied; the daemon holds a recognized network check under Not verified, where `coder.confirm_contract` can approve it, and `car code-task` refuses a contract file that has one, naming the checks. Declared credentials in a supplied contract are still approved as before. Verifier probes and `car coder-ab` mining probes in a supplied session no longer get network: they are not contract checks, so no flag approves them. Sessions saved before this change keep the approvals they recorded. `car coder-ab` corpus rows gain `network_approved_checks: [<check name>]` for the same purpose; both arms and the offline re-score honor it, and a name that is not a check in the row is refused at load.
- A completeness critic that fails is now retried once (on another model when its reply was unparseable). If the retry fails too, the session stops with `failure_kind: "infrastructure"` before any work runs, instead of proposing a contract that never had its completeness review. `outcomes_step` reports the critic as `retrying`, then `finished` or `failed`; it no longer reports `skipped`.

- Building CAR from source on a Mac whose `swift` defaults to the native SwiftPM build system (Swift 6.3.3 / Xcode 26.6) now links the in-process mlx-swift-lm text backend instead of building it and then dropping it with only a cargo warning. car-inference's build script now passes `--build-system swiftbuild`, the build system whose output layout and compiled Metal shaders it already depended on; a toolchain that does not know that value fails the Swift build and the script reports that error.

- Project `.car/` files are now looked for only from the working directory up to the git repository root, and CAR's own `~/.car` (or `$CAR_HOME`) is never read as a project. Before, three readers walked to the filesystem root. A team `.car/connectors.toml` search under your home directory could pick up `~/.car/connectors.toml` and connect every server in it. The project `.car/update-prefs.json` override could pick up your own user `~/.car/update-prefs.json` and count its policy as a team's choice. Meetings could be written into a `.car/` above the checkout, or into the old `~/.car` after `CAR_HOME` moved the state root. A file in the repository root, or in a folder between it and the working directory, is still found, also when the working directory is a symlink into the repository.
- Outside any git repository, team connectors are read only from the working directory's own `.car/connectors.toml`, the same as project policies; a team file in a parent folder no longer applies.
- `car do` and the coder no longer take `~/.car` as a project when run from your home directory: its `tool-labels.json`, `production-gates.toml` and (with `CAR_HOME` relocated) `policies/` are not loaded as project configuration. The policy check run from your home directory no longer reads the operator's rules twice.

- A tenant-scoped proposal (`scope.tenantId`) is now checked against the state each of its actions actually executes against (car#3121). `state_write`, `state_read` and `assertion` actions read and write the tenant's own keys, so the admission gates, the strict transactional pre-check, per-action preconditions and `state_dependencies`, replan verification and the per-action `state_before` a trajectory records now read the tenant's keys for them. Previously these checks read the shared store, so a tenant proposal whose dependency was in its own tenant state was refused as an unmeetable dependency, and a key that existed only in shared state passed the checks even though the action could not read it. `tool_call` actions run on the unscoped path, so their checks still read shared keys, as before. A tenant `state_write` therefore no longer counts as setting a key a later `tool_call` depends on. Under a tenant, those checks no longer see other tenants' keys: previously a tenant `tool_call` could name another tenant's stored `tenant:<id>:<key>` in a dependency or precondition and learn from the refusal whether it existed and what it held. A replanner for a tenant proposal is handed the state under raw key names, as before, minus other tenants' keys. Unscoped proposals are unchanged. Policies are the deliberate exception: a `require_state` policy still reads the shared store for a tenant proposal, because policies are operator rules and a tenant must not satisfy one by writing its own copy of the key. `car_validator::validate_action` and `check_precondition` now take any `car_ir::precondition::StateView` (a `&StateStore` still works). `ScopedStateView` implements `StateView`, `car_state::tenant_key`, `car_state::key_visible_to_tenant`, `StateStore::visible_to` and `StateStore::versioned_snapshot_visible_to` are added, and `car_engine::verify_gate::blocking_errors` takes the proposal's tenant.

- The transactional pre-check of a tenant-scoped proposal (`scope.tenantId`) now reports a conflict between a `tool_call` declaring an effect on a key and a tenant `state_write` of that key (write-write), or a tenant `state_read` / `assertion` reading it (read-write), when no dependency orders them (car#3133). A tool call's callback `state_changes` land in the tenant's namespace, so its declared `expected_effects` count as writes to both the shared key and the tenant's copy, which is how the static-verification gate already modeled them. Previously the pre-check counted them as shared writes only, so both actions ran and execution order decided the surviving value. In strict mode the conflicting actions are rejected; in warn mode the conflicts are recorded as `TransactionConflict` events and the actions run. The pre-check now takes ordering from the proposal as written, as the executor does, so a tenant action that lists the key in `state_dependencies` after the tool call is a sequenced step and runs, unless that action also writes the key: the executor records only the last declared writer of a key, so that pair conflicts, as it does in an unscoped proposal. Two unordered tool calls declaring the same key now report two write-write conflicts (the key and the tenant's copy) and reject the same two actions as before. An explicit `write_set` or `read_set` on a tenant `state_write`, `state_read` or `assertion` is now read in the tenant's namespace, so it no longer conflicts with a `tool_call` declaring the same raw key in its `write_set`, which only the tool's handler writes, in the shared store. `car_verify::check_transaction_ordered_by` is added: `check_transaction` with the "runs before" relation taken from a separate list of the same actions.

- Test suite: six tests that ended in a discarded `matches!(...)` (so they could never fail) now assert, and CI rejects any new discarded `matches!` result. The `car code-task` tests no longer copy the developer's whole Cargo registry into every baseline check, and test builds optimize the Argon2id and curve/hash/AEAD crypto dependencies, so those tests run in seconds instead of tens of seconds. Release builds and every KDF parameter are unchanged.

- A turn CAR recovers from a thinking-only pass (`stop_reason: "thinking_recovered"`) now reports the tokens and time of both passes. The pass that thought until its token ceiling and answered nothing was dropped from `usage` and `latency_ms`, so a recovered turn looked like a 30-token answer that took a minute: measured decode speed for thinking models read up to 60x low (gemma-4 tasks on vllm-mlx showed 0.5 tok/s against a real 34 tok/s), and the billed tokens of the discarded pass were missing from the usage callers sum. `usage.prompt_tokens` stays the retry's, since it is the context the turn ended at.

- A recovered thinking turn (`stop_reason: "thinking_recovered"`) whose retry or first pass reported no usage no longer shows the other pass's provider charge as the cost of the whole turn. The missing pass's output is now estimated (a first pass that stopped at its limit counts that limit), and `usage.reported_cost_usd` becomes the known provider charge plus the catalog price of the estimated pass. When that pass has no catalog price, the known charge stands for the turn. A turn's figure (including the sum of two provider figures) that lands above the sanity ceiling CAR applies to provider figures is now held at that ceiling instead of being dropped for the list price. Billing checks the turn against the price of the model that answered, so when the two passes ran on differently priced models the figure can still end below the first pass's charge. When neither pass reported usage, the turn reports none, as before.

- A Parslee token that expired while Parslee's token service was rate-limited or down no longer reports the account as signed out. `parslee.capabilities`, `parslee.auth`, Parslee product gates, Studio, the jev client and queued feedback used to answer "not signed in — run `car auth login`" because the stale token drew a 401 on the session check. That 401 now triggers one token renewal: a renewed token loads normally, a renewal that is temporarily unavailable is reported as a service failure ("You are still signed in — retry shortly"), and only a renewal that needs sign-in still reports the account as signed out. `car auth status` and `auth.status` report the same outage instead of the 401 they were renewing. Parslee inference rejected for the same reason now fails as a transient error instead of the original 401, so `car do` no longer calls it a sign-in failure; a 403 (signed in, no access) keeps its access-denied answer. Automatic renewal inside the 30-second retry interval after the token service rejected the refresh token now reports that sign-in is needed, rather than a temporary outage.

- Security: tokio updated from 1.53.1 to 1.53.3 for RUSTSEC-2026-0386 (`AsyncFd::new` and related safe constructors accepted any raw file descriptor, which could lead to a use-after-free in tokio's I/O driver when a descriptor was closed and reused while still registered). CAR's own code never constructs an `AsyncFd`, so the exposure was through dependencies only.

- A certificate-verified Lattice connection with a colleague's CAR now replaces an older unverified one (a LAN knock or an invite code) with the same CAR, instead of being refused because a connection already exists. Once it is active, each CAR ends the unverified connection on its own side. An offer a CAR refuses without asking its owner is announced as a `lattice.offer_refused` event, so the person waiting for it sees what happened.

- Coder: a short `silence_window_secs` in `coder.toml` could mark a session Stalled while the verifier ran a busy check that printed nothing, because the verifier measured that check against a fixed 15-minute window instead of the session's own. The verifier now uses the session's configured window (a window of 0, which disables the watchdog, keeps the 15-minute default). `car code-task --silence-window-secs` is honoured the same way.

- Independent verification now stops when the session's time limit passes. Checking a built agent counts against the time limit of the build attempt it checks (10 minutes by default; a repair after a failed check starts a new attempt), and an ordinary coder session with `max_session_wall_secs` (or `car code-task --max-session-wall-secs`) has its cap applied to verification too. Before, a verifier or auditor model call that never returned kept running until the silence window (900 seconds by default) ended the session. At the limit, the in-flight model call is dropped, a running check is killed (a file copy already preparing a check's tree finishes in the background), and the session ends `budget_exhausted` with a `budget_exhausted` event, so the build card shows a build that ran out of time. Its workspace is kept. Verification that finishes before the limit is unchanged.

- `verify-release.sh` on a nightly now ends with a pass or fail line for each of five areas (Mac, Linux, Windows, pip, npm) and names every catch-up file it cannot find, including the catch-up markers, the Linux arm64 files, the Linux `.node` and the Linux and Windows wheels. It no longer passes while `car-release status` shows a lane pending, because both read what a lane contributes from one place. When a catch-up file is missing, the hint points at re-running the failed catch-up jobs rather than at a macOS backfill. `--scope catch-up` runs just those five areas.

- A model id written without a tag, such as `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` (how a declarative agent pin of `model: claude-haiku-4-5, provider: anthropic` is addressed), now names the catalog row tagged `:latest`. Such a pin used to find no row: generation refused it as model not found, a saved agent's run treated the model as unavailable (it stopped, or Parslee stood in), and the reasoning allowance fell back to the plain 2048-token answer, leaving no room for a saved medium or high reasoning effort on a legacy Claude model. It now runs on that row with its saved reasoning, exactly as the tagged id does. An exact id still wins where both exist, a tagged id is never replaced, and an id no row has is still refused (car#2751).

- Qwen3.8-27B now decodes about 35% faster on Apple Silicon (16 → 21.5 tok/s on an M5 Pro) through speculative decoding with its own MTP drafter. A `managed_vllm_mlx` catalog source can name a drafter as `draft_hf_repo`; CAR downloads it into the model's directory (253 MB for Qwen3.8-27B) and starts vllm-mlx with it attached. Retiring the model frees the drafter too. Rows without a drafter serialize exactly as before.
- Runtime compatibility: CAR now requires vllm-mlx 0.6.0 or newer and upgrades an older managed install the next time it needs the runtime. Versions before 0.6.0 load only Gemma 4 drafters. In the managed venv the upgrade changes only vllm-mlx and llguidance; mflux, ltx and mlx-vlm keep their versions.
- A generation that uses its whole `max_tokens` budget now reports `stop_reason: "length"` (so `was_truncated()` is true) even when the server says `"stop"`. vllm-mlx does this with a speculative drafter: it returns 2002 tokens on a 2000-token budget and calls the response finished. A caller's stop sequence and any other provider reason are left alone.

- Qwen3.8 and other `vllm-mlx` models whose prompt opens a `<think>` block now answer instead of returning their unfinished thinking. The first request gets half of `max_tokens`, or the caller's `budget_tokens` when it fits. If the model is still thinking when that runs out, CAR closes the thought in Qwen's documented words and asks for the answer with the remaining tokens, through `/v1/completions` over the same prompt the server rendered. Before this, a response cut off mid-thought came back as raw chain-of-thought presented as the answer, because vllm-mlx's non-streaming reasoning parser doesn't account for a `<think>` opened by the prompt. vllm-mlx's own `thinking_token_budget` can't be used instead, because it isn't applied while the MTP drafter is attached. A response that finishes within its budget is returned unchanged, with no second request.
- Tool calls in the XML form Qwen3.5 and later emit (`<tool_call><function=…><parameter=…>`) are now parsed, typed from the tool's JSON schema. Before, only Qwen3's JSON form was recognized. The thinking continuation above relies on this for answers that end in a tool call.
- OpenAI-compatible responses that carry `reasoning_content` (vLLM, vllm-mlx, DeepSeek) now report it as the result's thinking, as OpenRouter's `reasoning` already was.
- Chat templates that write values through `| tojson` (every Qwen3.5+ template does this for tool definitions) now render. They render as Python's `json.dumps` would, which is how the model saw them in training.

- `GenerateParams.thinking` now reaches `vllm-mlx` models. `Off` and `On` are sent as `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`, and `Auto` leaves the model template's default. Before, vllm-mlx always rendered with thinking on. A caller asking for `Off` got thinking anyway, and the automatic "retry without thinking" after an empty, length-stopped answer repeated the same request. On Qwen3.8, a short question answered with thinking off takes 5 tokens where it took 54. Hosted providers are never sent the field.

- When a `vllm-mlx/*` model needs the vllm-mlx runtime and `uv` is not installed, the error no longer suggests `pip install vllm-mlx`, which often puts the runtime somewhere CAR does not look. It now says to install uv and run `uv tool install vllm-mlx`, or to set `CAR_VLLM_MLX_BIN` to the path of a vllm-mlx binary. When the installed runtime is older than CAR needs, the error names where it is and how to upgrade it: `uv tool install --upgrade vllm-mlx` for one uv installed (its tool environment holds uv's `uv-receipt.toml`), the `uv pip install` command for CAR's own runtime, and otherwise the tool that installed it (uv will not replace a program it did not install), or `CAR_VLLM_MLX_BIN`. The never-download refusal for an old runtime gives the same upgrade advice.
- CAR now also finds a vllm-mlx that `uv tool install` put in the directories named by `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR`, `UV_TOOL_DIR`, `XDG_BIN_HOME` or `XDG_DATA_HOME`, when they are absolute paths set in CAR's own environment.

- Local vllm-mlx models: while a supervised vllm-mlx server loads, CAR no longer sends `GET /health` to its port until the server's own process group is listening there (macOS and Linux). The port is free for the whole model load, so another program could take it; CAR used to poll that program every half second, and a 2xx from it counted as the model being ready. Now the program sees no requests while CAR can see it holds the port, and the load fails with the server's exit instead of reporting a stranger as ready. Two gaps remain: the ownership check and the probe are separate steps, so a program that takes the port between them can still receive one probe; and when the system returns no listener information for the server's process group, CAR probes the port as before.

- On Linux, stopping a walled agent now stops everything it started. Each walled agent is started by a small helper process of CAR's own binary (`car-agent-init` in `ps`, the pid `car ls` shows), which stays outside the agent's wall and keeps every process the agent starts in its own tree, including one that detaches with `setsid` after its parent exits. Stop, remove, a stop that outlasts its grace period, the agent's own process exiting, and the daemon exiting or being killed each end that whole tree; before, such a detached process kept running. The agent's exit status is reported as before, a missing command is still an immediate start error, and the daemon still reaps only its own children, so no other process it runs loses its exit status. A walled agent still running when a new daemon starts is now stopped and started again instead of being taken back under supervision. Programs that embed CAR (the Node and Python packages) cannot provide the helper, so they refuse to start walled agents with a reason; run those agents under `car-server`. The Mac and CAR's own assistant are unchanged.
- The container image now runs `tini` as PID 1 (`ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--", "car-server"]`), so a process handed to PID 1 is reaped instead of lingering. A `command:` in `compose.yaml` still replaces only `car-server`'s arguments.

- `web_search` (Parslee Core's assistant tool): a result link inside any element marked hidden (`hidden`, `aria-hidden="true"`, or an inline style that hides it) is no longer reported, not only one inside a `.result` block or a result's title or snippet. A hidden formatting element that a browser opens again hides what follows up to the next end tag of its name in its scope (an end tag inside a table cell opened after it does not end it), and a page whose `html` or `body` is marked hidden reports no results. A result page whose result links are all hidden is reported as a failed read, not as a search that found nothing. A result, an instant-answer topic or an abstract source whose address is not an `http` or `https` URL (`javascript:`, `data:`, `mailto:`, a relative path) is no longer reported; such a result link still ends the result before it.
- The daemon's web search (`car_inference::search`): DuckDuckGo results skip a result block, link or snippet that is hidden (or sits inside a hidden element or a `template`) and leave hidden text out of titles and snippets, using the same reader of hiding markup as Parslee Core, now `car_inference::web_markup`. A DuckDuckGo page whose result links are all hidden is a parse error rather than an empty result. DuckDuckGo, Tavily and Parslee results whose url is not an `http` or `https` url are dropped.

- Several web searches in a row now return results instead of only the first one. Parslee Core's `web_search` and the keyless `search` capability ask DuckDuckGo's result page with a form POST, as its own search form does, rather than a GET it starts refusing after a search or two. Requests to DuckDuckGo are spaced at least 2.5 s apart across the process, each search has a 60 s budget for its waits and requests, and after DuckDuckGo throttles a request (a 202, 403 or 429 from any of its endpoints, or its challenge page in answer to a direct request) CAR leaves it alone for 60 s instead of extending the throttle. On macOS, when CAR's browser is already running, `web_search` first reads the result page in a separate background tab of it; the tab leaves the agent's page and the drawer's tabs as they were and refuses every request the page makes to another site. A search never starts the browser or opens a window. When DuckDuckGo refuses that browser (it serves a headless browser its challenge page) or the tab cannot read the page, the search asks DuckDuckGo directly, says so, and skips that browser for 30 minutes. DuckDuckGo's own ad links are no longer returned as results, and the keyless `search` capability now reports a throttled search as an error rather than as no results.

- Security: rustls-webpki updated to 0.103.16, and webpki-roots and webpki-root-certs to 1.0.10, for RUSTSEC-2026-0382 (certificate verification could accept distrusted intermediates) and RUSTSEC-2026-0381/0383 (the bundled Mozilla root set still carried `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, so TLS connections could trust paths through distrusted emSign intermediates whose private keys are public).

- Windows CI no longer runs the coder tests that drive a builder child, which CarCoder refuses to start where it cannot confine writes; a Windows test now asserts that refusal instead.

- Windows CI is green again: a test helper that a Windows test uses is no longer compiled only on Unix, a test kept its temporary directory alive only on Unix, and `apps/host-windows/Cargo.lock` gained the TLS packages the workspace now pins.
- Windows: a spend-ledger append that failed part-way is now cut back as intended. The cut ran through the append handle, which on Windows has no write-data access, so it was refused and the torn line stayed: the next read of that agent's ledger failed, and a failed directory sync on a new ledger kept and charged the rows it should have dropped.
- Windows: when a declarative agent stops unfinished, a file it saved under two letter cases (`Transfers.csv`, `transfers.csv`) is named once, as on a Mac. File identity was read only on Unix, so NTFS's case-insensitive names counted as two files.
- Windows security hardening: `memory.persist` and `memory.load` now refuse a hard link to one of the daemon's own memory snapshots, as they already did on macOS and Linux. The check compared files by identity only on Unix, so on Windows a hard link under an export name was judged by that name alone and let through.

- Windows CI: the relay wire golden vectors check out with LF line endings, the Lattice end-to-end fixture starts its agent through an absolute `cmd.exe`, and the context-resolution test uses a path that is absolute on Windows. The public doc-link check accepts a 401/403 from the ChatGPT backend endpoint the docs name as the Codex credential's only destination.
- Windows: when a scheduled agent run has to start the daemon itself, the daemon inherits PATH as it is. It used to split PATH on `:` to put the macOS tool folders in front, which broke every `C:\...` entry.

- Release: stable promotion now opens the `microsoft/winget-pkgs` pull request for `Parslee.Car` itself (komac, using the `WINGET_PKGS_PAT` secret). It skips with a warning while the secret is unset and skips a version winget already has or has a pull request for.

- `wire-schema.json` (served by `server.schema` and published at car.parslee.ai/wire-schema.json) now describes JSON-RPC **params** as well as results (car-releases#98). Each `rpc.<method>.params` schema is generated from the Rust type the handler deserializes, and `coverage.rpc_params` names every dispatch method once: covered (91 methods, including `server.handshake`, every `host.*` approval method, `session.init`, `runs.start`, the `multiplayer.*` methods other than `submit_stage`, and the `mail.*` methods that take params), `not_read` (99 methods whose dispatch arm passes the handler no params, such as `host.subscribe` and `mail.accounts`), `typed_without_schema` (18 methods parsed into a type that does not derive a schema yet), or `unresolved` (the remainder, read field by field or through a path the generator does not follow). Params schemas follow serde's input rules, so optional and defaulted fields are not `required` and an object is closed only where the type uses `deny_unknown_fields`. The approval channel is covered end to end: `rpc.host.subscribe.result`, `notification.host.event.params`, and `type.host_approval_request` for the `approval.requested` and `approval.resolved` payloads. All six `mail.*` results are covered. `coverage.complete` remains `false`, because most params and results are still uncovered and server-to-client notifications other than `host.event` are not inventoried yet. Seven handlers that fall back to defaults on unparseable params (`mail.inbox`, `mail.mailboxes`, `meeting.list`, `registry.list`, `registry.reap`, `events.truncate`, `models.search`) are named in the schema's `limitations`, since for them the schema is stricter than the daemon. No method or protocol version changed. Fields that handlers used to read beside their parse are now part of the parsed params, so a mistyped one is refused instead of silently defaulted: `remote` on `multiplayer.*` (a non-string used to mean `origin`), `push` on `multiplayer.merge_check` (a non-boolean used to mean `false`), and `session_id` on `policy.register` (a non-string used to register the policy globally). `multiplayer.get`, `multiplayer.abandon` and `multiplayer.merge_check` report a missing `item` as an `invalid params` error.

- Workers, part two (`docs/proposals/orchestrator-workers.md`): workers are bounded, stoppable and visible only to their owner. Everything a worker writes lands under `<CAR_HOME>/workers/<handle>/` (logs, session journals, pid record, key-read and refusal rows, end reason), and on Linux its wall is its own `home/`. Stopping, removing or a for-good end of an orchestrator stops every worker it started within the stop grace period (the orphan rule); a worker's `time_limit_secs` is now enforced; each worker records how it ended. An orchestrator may `agents.start`, `stop`, `restart`, `wait` and `remove` its own workers (`agents.remove` takes `stop?: bool` and moves from the host role to the agent-or-host role), and any other worker handle is refused with `-32003 not_your_worker`. `agents.list`, `agents.health` and `agents.peers` show a worker only to the host and its own orchestrator. Removing a worker deletes everything that could start or resume it and keeps its records marked removed. Workers still start nowhere until the fence verdict is wired in.

- Workers, part one (`docs/proposals/orchestrator-workers.md`): an orchestrator's manifest can declare the worker bundles it may start (`[[workers]]`, `[workers.limits]`), a worker bundle (`[agent] role = "worker"`, `[worker] models`, `[report] counters`, `bundle_format_version = 2`) installs into the bundle store, and the new `workers.start` and `workers.report` methods start a labelled worker under a CAR-minted `wk_` handle and take its structured report. Every path that would run a worker passes one admission point (daemon auth, Linux with a passing network-fence self-test, label state, the author's caps over the tree), and a worker's session may call only `session.auth`, `server.handshake` and `workers.report`, with nothing pushed to its socket but its own responses. **No worker starts yet:** until the fence self-test is wired in, `workers.start` and the install or start of an orchestrator are refused with `-32013 fence_unavailable` (or `auth_disabled` under `--no-auth`). New error codes `-32013`, `-32014`, `-32015`; JSON-RPC errors may now carry `data.reason`. Unknown keys in the new manifest sections are refused, and CAR skips an installed manifest whose worker sections break the install rules.

- An orchestrator can now hand each worker its own secret values when it starts it: `workers.start { ..., values: { SOURCE_PASSWORD: "…" } }`, for example a short-lived token scoped to one tenant. Each name must be one the worker bundle declares in `secrets`. The worker reads the value in its environment under that name and through `secret.get` from its own session (now on the worker list, for declared names only), and it takes precedence over the CAR store for that worker alone; installed agents still read the one CAR-wide value per name. Each value must be at least 8 bytes. The values are kept owner-only in `workers/<handle>/values/`, a folder of their own that backups leave out, so the worker gets the same ones after a crash restart, `agents.restart`, a daemon restart or a boot resume, and they are deleted when the worker is removed or its start is refused. A worker whose handed value has gone missing is refused rather than started on the CAR store's value. A name the bundle does not declare is refused with `undeclared_value`; a name CAR controls, or a value equal to the daemon, host or a supervised agent's token, with `reserved_value` (the attempt is recorded without the value). No reply, error, event, record, export or daemon log line carries a value, and a value a worker prints is masked in its logs once its process ends. An orchestrator can tell a CAR takes `values` from the new optional handshake capability `workers.start-values.v1`.

- Workers, part three (`docs/proposals/orchestrator-workers.md`). **Workers start on Linux, without a network fence.** Where the file wall applies (Landlock) and the daemon is each worker's per-agent init, `workers.start` now starts workers; macOS, Windows and Linux hosts without the file wall still refuse with `fence_unavailable`. There is no network fence yet, so such a worker can reach any host, and every surface says so: worker rows in `agents.list` and `car ls --json` carry `network_fence_warning` ("Network fence: not built yet. This worker can reach any host."), shown in red by `car ls` and the dashboard, and by `car doctor` for workers running now; the `workers.start` reply carries it, and every start of a worker, restarts and boot resumes included, is a `worker_started` event in its orchestrator's and the host's event log (`events.query`) and a line in the worker's start records; a new session is given the newest 256 starts per worker and a `worker_starts_omitted` event counting the rest, and a start whose record cannot be written is logged and still delivered, with `record_error`. Workers may now call `infer`, `infer_stream` and `infer.cancel`: only listed request fields (`-32003 model_field_not_allowed` otherwise), pinned to the bundle's `[worker] models`, with a per-label value first in every cached prompt position, checked on the request bytes before each call is sent, so provider prompt caches never cross labels (any JSON schema shape is accepted), and usage reported without a cache split. The new `workers.spend` reports each label's and each worker's model spend per calendar day in the server's time zone, streamed calls included, every call that reached a model counted however it ends (cancelled, failed, timed out or cut off too) and a call refused before reaching one counted not at all, on the day it was sent, and local models at $0; the totals survive restarts and are not yet enforced as caps. At boot a worker comes back only beside its orchestrator (#3349), and a caller's refusal record caps the id it tried at 128 characters (#3350).

- **Remote access for outside orchestrators: the public door and outside credentials.** An agent installed from a bundle with `[transport] kind = "outside"` is an outside agent: CAR runs no process for it, and it reaches CAR only through an owner-issued credential. The host issues one with `credentials.issue` (`kind: "orchestrator"`, bound only to an outside agent; reserved ids and agents CAR runs are refused) and manages them with `credentials.list`, `credentials.revoke` (idempotent, never re-enabled) and `credentials.refusals`; refusals use the new code `-32017`. The token (`car_oc_` + 43 base64url) is shown once, and only its SHA-256 is stored, in an owner-only file under `<CAR_HOME>/credentials/`. A remove and reinstall of the agent ends credentials issued before it, and an expiring credential's open sockets close at `expires_at`. `car-server --public-bind <addr:port>` (`CAR_PUBLIC_BIND`) opens the door, behind a TLS terminator, and never under `--no-auth` or without a host token: it serves only `GET /v1/ws` (Bearer outside credential, checked before the upgrade; `400` for a `/v1/ws` request without `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, JSON `401` bodies, `429` past 16 connections per credential, `503` past 256 connections not yet upgraded, 1 MiB frames) and `GET /healthz`. A door session is pre-bound, starts with `server.handshake`, refuses `session.auth`, and may call only `server.handshake`, `server.schema`, `workers.start`, `agents.list`, `agents.health`, `agents.stop`, `agents.wait` and `agents.remove` (its own workers) on every platform; close codes `4001` revoked, `4002` expired, `4004` shutting down (`4003` reserved). `session.auth` on the private port refuses any `car_oc_` token. Unset, nothing changes.

- **Workers: one `agents.wait` says how a worker ended, and daemon restarts bring the right workers back.** `agents.wait` takes the new target `"ended"` (stopped or errored), and a worker's reply now carries `end_reason`, CAR's own `end_message` (for example "stopped: kept crashing"), `last_error` (`{ kind: "exit" | "signal" | "timed_out" | "kept_crashing" | "spawn_failed" | "environment_failed", exit_code?, signal? }`) and its last structured `report`, so an orchestrator needs no log read; none of these is text the worker wrote. End states are sticky until the worker next starts, so a wait started after the end still gets it. A worker that keeps crashing is restarted with growing gaps up to its bundle's `max_restarts`, then ends `kept_crashing` with the last crash's code or signal. At a daemon's boot, a worker that was running is started again, through the admission point and under the same handle, name, labels and history, after a clean shutdown, when its process outlived the daemon (it is killed first), or when the host-instance key changed (Linux boot id plus the start time of PID 1; macOS `kern.boottime`; Windows `BootId`), meaning it died with its host or container. A walled worker's init now records why it ended the worker (`workers/<handle>/init-outcome`): one that died because CAR's daemon exited or crashed is started again, on the same host too, and one that ended on its own while its exit could not be recorded ends `interrupted_by_restart`, with the exit its init saw, and is not started again. Every way a worker ends for good records an end reason, including the new `restart_refused` (a crash restart or a boot start the admission point refused; its `last_error` is `null`, since the crash before it is not the cause) and `environment_failed` (its wall could not be applied, or a declared key could not be handed over). A worker waiting out a crash restart's backoff when the daemon dies is started again at the next boot, and a worker stopped on purpose stays stopped even if the daemon died, or shut down cleanly, during its stop grace. A worker with nothing on record at boot ends `interrupted_by_restart` instead of staying stopped with no end, and an end that cannot be written to disk is still returned by `agents.wait`, with `end_record_error`. The workers of an outside orchestrator now come back too. The time limit keeps its first deadline across crash restarts and daemon restarts. `ManagedAgent` rows gain `last_error`, in process and in every `agents.*` reply that returns an agent row.

- The CAR plugin for Claude Code now routes Claude Code's own worktrees (subagents with worktree isolation, `EnterWorktree`, `claude --worktree`) through the worktree pool: new `WorktreeCreate`, `WorktreeRemove` and `SubagentStop` hooks run the new `car worktree hook`. In a repo that commits `.car/worktree-pool.toml` with `enabled = true`, creation leases a warm slot held by the Claude Code process, removal gives it back (refused while it holds work), and a finished subagent's clean slot is released. A full or broken pool fails creation rather than making a worktree outside the pool. In every other repo the hook makes the same worktree Claude Code makes with no hook (`.claude/worktrees/<name>` in the main checkout, even from a linked worktree, on `worktree-<name>` from the default branch, `.worktreeinclude` files copied, a symlinked `.claude` path refused), removes it with its branch, and removes a subagent's worktree that holds nothing. A new `car-worktree` skill, shared by the Claude Code and Codex plugins, tells agents to use `car worktree acquire` instead of `git worktree add`. The hooks run a POSIX `sh` script that hands them to `car worktree hook`; with no `car`, or one too old to have it, the script makes, removes and cleans up the same worktrees Claude Code makes with no hook (without pooling), so updating the plugin before CAR never breaks worktree creation.

- New `car worktree` command group: agents on one machine lease a warm git worktree from a small per-repo pool (`<parent>/<repo>-pool/slot-N`) instead of each creating a cold one with `git worktree add`. `acquire <branch>` prints the slot path, `release` gives it back (refused while it holds unsaved work; build output is kept for the next agent), `status` shows the holders, `reclaim` frees slots whose holder process is gone, and `clean` finds stale ad-hoc worktrees and, with `--apply`, archives each one (a tag plus patches and tarballs) before removing it. A full pool exits 3 rather than creating another worktree. The pool is off until a repo commits `.car/worktree-pool.toml` with `enabled = true` (`car init` now writes a commented `.car/worktree-pool.toml.example`); the pool size stays per machine in `git config wtpool.size`. Leases and the pool lock are compatible on disk with the `wt-pool.sh` script this replaces, and nothing needs Python or the daemon. Pooling is not yet supported on Windows, where the commands refuse.

- Office file editing reads and writes archives with `zip` 9.0.3. Every earlier `zip` release was yanked upstream after a round of fixes for malformed archives (over-long reads and arithmetic overflows), which also turned CI's supply-chain check red for every pull request.

## [v0.58.0] — 2026-10-15

### Changes

- Build an Agent: a build whose agent passed its own test scenarios no longer fails at the independent check that follows. That check handed the agent's scenario placeholder, `(in-daemon scenario evaluation)`, to a shell, which failed with "command not found" every time, so every agent build ended with "verification made no progress". The independent check now re-runs the delivered `agent.json` scenarios inside the daemon, the same way the build ran them, and passes or fails on their real result. The placeholder is never run as a shell command. If inference fails during that re-run, the session ends as an infrastructure failure instead of blaming the agent.

- Build an Agent: an agent that works in a folder now passes the independent check after its build. The check re-runs the agent's test scenarios in fresh copies of its working folder, as the build does, instead of in the build's project folder, which holds only `agent.json`, so an agent that reads files from its folder no longer fails there. If a copy of the folder cannot be made, the check ends as an infrastructure failure instead of grading the agent as failed, and making the copies counts against the check's time limit.

- Node and Python agent loops: a caller-owned runtime that was closed and reused, or that reconnected after a daemon restart, now registers its tools and policies again on the new daemon session, and a serving chat agent (`serveChat` / `serve_chat`, `--serve`) does the same before each chat turn instead of failing every turn after a daemon restart. The loops remembered registrations per runtime object, so the second run on a blank session failed with the tool not registered and ran without its declared policies. New `CarRuntime.connectionEpoch()` (Node) / `connection_epoch()` (Python) reports which daemon session calls land on; the loops key their once-per-session registration on it.

- **Android: approving or denying a chat approval now reaches the waiting
  turn.** The Android host sent `agents.chat.approve` as `{id, resolution}`,
  which the daemon rejects for want of `session_id` and `approval_id`, so every
  answer failed and the turn waited out its timeout. Android now answers a chat
  approval with `session_id`, `approval_id` and `decision`, and any other
  approval through `host.resolve_approval`, as CarHost does. The approval list
  is rebuilt from the `host.subscribe` snapshot on every connect, so an
  approval resolved while the phone was offline drops and one requested
  meanwhile appears, while a request that raced the snapshot is kept. An
  answer given offline keeps its card pending until it is delivered and lands;
  it is resent after a dropped connection, but not after the daemon refused
  it, and an approval resolved elsewhere settles it. A timeout on a live
  connection shows the error and keeps the card, so tapping again resends. A
  refused answer, a chat reply without `resolved: true`, or a ledger row
  already resolved another way shows the approval error instead of reporting
  success, including from a notification action. `approval.resolved` closes
  the card and withdraws its notification, a chat `approval_resolved` frame or
  a resolved row in the snapshot settles the inline card, and only
  `approval.requested` opens a card.

- Parslee Core is now told the local date, time and time zone on every turn, so requests that say "today", "tomorrow" or "this week" (in chat, `car do` and the MCP assistant) use the real date instead of a guessed one.
- Multi-turn assistant runs on Anthropic models read their conversation history from the prompt cache again when the turn carries a task list or remembered facts; the cache breakpoint no longer lands on the per-turn state text that the next request does not re-send.

- Built-in assistant: after a restart in the middle of a turn, resume now finds the durable action record the turn wrote. Before, it looked the record up under the provider's tool-call id while the turn had recorded it under its own `turn_<n>_call_<k>` id, so every interrupted call was closed as "interrupted before approval; not replayed". A call that was already dispatched is now reported as indeterminate and not replayed, so the model is no longer told an action that may have run never ran. A call approved before the restart is now replayed once, after the usual re-checks. Two host-visible ids change as a result: a `delegate` child's calls are recorded under `<parent call id>/<child call id>`, so the `action_id` on its `approval_pending` frames (a digest of that id) differs from before; and receipts replayed from earlier turns of a thread now number turns with the same compaction-aware count as live `tool_call`/`tool_result` ids, so the two agree.

- On macOS and Linux, approved local assistant shell commands now run inside CAR's OS secret sandbox, which denies reads of the daemon `auth-token` and `host-token` files after path resolution and refuses a protected inode with a pre-existing hard-link alias. Encoders, split reads, globs, symlinks, `/dev/fd`, and subshells can no longer return token-derived bytes; exact-value output redaction remains as a second layer. Windows keeps its existing approval and redaction behavior while its OS read-denial boundary is tracked in car-96vm.

- `browser_await_signin` no longer reports `signed_in: true` for a sign-in nobody completed. A call like `{url: "https://github.com/login", success_url_contains: "github.com"}` ended on its first check with the login form still up, and so did a call without `success_url_contains` that started on a page whose URL has no login marker. A start page that already passes the success test is now refused with an error that says why. `success_url_contains` is matched against the URL without its query string. The wait also reads the browser's live URL, so a sign-in completed by a form POST or an identity-provider redirect is detected; it used to read a cache those never update. `browse_wait` with `url_changed` reads the live URL for the same reason.

- `car bench` decode-speed calibration now measures a generation only after an earlier one has succeeded. When just one of the two calibration generations succeeds, the run keeps the base time limits instead of scaling them from the timing of the generation that loaded the model.

- `car-bench-run` could-not-run records now scrub their saved reason with the same redactor `car feedback` uses, then mask any user directory left mid-word, so every user directory is masked: several paths joined in one word (`/Users/a/models:/Users/b/models`, a `PATH`), Windows profiles (`C:\Users\<name>`, the `USERPROFILE` directory, `/mnt/c/Users/<name>` under WSL), other volumes' `Users` folders, and profile names with a space. Previously the second username and path stayed visible in a result meant for sharing, and a `HOME` that prefixed another user's directory (`/Users/al` vs `/Users/alice`) left part of that name behind. The reason also takes the shared token scrub, so a 40+ character high-entropy run such as a full commit SHA or digest now reads `[REDACTED]`.
- The shared redactor (`car feedback` bundles and the `car coder-ab` ledger) now masks a home path after `;` or `|` and in a `file:///Users/<name>` URL, and no longer reads the `s:` of `models:/Users/<name>` as a Windows drive, which had dropped the separator from a joined path list and could hide a real `C:\Users\<name>` path that followed.

- `car code` and `car board` no longer lose text you wrote when a send fails. A refused conversation message goes back into the composer (several refusals in the order you sent them, ahead of anything typed since), its "you:" line is removed so it does not read as sent, and Enter retries it; if the composer is closed it is held until you reopen it, and switching, closing, or quitting warns first. Messages queued before a conversation failed to open come back the same way, or are listed in the exit summary when the daemon does not support conversations. An answer to a coder question that never reached the daemon is kept and the question stays answerable. When the daemon connection drops (including while you are on another screen, for answers, guidance and revisions), a refusal arrives for a conversation you have left, or an answer's question has closed, the text is printed in the exit summary marked "may not have been sent". A refused or unhonored contract revision is kept for retry: `e` in the board and `c` at the `car code` approval menu reopen it filled in, and a failed revision there returns to the menu instead of ending the review.

- Model-reachable HTTP reads beyond `http_request` stop at a byte cap instead of downloading the whole body first, so a server sending a huge or endless body costs at most the cap rather than holding the read open until the timeout (or, for remote MCP connectors, which have no timeout, forever). Parslee Core's `web_search` reads the result page up to 256 KB and the instant-answer JSON up to 1 MiB; a longer answer is reported as a failed search. The daemon's `web_fetch` reads up to 8 MiB and a longer page's `text` ends in `…[truncated]…`; the keyless DuckDuckGo `search` fallback reads its result page up to 8 MiB. A remote MCP connector reply longer than 8 MiB is an error naming the cap. Bodies are still decoded by their `Content-Type` charset.

- CAR release binaries can now carry a `YYYYMMDD-sha7` build ID in `--version` output, and the daemon records it in `version.json`.

- `runs.cancel`: when the audit-journal append fails after a cancellation has already made the run terminal in the run store, the exact retry now finishes whichever journal rows are missing (the terminal row, the `run_cancellation_result` receipt, or both), each exactly once, before answering. Before, it returned the receipt from the run store while the journal never got it. This covers host cancellation of an orphaned run and confirmed owner cancellation, including a retry from another connection after the owner disconnected and a same-key request that was waiting while the first one failed. The owner's retry also releases the run's journal binding. If the daemon restarts first, startup reconciliation restores the receipt from the durable terminal.

- `car claude` no longer adds a second `car-collaboration` server beside the plugin's (which still refused, so the model saw two near-identical tool sets). It writes the session's identity to an owner-only file and gives `claude` only that path in `CAR_COLLABORATION_CREDENTIALS`, which `car-mcp --collaboration` reads when no `CAR_AGENT_ID` is set. Its cleanup of a killed launcher's leftover agent now works on Windows too (`OpenProcess` liveness, shared with `car doctor`).

- New `car claude`: starts Claude Code as a CAR-supervised collaboration session, so the plugin's `car-collaboration` tools (`collaboration_status`, `peer_*`, `lattice_*`) work instead of reporting "launch this coding session through CAR supervision". It binds the work context `car auth resolve` names for the directory (no org argument), enrolls a per-session agent whose token is scoped to the collaboration methods, passes the identity only to a session-only MCP server rather than to `claude`'s environment, and removes the agent when `claude` exits. Arguments after `--` go to `claude`.

- Ctrl-C (or SIGTERM) at a waiting `car do` approval prompt, or at the conversational `car do` `›` prompt, now ends the run at once with the "interrupted" line and exit code 130 (143 for SIGTERM) instead of waiting for Enter; the pending call is not approved.
- `car agent new`'s "Build this agent?" and "Add it to your agents?" prompts now cancel the build session on Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP, including when the answer comes from piped stdin, instead of ignoring Ctrl-C or leaving the session open. `car code`'s approval prompts and contract menu also turn SIGTERM and SIGHUP into a cancel, so the terminal is no longer left in raw mode. On a terminal, Escape and Ctrl-D at the car agent new prompts cancel too, and the prompt closes with a pointer to `car board` if another client changes the task.
- `car code` and `car agent new` exit 130 when Ctrl-C, or Escape or Ctrl-D at a terminal, interrupts one of their prompts, 143 for SIGTERM and 129 for SIGHUP, after cancelling the session. They used to exit 0, which reads as finished work; the codes match `car do`. Answering no still exits 0.

- Every on-device last resort — `car do`, the daemon's chat and `infer` paths, and streaming inference — now falls back only to a model installed through CAR: its files in CAR's models directory (from `car models install`/`pull`, CarHost's Models setup, or placed there by hand) or a CAR install receipt. OS-provided models such as Apple's foundation model still qualify. A complete snapshot that only sits in the shared Hugging Face cache is no longer used; when a chain then runs out, the error names `car models adopt <id>` for each such model. Among eligible models the fallback is the most capable one that fits in free memory (tool-capable first, then the largest) rather than the smallest. `car do`'s startup choice of a substitute for a model that cannot call tools follows the same rule (car#1439).
- A `car.do/1` run answered by a model other than the one it named now reports `status: "success_substituted"` instead of `"success"` (still an answer, still exit 0), with top-level `substituted_from` and `substitution_reason`. The reason is `credential_rejected`, `credential_absent`, `rate_limited`, `quota_exhausted`, `timed_out` or `failed` for a request-time fallback, or `not_tool_capable` / `unavailable` for `car do`'s startup substitution. The same two fields ride on each substituted `models_served` entry and on `model_served` events: the `car do --json` stream, the host `agents.chat.event` stream, and `coder.discuss` events. CarHost's answer caption and the coder conversation now name the model a fallback replaced. `--strict-model` still disables substitution entirely (car#1439).
- Streaming reports an on-device last-resort substitution too. When a model installed through CAR answers a remote-only streaming request in place of the routed model, the `infer_stream` final result and the voice fast track's `voice.turn.fast_done` frame (daemon and the UniFFI host) carry `local_last_resort: true`, `substituted_from` and `substitution_reason`, the same fields the non-streaming surfaces use. Internally the stream leads with a new `StreamEvent::Substituted` (car#1439).

- `car do`: a one-shot run that tried an action and never got it done now ends as not done and exits 1, instead of exiting 0 because the model's final answer explained what happened. That covers an action declined at the approval prompt or by a saved "don't allow", one that could not be approved because nobody could be asked (piped input, a script, CI, a timed-out request), and one that could not run. The answer still prints, followed by a plain line saying the request did not finish. `--json` reports `status: "error"` with `error` / `failure.cause` of `ApprovalDenied` / `approval_denied`, `NeededApproval` / `needed_approval`, or `ActionFailed` / `action_failed`. A refusal is cleared only by a later successful call of the same tool with the same arguments, a failure by any later successful call of that tool; a command that ran and exited non-zero (a `grep` that found nothing) is a result, not a failed action. Batch exit codes now follow the turn outcome contract: `max_turns` exits 1 (was 0) and `auth_required` exits 3 (was 1). In Chat, the built-in assistant's `error` terminal now carries `state: "not_done"` and a `cause`, and such a turn ends on that frame instead of `done`. `assistant_poll` keeps reporting the handle as `ok` when such a run settles; the nested document carries the not-done status.

- `car do --resume` keeps the run's full turn count after history compaction, so turn numbers are not reused and `max_turns` still caps the whole run. A run stopped between the model's tool calls and their results now resumes with those calls answered as failed with an unknown outcome (not replayed) instead of asking the model for a new turn over unanswered calls. The guard runs on every assistant-loop entry; it is mainly reachable on `car do --resume`, since durable chat already answers these calls before its loop starts.
- Rust API: `AssistantDurability::checkpoint` (car-server-core) gained a `turns_completed: Option<u32>` parameter carrying the agent loop's turn counter. External implementors of the trait must add it; an implementation that saves no turn count can ignore it.

- `car do --serve` now refuses `--org` and `--personal` with an error instead of ignoring them. Before, `car do --serve --org <ORG>` started a personal agent with personal tools and storage; a served agent's organization comes from its registration with the daemon. Every option `--serve` refuses is now rejected before CarHost registration, so an invalid invocation leaves no registration behind.

- `scripts/car-lane.sh` now admits a release pair to a lane only when it satisfies Apple's Developer ID requirement for team `3R69WXRDNY` (an Apple-anchored chain, not the signer name `codesign` prints), so a self-made certificate that copies the expected name is refused. `install-release` and `promote` also put the previous pair back (or leave a first install empty) when a rename fails or the command is interrupted mid-swap, instead of continuing without a rollback path or leaving half a pair; exit status 5 from a failed or interrupted swap means restoring the previous pair failed and the lane needs manual repair, while a cleanly restored swap interrupted by SIGINT or SIGTERM exits 130 or 143. A `promote` rollback that cannot copy the previous pair no longer restarts the failed release and reports success.

- macOS: `car update` and `car doctor --repair` now create the `car-mcp` link beside a `car` that links into CarHost.app (for example `/usr/local/bin/car-mcp`), and replace a dangling or wrong-bundle one. Sparkle updates never re-run the package postinstall, so an install that predates `car-mcp` kept `car` working while the Claude Code / Codex CAR plugin, which runs `car-mcp`, silently had no CAR tools. `car doctor` reports the problem without `--repair`; a regular file at that path is never overwritten, and a permission error prints the exact `sudo ln -sfn` command and exits non-zero.

- CarHost's Parslee account display no longer goes back to an older state when an `auth.status` answer arrives late. An answer to a read sent before a sign-in, sign-out, account switch, org switch, or account removal that CAR has since confirmed changes nothing, and neither does an older read answering after a newer one or a read that answers while a sign-in is still finishing. A failed read now leaves the account status unknown, with Verify and sign-in still offered, instead of treating the account as signed out (Chat no longer shows the Parslee sign-in card after a failed check). A sign-in that is still finishing when another account change is confirmed now reports that it was superseded by a newer account change. Connections keeps its state when the account rejects a Verify answer as stale, and a late passive credential hint no longer overrides a confirmed sign-in. The Accounts list and the default organization ignore late answers the same way. On iPhone, a Parslee runtime found for an account that signed out while it was being looked up is no longer used, so the phone does not connect after a sign-out.

- CarHost: Approve or Deny on a chat approval from Approvals or Command Deck, and an inline chat approval in the iOS app, now show an error when the daemon reports the decision did not reach the waiting turn, instead of looking accepted. Approvals, Command Deck and `car-host approve`/`deny` also report an error when the approval was already resolved some other way (another decision won, or it expired) instead of claiming the answer was applied.

- macOS setup's "Let Parslee control your Mac" step now shows Automation as Granted once it is allowed. macOS cannot say whether an app may control System Events while System Events is not running, and it usually is not, so the row kept offering "Allow…" after the person had allowed it. CarHost now starts System Events in the background (it has no window) and reads the permission again, and re-reads it when you come back from System Settings. "Allow…" starts System Events first too, so macOS's own prompt actually appears; if System Events takes more than two seconds to start, that press shows no prompt and the next one does. The Automation row in Settings → General gets the same fix. Mail is never opened just to check its permission; while Mail is closed its permission still reads as not yet known (#2719).

- In CarHost Chat, deleting a chat whose images can't be moved to the Trash no longer removes it: its file is put back, the chat stays in the list, and an alert says so, so you can delete it again. Only if the file can't be put back does the chat go without its images, and the alert names the folder they're still in. A chat file copied into the chats folder outside CAR is loaded once every image its original still has can be copied with it; until then it stays on disk, Chat says so once, and it's tried again each time Chat opens. Images the original no longer has don't hide the copy: it's loaded without them, with a note in the chat, and Chat says so once.
- CarHost Chat forks and copies now keep the source chat's task list. An image that exists but can't be read right now (a permissions or disk error) is now named as not copied by a fork, copy or export, instead of being skipped as if it were already gone.
- In CarHost Chat, an image that loads slowly (pasted from a slow source) goes to the chat it was pasted into, even if you've switched chats since.
- A CarHost chat with no reply yet now remembers its agent by id, so when two agents share a name it picks the agent the chat was started with. When a chat's agent isn't available, or an older chat's agent name is shared by two agents, Chat no longer falls back to the default agent or keeps the previous chat's agent: no agent is picked, and the message box asks you to add one. A new chat with no agent recorded still starts with the default.
- A CarHost chat turn sent to an external CLI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) now gets the stall watchdog from the moment it's sent. Before, a CLI that died before its first output left the chat waiting forever. After a CLI turn, the next supervised turn starts a new daemon session, so it no longer picks up a thread that never saw the CLI exchange.
- In CarHost Chat, a reply that has gone silent is given up 15 minutes after CAR stops waiting for it, and its turn is stopped on the daemon; a reply that arrives within those 15 minutes still lands. The same applies to a reply CAR couldn't confirm had started. Sending a new message after a turn was given up on (stalled, or not confirmed as started) now drops that turn's event subscription. Image files left behind when Edit & Resend drops later messages are now removed the next time the Chat screen opens.

- CarHost no longer shows a change as saved when its disk write failed. A Coder task or saved-conversation link whose write fails is put back as it was, and opening it again writes it, where before the retry found the unsaved link in memory and skipped the write, so the link vanished on restart. A Coder draft that cannot be saved is now reported in the conversation. A chat rename, goal or working folder that fails to save is not kept, but the name, goal or folder you entered stays in its field with the error so you can try again without retyping. Pins, archives and pinned order are put back whole. A new chat or transcript that fails to save stays listed, is written again by the next save or reload, and the chat rail says how many chats are still unsaved. Exporting one chat as Markdown now reports a failed write. A Multiplayer stages list that fails to save is written again on the next refresh and at Quit.

- CarHost chat no longer sends a message without its image when the image cannot be saved. A failed save (Application Support unavailable, or the image file failing to write) used to send the text alone and clear the image from the composer with no message. Now nothing is sent, Chat says which image could not be saved, and the text and images stay in the composer to send again.
- CarHost chat now says when an image goes missing in the other places it used to drop one quietly. A regenerate or edit whose earlier image file is gone still sends and names that image, and a fork or duplicate names any images it could not copy, both under "Some images weren't included" rather than as a failed send. Paste, drop and the file picker name any file whose contents could not be read. Export all says how many images could not be copied beside the Markdown, and exporting one chat shows an alert when the file cannot be written.
- Exporting one CarHost chat as Markdown now copies its images into an `attachments/` folder beside the file, as Export All already did, so the exported image links resolve. Before, the links pointed at files that were never written. Images that could not be copied are counted in an alert.

- CarHost now decides whether a loaded LaunchAgent owns its daemon port from the arguments launchd actually loaded (`launchctl print`), not from the plist on disk. When `car-lane.sh` had rewritten a lane's plist for a new port but launchd was still running the old job, CarHost used to record launchd supervision of the new port and start nothing there; it now treats the new port as unowned and serves it.
- When CarHost attaches to a launchd lane it reads that lane's auth and host tokens from the lane's own `CAR_HOME` (or the default directory, for a lane that unsets it), instead of from CarHost's own home, which can belong to a different daemon.
- `car-lane.sh install-plist` now boots out an already-loaded lane before bootstrapping it again, and does every bootout before replacing the plist. Reinstalling a loaded lane used to fail at `launchctl bootstrap` and leave the new plist beside the old running job; a failed bootout now leaves the plist matching the job launchd is still running.

- CarHost Chat's Regenerate and Send again now keep the reply they replace in the saved chat until the new reply arrives, so quitting or crashing mid-reply no longer loses it.

- CarHost's **Run scenarios** on a registered agent now shows the scenario report, with Keep and Revert, instead of always failing with "CAR returned unreadable scenario results". The host read any `0` or `1` in the daemon's reply as a JSON boolean, and the first scenario is always numbered 1. The same misreading hid the agent builder's live progress line during a first attempt; it now shows.
- A multiplayer stage's saved locked contract no longer turns a `0` or `1` into `false` or `true` when CarHost writes its stage file, so confirming that contract after a restart sends the numbers the item locked.

- CarHost Chat: Send again on a reply whose outcome is unknown now decides whether the message can go out before it cancels the first attempt. When it can't (another chat is on screen, the reply is no longer the latest, or a turn is running), the first attempt is left running and listened to, the chat says why, and the reply still offers Send again. When it can, the cancel is queued on the socket and the message goes out with nothing in between, so the first attempt can no longer be cancelled with no replacement sent.

- CarHost Chat's completion receipt now lists only the checks the turn you just watched recorded. A check from an earlier turn, such as a GitHub sign-in browser proof, no longer repeats as "1 of 6 check recorded" on every later turn, including turns that called no tools. A goal turn's receipt covers every iteration of that goal run, and its desktop actions and tool rows now include the earlier iterations too, not just the last one. When a goal turn has more rows than the receipt holds, the latest ones are kept, since the final iteration is the one that met the goal. The `receipt_report` frame's `completion` field is built from the turn's own tool receipts. Each evidence string carries the turn's `call_id` and the call's redacted excerpt, bounded to 2,048 bytes overall, and a call that succeeded but reported an `error` no longer counts as a check.

- CarHost's Command Deck and Dashboard now show a Chat approval as the tool, its target and the call's parameters, instead of the raw approval JSON with the chat session id in it. Slack, iMessage and Windows tray approval summaries for a Chat approval now open with `Agent: <agent_id>` followed by the call's parameters, and never fall back to the whole approval blob with the chat session id in it (which happened when the call sent no parameters or non-object ones). iOS no longer shows `<null>` for a Chat approval with no parameters.

- CarHost Chat: drop any file anywhere on the chat screen, the message list included, and it attaches to the chat on screen. One highlight shows while you drag, and says so when a drop can't be taken. Several files can go at once, and a drop that mixes files and images keeps them all. Dropping a file on the message box attaches it; it no longer types the file's path into your message. Dragging the floating thumbnail that appears after ⌘⇧4 attaches the screenshot, the same as a saved PNG from Finder: the file is copied the moment it is dropped, so the thumbnail going away can't lose it. Refs #2447. Refs #2374.
- A dropped or pasted file shows in the message box at once, with a spinner, while it is read; Send waits for it. A file another app still has to hand over (a promised file, or several from one drag) is waited for up to 30 seconds, and if some never arrive the chat names each one. A pasted item the other app never hands over is given the same 30 seconds, then marked "It didn't arrive within 30 seconds" so Send works again, and the rest of the paste still loads. It always ends up in the chat it was dropped on, even if you switch chats first; one dropped on a new chat you leave before it is ready is dropped and said so, not moved into the next chat. Files are read in the background, one pasted file at a time, no file is read past its size limit, and one message holds at most 100 MB of attachments in all, Attach Image… included. While Send saves a message's files, that chat's message box shows "Saving files…" and waits until the message has started, so nothing typed or dropped then is lost and pressing Send again does nothing; other chats are not held. A save that hasn't finished after a minute stops holding the message box; the message stays unsent, the file shows it is still saving, and Send works again once that save has finished.
- What the agent gets for each file. Images are sent as images, as before. Text files, code, CSV, Markdown and JSON go into your message as text, up to 256 KB each; a text file saved in Windows Latin 1 (such as an Excel CSV) is read too. A larger text file is saved with the chat and referenced, and the message says it was too large to include as text. A PDF is saved with the chat like any other file: the agent is told its name, type, size and where it is saved, with a line saying "PDF text isn't extracted; open the file at its path to read it." CarHost doesn't read a PDF's text itself. Any other file, and any text file that can't be read as text, is saved with the chat and the agent is told its name, type, size and where it is saved, not its contents. Files other than images are saved up to 25 MB each, and images up to 50 MB, whether dropped or pasted as a file or as image data. A file's text can't end or fake the section it is placed in: a literal attached_file tag inside a file is escaped, and the message says so. A symlink is treated as what it points to. Folders can't be attached: use Choose Folder in the + menu to work in one. Pipes, devices and other special files are refused. A file another app hands over (a promised file, or a pasted file) must be a real file in the place it was handed over, and it is copied from the file that was checked; a link, or a file reached through a linked folder that leads elsewhere, is refused with "This app sent a link, not a file". A pasted image whose file is somewhere else is taken as image data instead.
- When something can't be attached, the chat it was dropped on says why above the message box: for example that the chat's agent can't read images, "Too large (max 25 MB)", "Not a regular file", or "Wait for this reply to finish, then attach it again". If a file can't be saved with the chat when you press Send, the message isn't sent and the file stays, marked, so you can remove it or send again. Text and other files attach for any agent that can chat; only images need an agent that reads images.
- Files saved with a chat, images included, are readable only by you (their folders 0700, the files 0600). Copies of files waiting to be sent are removed when they are sent, removed, or their window closes, and any left by a quit or crash are cleared at the next launch after a day; each build keeps its own, and nothing still in use is touched. If there's no room to receive a promised file, the chat says so instead of waiting.
- Paste: a file copied in Finder attaches with ⌘V, and a screenshot copied with ⌘⇧⌃4 still attaches as an image; both get their place in the message box the moment you paste.
- Known limit: an image dragged or pasted only as in-memory data (not as a file) is read in full before the 50 MB image limit refuses it, because macOS gives no size for such data until it is read. Nothing over the limit is kept, and a pasted image is taken as a file whenever the source offers one.

- CarHost Chat: a late approval result no longer turns an Expired card into a decision, in any chat view or the saved transcript, including a host-ledger resolution of a card the sending view has already expired.
- Daemon: an agent's `approval_resolved` for a reused approval id now closes the approval it belongs to. A decision matches the oldest answered approval with that id and a timeout the oldest unanswered one, and a late result from a replaced, cancelled or failed turn is consumed against that turn's own approvals, so an older call's result can no longer close a newer approval and leave it unanswerable. When the agent refuses a decision (`resolved: false` or an error), the daemon closes the mirrored ledger row (`timeout` or `interrupted`) instead of leaving it pending.
